# Orbex Sonar-DB Design System · full documentation

> Every page of https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/ as Markdown, in reading order (56 pages, 2026-10-29). The summary, the machine-readable files and the usage rules for agents are in https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/llms.txt. Interactive demos are left out. © 2026 988©STUDIO; code MIT, documentation CC BY 4.0.

# Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/

> The design system behind Sonar-DB, the Orbex dashboard for orders, deliveries and stock: tokens, foundations and live components.

[v1.1.6, changelog](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/changelog/)

## Orbex Sonar‑DB Design System

The design language of Sonar-DB, the Orbex dashboard where logistics teams follow orders, deliveries and stock on desktop, tablet and phone. Built on Material 3 Expressive and measured for dense figures.

*Figure: Black Lightness White*

### This release

**1.1.6**, October 29, 2026. 272 tokens, 9 foundation pages, the layout, 24 components with their sizes, variants and states, and the patterns of the overview. Restaurado estado de clic cuadrado en botones: the press shape of the approved videos (v38) is back on the two pills that had lost it. Nothing else changes; 1.1.5 and earlier are unchanged and their zips stay as they were. Every change is in the [changelog](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/changelog/).

# Changelog · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/changelog/

> Every release of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System, newest first: what was added, changed, fixed and deprecated.

## Changelog

Tokens and components are released together, so one version names the whole system. Versions follow semantic versioning; until 1.0.0, a minor release may rename or remove what an earlier alpha added, and says so here.

### Releases

    1.1.6 October 29, 2026  Restaurado estado de clic cuadrado en botones: the press shape of the approved videos (v38) is back on the two pills that had lost it. Nothing else changes; 1.1.5 and earlier are unchanged and their zips stay as they were.

#### Fixed

- Unit menu: squarer while pressed again, 10 → 6 px on the 200 ms spatial spring, as v38’s pill and the videos; open, it is a pill again. The menu opens on press, which takes `:active` away from the trigger, so `UnitMenu` marks its own press (`data-pressing`, while the pointer is down). Removed in 1.0.0-alpha.13, when the pill was redrawn to stay a pill while open.
- Calendar View button (Deliveries): squarer while pressed again, 10 → 6 px, as v38’s View pill. Its own 10 px radius (`.cal-rows .sonar-button.cal-view`, outside the components layer) outranked Button’s press shape; the pattern now states its pressed radius.

    1.1.5 October 28, 2026  Four fixes from the usage rules (the system’s grammar of nouns, verbs and surfaces), and the documentation made readable by search engines and agents. Nothing else changes on screen. 1.1.4 and earlier are unchanged; their zips stay as they were.

#### Added

- For search engines and agents (nothing visible): `robots.txt` (everything allowed), `sitemap.xml` and `llms-full.txt` (every documentation page as Markdown, in reading order), both written from the built pages (`site/build/agent-files.mjs`); a canonical link and JSON-LD on every page (`SoftwareSourceCode` for the system: version, MIT, 988©STUDIO; each page a `TechArticle` under CC BY 4.0).
- `llms.txt`: version, licence and source, links to the machine-readable files (`tokens.json`, `api.json`, `sizes.json`, `llms-full.txt`, `sitemap.xml`), and “Usage rules for agents”, the 37-line grammar for composing screens with the system (`site/src/lib/usage-rules.ts`).

#### Fixed

- Sidebar only navigates (usage rule 9). Release stock left the sidebar’s Operations group: it is now the Inventory card’s own action, a text button in the card’s header beside the unit menu (24 px tall, so the card’s content keeps its place). It still acts at once, the toast still says “Stock released” with Undo, and the button rests until Undo. An app provides the action through `ReleaseStock` (`InventoryCard.tsx`); a card drawn without it has no button. Search still offers Release stock.
- One name per object: “notifications” now names only the operational alerts (the Notifications card). The bell’s panel, the product’s own news, is “What’s new” (was System notifications), and so is its button in the phone’s bottom app bar (was Alerts) and its accessible name (“What’s new, 2 unread”).
- One place to edit the overview (usage rule 10): Edit layout. Customize overview left the sidebar’s Support group, and the module sheet it opened is now “All modules”, reached from the New element card while editing the layout (the link read Customize overview). In search the action reads Edit layout and starts it. On phones the modules are switched in Edit, as before.
- Phones: no scrim under What’s new or the AI assistant, as the Panels guide says (bottom sheet, no scrim). The 32 % veil (`m-veil`) is gone from the app shell and the prototype; the sheets close with ×, a swipe down or Escape, as before.

    1.1.4 October 26, 2026  One fix after a 988©STUDIO iPhone recording of 1.1.3: the Deliveries alert triangle looked frozen and dim on iOS Safari. 1.1.3, 1.1.2, 1.1.1, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 are unchanged; their zips stay as they were.

#### Fixed

- AlertMark blink sync now uses CSS animation-delay instead of setting startTime, fixing a frozen/dim triangle on iOS Safari. On a real iPhone the triangle stayed dim and went fully off for about a frame every 1.2 s until the page was touched (not reduced motion; Playwright’s WebKit did not show it). Each blinking mark now gets an animation-delay once, from the page’s clock, so every triangle still blinks on the same beat, including marks drawn later; nothing writes to the animation from script any more. On this site, examples that hold a blinking triangle are no longer skipped by content-visibility when out of view. Same keyframes and timing (in over 90 ms, on for 420 ms, out over 150 ms, off for the rest of 1.2 s); with reduced motion it still stays on.

    1.1.3 October 26, 2026  Two fixes after 988©STUDIO reviews of 1.1.2: card lists still stopped on their rows with a mouse on a desktop, and the Deliveries alert triangle blinked out of step on this site. 1.1.2, 1.1.1, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 are unchanged; their zips stay as they were.

#### Fixed

- Card lists on a desktop (988©STUDIO, 26 October: «sigue haciendo snap con ratón en escritorio»): 1.1.2 took the snap off only when the wheel’s events looked like a mouse’s, and a mouse can read as a trackpad (in Chromium at 2× scale each notch arrives as half a notch), so the rows still snapped. The snap no longer depends on the wheel: on a desktop (a pointer that hovers and is fine, `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`: mouse or trackpad) card lists and scroll areas have no row snap and stop wherever the wheel leaves them, still eased with a mouse. Touch screens (phones, tablets) keep the stop on each row.
- Alert triangle in Deliveries, on this site (988©STUDIO, 26 October: the blink looked wrong on a phone): each triangle keeps the document’s clock (AlertMark, 1.0.0-alpha.23), but only once its example had woken up; until then it blinked on its own beat and jumped when the example woke, a second or more after it came into view in Safari. The pages now put every triangle on the same clock from the first frame. Same animation and timing; with reduced motion it still stays on.

    1.1.2 October 26, 2026  988©STUDIO reviews of the prototype on 1.1.1: where the sidebar’s rows disappear when it scrolls, a menu that reopened where it was left, and the mouse wheel in card lists without the stop on each row. 1.1.1, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 are unchanged; their zips stay as they were.

#### Changed

- Mouse wheel in lists that stop on their rows (988©STUDIO review 20261026-1451, note 2: smooth scroll without the snap, with a mouse only): a card list a mouse wheel scrolls keeps its snap off and stops wherever the wheel leaves it, still eased; in 1.1.0 it eased to the nearest row after each turn of the wheel, which felt like a jump in short lists such as Recurring orders. The first touch or pen gives the snap back; touch screens, trackpads and the keyboard are unchanged.

#### Fixed

- Sidebar and rail, when the column scrolls (988©STUDIO, iPad): the rows disappeared 32 px below the top bar, under the logo’s margin (at 101 px; the bar ends at 69). They now disappear level with the foot of the top bar: the logo row and the top bar share one height (--top-h, 69 px; on a tablet both add the same safe area) and the logo’s 32 px of air moved inside the scrolling column, so at rest every row stays where it was. Phones are unchanged: the drawer scrolls whole, logo included.
- Menu (988©STUDIO review 20261026-1451, note 1): the phone’s drawer and the tablet’s sidebar reopened where they had been scrolled the last time. A menu that opens over the page now opens at the top every time (Sidebar, before the first frame). The desktop sidebar, which folds in place, keeps its scroll.

    1.1.1 October 26, 2026  988©STUDIO review of the prototype on 1.1.0: the phone’s search field, the logo’s last letter and the phone’s bottom bar, which now floats. The dashboard’s native mode is dark, so the app demos open dark on these light pages. 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 are unchanged; their zips stay as they were.

#### Added

- Floating bottom bar, phone (988©STUDIO, after the prototype’s A/B test): the same items, icons, labels, active pill and badges, drawn as a capsule that does not touch the edges. 12 px from each side and 12 px above the safe area, 64 px tall, the full corner radius, 8 px inside each end, elevation 2 instead of the hairline. The page scrolls under it and ends 100 px plus the safe area lower, so the last card clears it; the drawer ends in 76 px of room, so View mode clears it; it floats whole over the open drawer and steps aside while the layout is edited; toasts over the page sit 92 px up (PHONE_TOAST_BOTTOM).
- The capsule is the same in both themes: PhoneNav is a dark-theme scope (data-theme="dark" on the nav), so a light page shows the dark bar, with the dark theme’s surface, icons, labels, active pill and badges. Its shadow is the page’s. theme="light" or theme="page" draws it otherwise.
- Theme scopes inside the app: a data-theme on any element in the shell resolves the app’s names from that scope’s tokens, and the shell’s light and dark rules follow the nearest scope, so a dark frame inside a light page (or the reverse) draws as one theme.
- AppDemo theme (default dark) and ThemeScope: the frame carries its own theme and its View mode switch changes the frame only; theme="page" follows and switches the page, as the product does.

#### Changed

- The documentation’s app demos (App shell, AI assistant, Customize overview, Unbuilt module) open in dark, the dashboard’s native mode, whatever this site’s theme. The site itself still reads in light by default (or the system’s theme), and the card and overview specimens follow it.
- Phone bottom bar badge: the solid danger fill, as the system’s Badge, so its white numeral reads 4.53:1 in both themes (on the dark theme’s brighter danger it read 3.61:1).

#### Fixed

- Top-bar search (988©STUDIO, iPhone): the app shell’s resets drew a second green box inside the pill while typing, and took the clear button’s automatic left margin, so on touch screens the × sat over the text. The shell’s resets and its focus outline now leave the SearchField alone, as they leave dialogs and the cards; the pill keeps its own ring, and the clear button its own focus outline.
- Logo (988©STUDIO review 20261026-1337): the italic M of «TM» was clipped by 2 px at the end of the wordmark; the wordmark has 3 px of room inside its clip, and still fades when the sidebar folds.

    1.1.0 October 26, 2026  What building the Orbex prototype on 1.0.0 asked of the system (pending items 1 to 21), 988©STUDIO review of 1.0.0 (smooth mouse wheel; the assistant’s conversation on phones) and the rail on short tablet screens. The patterns become a package, the top-bar search and the toasts get the product’s options, the sample data is v38’s own, and the sidebar keeps its rows and scrolls.

#### Added

- Patterns package, @orbex/sonar-patterns (1): the app shell, the overview cards and their panels, Customize overview, the AI assistant, Edit layout, smart search, the sample data, the overview grid and the theme helpers, as the source the documentation draws with. Apps import them instead of copying them.
- Search field, top-bar look (2, 16): variant="top-bar" fills the app bar’s 39 px search pill with a 22 px icon, 12 px text and an 18 px clear mark, as in v38; icon and clearIcon take the app’s marks. On touch screens its text is 16 px drawn at three quarters, so iOS does not zoom in and the pill looks the same.
- Search field, placement (3): popupClassName, align and popupWidth place and size the results from the app. Their head band and highlighted row read two new roles, surface.search-head and surface.search-active (v38: #F1F4F0 and #E0E9DD; dark #252C25 and #2E392E), checked for AA with every reading level.
- Search field, status icon (6): statusIcon draws a mark in the status line’s 28 px accent circle, such as the sparkle of a smart search.
- Toast (9, 10): inset centres the toasts on the main area and lifts them above a footer or a bottom app bar, as v38 does; closeButton={false} leaves out the close button, on the provider or on one toast. The close button stays by default.
- Smooth mouse wheel (22, 988©STUDIO review of 1.0.0): on a desktop with a mouse, each wheel step eases over about a quarter of a second, on the documentation pages and in every list that scrolls (cards, panels, the assistant). Touch screens, trackpads, the keyboard and scrollbars keep the browser’s own scrolling; with reduced motion the step lands at once. smoothWheel() in @orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area turns it on; every scroll area, card list and dialog does.
- Overview grid: desktopColumn and tabletColumn, the product’s fluid columns (12): 370 px at 1440 with the sidebar open, 425 folded; 346 at 820 on a tablet. v38’s 4- and 5-column layouts for very wide screens are not built yet.
- Layouts remembered per mode (13): loadLayout, saveLayout and forgetLayout keep one overview layout per mode, as v38 does in localStorage. The documentation’s examples start from the default.
- App shell: SearchSlot puts the app’s own search in the top bar (the bar draws the plain pill without it); data-shell="window" makes the shell read the device’s safe areas when it is the page (15). In the documentation’s frames they stay 0.
- Surface role surface.well-hover: the hover of a control drawn on the well (v38 .addbtn:hover: neutral 90, dark neutral 27).

#### Changed

- Sidebar and rail (prototype round 2, note 1; 14): every row keeps its v38 height and the part under the logo scrolls when the window is too short, instead of squeezing the rows to fit. On an iPad Pro 10.9” in landscape (about 1180 × 740 in Safari) the logo was pressed against the top edge and the Support icons were crushed into each other. The logo and the collapse button stay at the top; the rail’s tooltips still hang beside their row while it scrolls.
- Phone drawer (14): the rows keep their heights and the drawer scrolls under the bottom app bar, whose buttons stay on top of it, on a 64 px footer of the drawer’s own surface.
- Search field (4, 5): the first result is highlighted whenever the list opens or changes, so Enter takes it at once; Escape clears the text first and keeps the list, then closes it, as its documentation said.
- App shell, Edit layout (7): the pill reads Save layout while editing and saves when pressed, as v38. On phones the list opens at the top even when the overview had been scrolled.
- App shell, phones (8): Customize overview opens on phones too, as in v38.
- Customize overview, Reset to default (20): asks first («Reset to default layout?» · «The overview goes back to the default modules, positions and sizes.»), then brings back the default modules, positions and sizes, kept as saved, and the predefined layout menu goes back to its first role. It used to go back silently to the last saved layout.
- Sample data (11): every day’s deliveries and invoices are v38’s own (its hash of the ISO date, codes, figures and states): 04-139C has 1 item. Smart search says «deliveries & invoices» and finds INV-7712, due today, among the overdue, as v38.
- Unit menu (18): hovered, it also fills with an 8 % tint of its text, as v38’s pill.
- Search results: the status band and the highlighted row use the new search roles (v38’s colours) instead of the container surfaces.
- Search field, top-bar look: its results are placed against the window, so they stay under a top bar that sticks to the top of a page that scrolls.

#### Fixed

- Card lists and the mouse wheel (17): a list that stops on its rows pulled each wheel notch back to a row, so it stuttered. While a wheel turns over it the snap rests, and when the wheel stops the list eases once to a row, so a row that stops is never half under the fade. Touch keeps the snap.
- Orders card, New order (19): it lost its hover, because the pattern’s background shorthand wiped the button’s state layers. The pattern sets only the colour, and the hover is v38’s.
- AI assistant on touch screens (21, 23): the field is no longer focused when the sheet opens on a touch screen (with a mouse or keyboard it still is), the conversation takes a finger at once after the sheet rises, and its scroll does not pass to the page. In the documentation’s 390 × 844 phone frame the sample conversation is shorter than the sheet, so it has nothing to scroll until a question is asked; it scrolls as soon as it is longer.
- Phone top bar: opening the search no longer takes a page that scrolls back to the top when the shell is the page (prototype round 2).

    1.0.0 October 25, 2026  First stable release, identical to alpha.24. Only the version number changes; tokens and components are now a fixed base, and anything new goes into a later minor release.

    1.0.0-alpha.24 October 25, 2026  988©STUDIO review of alpha.23 on a phone and a desktop: no glow left on a card after its panel closes, Recurring orders’ fade clear of Reorder, specimens cut as far from the right edge as they start from the left, green buttons on the Panels page, and a theme switch that holds its place on the screen.

#### Changed

- Recurring orders: at rest the bottom fade ends above Reorder, clear of the button by half the room from the button to the card’s foot, instead of level with it. Only this card; the others keep their fade.
- Specimens on the component pages: a grid wider than its block is cut as far from the block’s right edge as it starts from its left edge, and scrolled to its end it stops there too (it was cut 6 px short).
- Panels page: the buttons that open each panel are filled, in the system’s green, as the product’s buttons are. Nothing else changes colour.
- Side navigation (tablets and desktops): the column is held by the top and the bottom of the window itself, with no viewport unit, so the theme switch keeps one place on the screen whether Safari’s bar shows or hides, level with the signature’s line when the page is scrolled to its end. With the alpha.23 height it rose when the bar hid.

#### Fixed

- Dialog (side panels and sheets): on a phone, closing a panel opened from a row of a list that had been scrolled gave focus back to the whole list, with its focus ring, a glow around the card once the sheet had gone. Focus goes back to what opened the panel, without its ring after a tap; the ring still shows from the keyboard.

    1.0.0-alpha.23 October 25, 2026  988©STUDIO review of alpha.22 on a phone and a desktop: card lists that never lose a row while they scroll and reach down to their footer, panels that open from the window, a steady alert blink, a theme switch that stays put, search on the phone frame, and the assistant scrolling from the start.

#### Changed

- Scroll area and card lists: the list reaches down to the card’s footer, as in the product, and the first row lies right on the title’s rule, with as much room above its content as below it, at rest too. The list no longer stops at a whole number of rows with the room under it left empty (the large space at the foot of the optional cards). The bottom fade is the product’s 24 px; rows still stop on the rule, scrolling down or up, and the last stop puts a row on it too.
- Side panels and sheets that are not modal are placed against the window, as in the product: on phones the sheet rises from the bottom of the screen; on tablets and desktops the panel runs the full height of the window at its edge. They had been placed against the card, the example or the section that opened them. The drawn app frames still hold their own panels.
- Overview, New order: the same room above and below its add button, so the button and its two lines sit centred between the rules (the product has 9 px above and 6 below; the card keeps its height).
- Side navigation (tablets and desktops): its height is the window’s smallest, so the theme switch at its foot no longer moves when Safari’s bars grow or shrink or the page scrolls. Its scrollbar runs at the very edge of the column, clear of the links.

#### Fixed

- Cards: rows vanished while a list scrolled (the room under the last whole row was hidden during the scroll) and, in Safari, a list could re-measure itself mid-scroll and jump to another row when an example out of view was skipped by the browser and drawn again. Both are gone: a list no longer changes its height when it fits again, so skipping examples out of view, which keeps taps on Cards quick, no longer moves it.
- Alert mark: every blinking mark keeps one beat, on the product’s 1.2 s cycle (in 90 ms, on 420 ms, out 150 ms). Marks drawn at different moments blinked out of step.
- Scroll area example: the list drew a second rule under the title’s.
- App shell, phone frame: the search button opens the search across the top bar, with Cancel, as in the product.
- AI assistant: the conversation opens at its latest line and scrolls before the first message is sent.

    1.0.0-alpha.22 October 25, 2026  988©STUDIO review of alpha.21: even room around Previous and Next, a side navigation that stays still, lists that stop with even room on the title’s rule, Notifications as in v38, a lighter Cards page, and checks in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

#### Added

- Notifications: the delay unfolds its help, “What to do in this case?”, with FAQs, Support, Contact and Call the driver, on a press anywhere on it but its code, as in v38 (the spatial unfold, 320 ms open and 200 ms closed). The list has v38’s nine notices.

#### Changed

- Previous and Next: the same room under them down to the signature’s rule as from the rule above them, 36 px each side (it was 36 above and 60 below). The same on every page.
- Side navigation (tablets and desktops): a column fixed to the window that scrolls on its own. At its top or bottom it no longer bounces, and the page does not scroll on with it; only the content bounces.
- Scroll area: a row that stops at the top lies on the title’s rule, with as much room above its content as below it, down to its own rule; the last stop mirrors the first. The area shows whole rows (or whole groups and files) at every stop, and the fades cover only the room inside a row (or between bands), so no row that has stopped is half covered. Checked in every card with a list: Invoices, Credit notes, Notifications, Latest documents, Scheduled orders, Deliveries and Recurring orders.
- Cards page: the live examples come to life as they come near (they waited for the page to be idle, all at once), and examples out of view are skipped by the browser until they come near, at their own height. After arriving and jumping to the end, nothing keeps the page busy.

#### Fixed

- Notifications: the notices touched each other; they are 8 px apart again, with v38’s rounded corners, and in dark mode take v38’s stronger bands.
- Scroll area: a list could keep measuring itself every frame, which kept heavy pages busy.

    1.0.0-alpha.21 October 25, 2026  988©STUDIO review of alpha.20: the side navigation on tablets, Previous and Next and the signature at the foot of short pages, lists that stop on their rows, Release stock and download notices in the demos, and fixes for touch.

#### Added

- Scroll area: the list stops on its rows, scrolling down or up, so the first row shown starts at the rule above it; with rows of one height it shows a whole number of them, so the last row ends at the rule below. Lists in a card (CardScroll) stop on their rows too.
- App shell: Release stock works as in the product. The Inventory card releases half of what is on hold (840 → 420 plt; the ring and the figures move to it) and a toast says “Stock released”, with Undo.
- Cards: the download buttons of Invoices, Credit notes and Latest documents, and Download PDF in Invoice details, say so with the system’s toast (“INV-0025698.pdf downloaded”), as in the product.

#### Changed

- Documentation site: on tablets (from 744 px) the side navigation is always there, as on the desktop, instead of the drawer. Examples and tables now follow the page’s own width, which is narrower beside the navigation. The product’s own rules (Layout › Navigation by device) are unchanged.
- Short pages: Previous and Next and the signature sit at the foot of the window; the space left over opens above the rule of Previous and Next.
- Signature: on tablets and desktops its line sits level with the theme switch at the foot of the navigation; on phones it has as much air below as between its rule and its line.
- AI assistant: on tablets, phones and any touch screen the window no longer resizes from its edges and corners, and the corner mark is gone; the button in its top bar still toggles its two sizes. With a mouse on the desktop it resizes as in v38.

#### Fixed

- Previous and Next answer the first tap. At the foot of the page a finger often arrives while the page still glides or bounces, and iOS kept that tap to stop the page; a tap that gets no click now follows the link. On touch they no longer take the hover state, and they wait for no double-tap.
- Panels: closing one with a press left a glowing ring around the list it was opened from (in Safari the list, not the button, had taken focus). Focus now goes back to what was pressed, without its ring; from the keyboard the ring returns as before.
- Edit layout in the App shell’s frames on the iPad: the cards could not be dragged by touch. While editing, a touch on a handle never starts a scroll, and the page refuses to scroll under a held card, whatever the frame’s scale.
- Cards page, 744–840 px: the anatomy key overflowed the page sideways; it now stacks by the page’s width.

#### Added

- Panels that are not modal keep the keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab go round inside them, and on phones the page behind a sheet is inert, so a screen reader stays in it. Escape, × and the return of focus work as before.

- Edit layout: with a finger, the move and remove handles answer in at least 44 × 44 px; nothing is drawn larger.

#### Fixed

- Edit layout on tablets and phones: a card dragged to another column froze, lifted, until the next touch. The card is now held by the grid, so it follows the finger across columns and drops into its slot.
- Edit layout: after a card changed column it could fly away from the pointer, and its first move sent it to the end of its own column. Where it lands is now worked out from the layout, and it stays under the pointer.

    1.0.0-alpha.13 October 23, 2026  The overview at its real size, side panels without a scrim, an animated theme switch, and colors, charts and small parts brought exactly in line with the product.

#### Added

- Motion: fixed duration tokens for hover, panels, sheets, menus, search, tooltips, the theme switch and cards changing columns, with three new curves (accelerate, emphasized and crossfade). The Motion page lists them and describes the theme switch.
- Theme switch: the knob slides first, then the whole page cross-fades into the new theme in 700 ms. Without View Transitions, colors ease over 250 ms; with reduced motion, the change is immediate.
- Color: muted and meta text roles, and two anchored neutral families holding the product’s exact dark surfaces and grays. The Color page gives the contrast of each of these colors on cards.
- Text field: a suffix, such as the unit after a quantity.
- Status: the label can be hidden, leaving the dot with its name for screen readers.
- Dialog: non-modal side panels, which leave the page usable behind them, and a bottom sheet on phones that closes with a swipe down.

- Editing the overview: the demo draws the grid at 1:1, three columns of 370 px as on a 1440 px desktop or two of 341 px as on an 820 px tablet, in a frame that scrolls sideways. Tablet handles are larger. A lifted card grows to 103 %, neighbors make room in 320 ms, a dropped card glides into place in 500 ms, a resized card eases to its height, and cards travel to their new columns in 620 ms.
- Side panels: no scrim, below the top bar, 402 px wide with rounded leading corners and a soft shadow; the row that opened one stays marked. They arrive in 420 ms and leave in 150 ms. On phones, details open in a bottom sheet with a handle.
- Trend chart: the daily line dashed and the running total dotted, the whole month with axes from 0, ticks on the 1st, 15th and last day, the legend in plain text, and one figure at a time in a bubble beside its point.
- Unit menu: a small pill that stays a pill while open, with the units in capitals and no heading.

- Menus, search results and tooltips open and close with the product’s timings.
- Phone navigation: the top bar holds the logo, the account switch and search; the bottom bar holds Alerts, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu.
- Colors: dark surfaces, lines and grays, the secondary, muted, meta and disabled text, control borders, the scrim and the chart lines take the product’s values; each still meets its contrast minimum.

- RingChart takes a direction. Card takes a label for when the same card shows twice on a page.

#### Changed

- Deliveries: week and month views from March to June, a week strip that keeps the chosen day in the middle, an alert on a delayed delivery, an empty day that points to the next delivery, and View opening its details.
- Balance: the payment calendar, folded, with each invoice’s details. Orders: Previous and Next by name, and New order opening its panel. Daily shipments: a closed month shows its total.
- Inventory: on hold runs counterclockwise toward its figure. Recurring orders: a quick action, stock lines, an out-of-stock product with its alternative, and Reorder opening its review.
- Figures count to their new value when the unit changes.

#### Fixed

- Recurring orders XL fills its size with the list instead of leaving room at the foot.
- Cards: region names no longer repeat when a card shows in several sizes.

    1.0.0-alpha.6 October 23, 2026  Cards that keep their header and footer in place, and a site that is easier to move around.

#### Added

- CardScroll: the list in a card that scrolls first when the card’s size leaves no room. The card’s budget is 4 KB, named in the build with its reason.
- An index page for each section, a breadcrumb on every page, and links to the previous and next page.

#### Changed

- Cards keep their header and footer in place and scroll what does not fit between them: no scrollbar, a fade at the edge that has more, a thin indicator while scrolling.
- Deliveries shows every delivery of the day and Recurring orders every product, scrolling when needed, instead of cutting the list.

    1.0.0-alpha.5 October 23, 2026  Accessibility written down, and every size, variant and state on view.

#### Added

- Accessibility: the WCAG 2.2 AA commitments and how each is checked, and on every component page the keys it answers to and what it gives assistive technology.
- Sizes, variants and states on every component page, side by side, hover, focus and press included; each card in every size it offers.
- ChartLegend, under every chart that needs one.
- color.warning.container, in place of a tint mixed inside the notice. The contrast contract measures every notice tint over the card and the page.

#### Changed

- Tick bars draw one row of ticks for the whole bar: parts meet without a gap and no tick is split in two colors.
- The notice action takes the strong text level, which passes on every tint.
- The sample data agree with each other: every card reads Tuesday, May 12, 2026.
- The unit menu and the month and day buttons are named by the text they show.

#### Fixed

- Hidden text in Segmented control, Badge and Trend chart could widen a scrolling page; each component now contains its own.
- Pages open at the top, and long code scrolls inside its block.

    1.0.0-alpha.4 October 23, 2026  The overview: its cards, charts and patterns.

#### Added

- Patterns: the six cards of the overview, built only from the system, and pages for charts, the overview, feedback and editing the overview.
- Components: Card with CardLink and UnitMenu, TickBar, RingChart and TrendChart, Notice, and Toast on Base UI. Each chart is its own entry point.

#### Changed

- Calendars leave the days of other months empty.
- A chart series that is turned off keeps its name at the tertiary level, with a hollow marker.
- The order of the cascade layers is declared before any stylesheet, so a bundler can never put the reset after the system.

#### Fixed

- List markers showed beside lists drawn as layouts. Every list with role="list" drops its markers.

    1.0.0-alpha.3 October 22, 2026  The first components.

#### Added

- A new package, @orbex/sonar-components: Button, IconButton, Badge, Status, Switch, Checkbox, SegmentedControl, TextField, SelectField, Menu, Tooltip and Dialog. Native HTML first; Base UI for the menu and the tooltip.
- One entry point and one stylesheet per component, a 3 KB gzipped budget each, and the props of every component published as data (api.json) and in /llms.txt.
- Tokens for control and icon sizes, and the focus ring (color.focus, at 3:1 or more on every surface).
- Changesets: tokens and components are released together.

#### Changed

- Cascade layers: the system lives under one layer, sonar, with tokens and components inside. Apps put their reset before it and their own styles after: @layer reset, sonar, app.

    1.0.0-alpha.2 October 22, 2026  Contrast on every surface, and layout tokens.

#### Added

- Layout tokens: size classes, card heights, margins, bars and the drawer. Groups keyed by size class follow the window, and sizeClasses gives scripts the same breakpoints.
- Pages: Breakpoints and grid, Navigation by device.

#### Changed

- Tertiary text is neutral 43 in light and 65 in dark, so it passes AA on containers and selected rows too.
- Placeholders read at the tertiary level; disabled text is held at 3:1.
- Danger text in dark is a lighter red, which passes on selected rows.
- Layout values sit on the 2 px base: desktop margins are 32 px, the top bar 68 px.
- Breaking: layout.sidebar.expanded and layout.sidebar.collapsed are renamed layout.sidebar and layout.rail, so they no longer share names with the size classes.

#### Fixed

- Contrast is never lowered with opacity; days outside the month are not shown, and decorative previews are hidden from assistive technology.

    1.0.0-alpha.1 October 18, 2026  The first release: the tokens.

#### Added

- Tokens in the W3C Design Tokens format, as CSS custom properties and typed data.
- A palette whose neutrals are generated from the brand hue, named by lightness.
- Six text levels defined by contrast; colored text roles (accent, danger, warning) in their own tones; a danger.solid role for badges.
- Named type roles, and motion springs stored as a duration and a bounce, with curves generated by the build.

#### Changed

- The brand green is #1A8838 (0.8 ΔE from #1E8A3A), so white text on green buttons reaches 4.5:1.
- In dark, text on green buttons is dark green, at 5.3:1.

How versions are numbered, and how a token is deprecated before it goes, is in [Principles](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/principles/#versioning).

# Installation · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/

> Install the Orbex Sonar-DB tokens and components, set the cascade layers and use a first component.

## Installation

Two packages, released together under one version: the tokens, which any stack can use, and the React components built on them. Five steps from an empty app to a first component.

### 1. Install the packages

Node 22.18 or later, React 19.2 or later. The components depend on the tokens and on Base UI, which npm installs with them.

 sh

```
npm install @orbex/sonar-tokens@1.1.6 @orbex/sonar-components@1.1.6 react react-dom
```

### 2. Set the cascade layers

The system’s styles live in one cascade layer, `sonar`, with `sonar.tokens` and `sonar.components` inside. Declare the order once, before any stylesheet loads, so a reset can never override the system and the app’s own styles always win without `!important`.

 css

```
/* Once, before any stylesheet (a <style> at the top of <head> is safest, since bundlers may reorder files):
   the order of the layers. The system sits under one name, sonar: after any reset, before the app’s own styles. */
@layer reset, sonar, app;
```

### 3. Import the tokens

 css

```
/* At the root of the app, once: every token as a CSS custom property, in both themes */
@import '@orbex/sonar-tokens/tokens.css';

/* Optional: the type roles as classes (.sonar-type-title-md …) */
@import '@orbex/sonar-tokens/type.css';
```

Style with role tokens, which describe what a value is for and change with the theme. Palette tokens stay underneath: a component never reads them.

 css

```
.delivery-card {
  background: var(--sonar-color-surface-card);
  border-radius: var(--sonar-shape-corner-medium);
  box-shadow: var(--sonar-elevation-1);
  color: var(--sonar-color-text-default);
  padding: var(--sonar-space-16) var(--sonar-space-20);
}
```

Both themes ship in the same file. Without an attribute, the system follows the operating system; `data-theme` forces a theme on an element and everything inside it.

 html

```
<!-- Follows the operating system by default. Force a theme on any element and everything inside it -->
<html data-theme="dark">
<aside data-theme="light">…</aside>
```

### 4. Use a component

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. All 24 weigh 47.8 KB gzipped together, script and styles.

 tsx

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/button.css'

export function PlaceOrder() {
  return <Button onClick={() => console.log('Order placed')}>Place order</Button>
}
```

 tsx

```
/* Apps that use most components: every component’s styles in one file */
import '@orbex/sonar-components/styles.css'

import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
```

Components take icons as elements: the [Icons](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/icons/#import) page shows how to make one from Material Symbols.

### 5. Read tokens and props from code

The tokens are also typed data, for scripts, charts and tools. The props of every component are published as JSON, in the package as `@orbex/sonar-components/api.json` and on this site at [/api.json](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/api.json); [/llms.txt](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/llms.txt) describes the whole system for coding agents.

 ts

```
import { tokens, sizeClasses } from '@orbex/sonar-tokens'

/* Every token with its CSS variable, description and value in each theme */
const accent = tokens.find((token) => token.name === 'color.accent')

/* The window size classes, with a media query for each */
const compact = matchMedia(sizeClasses[0].media).matches
```

# Foundations · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/

> The principles and the accessibility commitments, and the tokens every component is drawn with.

## Foundations

The principles and the accessibility commitments, and the tokens every component is drawn with.

- ### [Principles](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/principles/)

What the system optimizes for, and how tokens are named, versioned and tested.
- ### [Accessibility](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/accessibility/)

WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, focus, target sizes, motion, keyboard and screen readers.
- ### [Color](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/color/)

The palette, the roles for text, surfaces and states in both themes, and the contrast of every pair.
- ### [Typography](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/typography/)

Three families and the type roles of the product, from figures in a chart to page titles.
- ### [Icons](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/icons/)

The marks the components draw, the Material Symbols the product uses, their sizes, weight and how to import them.
- ### [Spacing](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/spacing/)

The spacing scale, and how cards and their content line up.
- ### [Shape](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/shape/)

Corner radii, from the tightest to fully round, and what each is for.
- ### [Elevation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/elevation/)

Shadows for cards, menus, panels and dragged cards, in both themes.
- ### [Motion](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/motion/)

Springs and fades: durations, easing, and what changes with reduced motion.

# Principles and governance · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/principles/

> What the Sonar-DB design system optimizes for, how its tokens are organized, named, versioned and tested.

## Principles and governance

What the system optimizes for, and the rules that keep it coherent as it grows: how tokens are organized and named, how themes work, what is tested, and how changes are versioned.

### Principles

- #### Figures first

People open Sonar-DB to read quantities: pallets on hold, deliveries due, invoices overdue. Type stays small and steady, and hierarchy comes from weight and color, so a column of figures scans in one pass.
- #### Measured, not picked

Neutrals come from one formula, text levels from contrast targets, springs from a duration and a bounce. A value that can be explained can be extended without guessing.
- #### Calm by default, expressive on purpose

Motion settles without overshoot and color is reserved for meaning. The Material 3 Expressive character shows in shape and in two moments: dropping a card into place and a confirmed success.
- #### One system at every width

From a 402 px phone to a five-column ultra-wide monitor, the same tokens and the same components. Layouts are derived from the desktop reading order rather than designed five times.
- #### Accessible by contract

Contrast targets are written down and tested on every build. Touch targets are 48 px, status never relies on color alone, and reduced motion is respected.

### Three tiers

Tokens are layered. Each tier only refers to the one below it, so a palette change reaches every component through the roles, and a component never hard-codes a color.

*Figure: Palette feeds roles, roles feed components.*

### Naming

Every custom property starts with `--sonar-`, then goes from general to specific. Palette names describe what a color looks like; every other name describes what it is for, so a role keeps its name when its value changes. Names are in English, in full words, without abbreviations.

*Naming examples*

| Example | Pattern | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-palette-neutral-24` | `palette-{family}-{tone}` | Describes appearance. Never used by components. |
| `--sonar-color-text-tertiary` | `color-{role}-{level}` | Describes purpose. Values change with the theme. |
| `--sonar-color-on-accent-tonal` | `color-on-{fill}` | Content placed on a colored fill. |
| `--sonar-color-state-hover` | `color-state-{interaction}` | Translucent layer added on interaction. |
| `--sonar-type-title-lg` | `type-{role}-{size}` | A font shorthand; tracking is -tracking. |
| `--sonar-motion-spatial-fast-easing` | `motion-{kind}-{speed}-{part}` | Duration and easing come in pairs. |

### Themes

Light and dark define the same roles with different values. Without any attribute, the system follows the operating system. `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` forces a theme on the element and everything inside it, which is how this site shows both themes side by side.

The dark theme is not an inversion. Its text levels are chosen to reach the same contrast on dark surfaces as the light ones do on light surfaces, so a role reads with the same weight in both.

### Accessibility

The system aims at WCAG 2.2 AA. Contrast is a contract in the tokens package, tested in both themes on every build; focus, target sizes, motion, keyboard and screen readers are built into every component. [Accessibility](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/accessibility/) sets out each commitment, the measured ratios and how they are checked.

### Versioning

- **Patch**: a value adjusted without a visible change (under 1 ΔE), or documentation.
- **Minor**: new tokens, new roles, new components.
- **Major**: a token renamed, removed or given a different meaning. The old name is kept for one minor release, marked `$deprecated` in the token source, before it goes.

What changed in each release is in the [changelog](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/changelog/); how to propose a token or a component, in [Contributing](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/contributing/).

---

# Accessibility · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/accessibility/

> How the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System meets WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, focus, target sizes, motion, keyboard and screen readers, and how each is checked.

## Accessibility

The system aims at WCAG 2.2, level AA, for everything it ships: tokens, components and patterns. What it can guarantee is built in and tested on every build; what only an app can know is written down as rules.

### Who does what

*What the system guarantees and what each app provides*

| The system | Contrast of every color pair, focus rings, target sizes, keyboard behavior, roles and states of every component, reduced motion. |
| --- | --- |
| The app | Page titles and headings, the language of the page, the names it gives to components (labels, button text, chart labels), error messages that say how to fix the error, and the order of content. |

### Contrast

Every text level meant to be read, placeholders included, reaches **4.5:1** on every surface that carries text, in both themes (WCAG 1.4.3). Control boundaries, the focus ring and marks such as checkboxes and chart alerts reach **3:1** (1.4.11). Disabled text is exempt from both; the system still keeps it at 3:1 so it can be read.

The 125 pairs below are a contract in the tokens package, `lib/accessibility.ts`. The token tests measure each one in both themes on every build, and a change that breaks one fails the build. Each row shows the lowest ratio across its backgrounds, measured now. Every text level on every surface is in the matrix of [Color](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/color/#contrast).

*Contrast pairs and their measured ratios*

| Foreground | On | Minimum | Lowest, light | Lowest, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text.strong` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 13.6:1 | 9.8:1 |
| `text.default` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 10.1:1 | 9.3:1 |
| `text.secondary` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 7.9:1 | 7.0:1 |
| `text.muted` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 7.3:1 | 4.7:1 |
| `text.tertiary` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 4.6:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.placeholder` | Every text surface | 4.5:1 | 4.6:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.meta` | `surface.card, surface.page, surface.raised, surface.menu, surface.hover` | 4.5:1 | 5.1:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.accent` | `surface.card, surface.page, surface.raised, surface.menu, surface.hover, surface.selected` | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 | 5.1:1 |
| `text.danger` | `surface.card, surface.page, surface.raised, surface.menu, surface.hover, surface.selected` | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 | 4.6:1 |
| `text.warning` | `surface.card, surface.page, surface.raised, surface.menu, surface.hover, surface.selected` | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 | 6.1:1 |
| `text.strong` | Every notice: the neutral container, and each tint over card and page | 4.5:1 | 13.4:1 | 9.0:1 |
| `text.default` | Every notice: the neutral container, and each tint over card and page | 4.5:1 | 9.9:1 | 8.6:1 |
| `text.accent` | `success.container over surface.card, success.container over surface.page` | 3:1 | 4.2:1 | 5.2:1 |
| `text.warning` | `warning.container over surface.card, warning.container over surface.page` | 3:1 | 4.3:1 | 5.2:1 |
| `text.danger` | `danger.container over surface.card, danger.container over surface.page` | 3:1 | 4.0:1 | 5.0:1 |
| `text.inverse` | `surface.inverse` | 4.5:1 | 11.6:1 | 11.9:1 |
| `accent.inverse` | `surface.inverse` | 4.5:1 | 7.9:1 | 4.7:1 |
| `on.accent` | `accent` | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 | 5.2:1 |
| `on.accent-tonal` | `accent.tonal` | 4.5:1 | 12.9:1 | 7.4:1 |
| `on.emphasis` | `danger.solid` | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `border.control` | `surface.card` | 3:1 | 3.1:1 | 3.3:1 |
| `focus` | `surface.card, surface.page, surface.menu, surface.container` | 3:1 | 3.6:1 | 5.4:1 |
| `accent` | `surface.card, surface.page` | 3:1 | 4.2:1 | 6.2:1 |
| `danger` | `surface.card, surface.page` | 3:1 | 4.1:1 | 4.3:1 |
| `chart.primary` | `surface.card` | 3:1 | 4.4:1 | 6.2:1 |
| `chart.secondary` | `surface.card` | 3:1 | 20.4:1 | 12.1:1 |

### Focus

- Every control shows a ring when it is reached from the keyboard (2.4.7): `focus.width` 2 px, at `focus.offset` 2 px, in `color.focus`, which keeps 3:1 against every surface it can sit on. A ring is never removed without another visible indicator in its place.
- Pointer clicks draw no ring; `:focus-visible` decides, as the browser does for its own controls.
- Nothing covers what has focus (2.4.11). On phones and tablets the top bar is sticky, so the page keeps room for it above anything scrolled into view; menus and tooltips open beside their trigger, never over it.
- A modal dialog moves focus in and returns it to what opened it; nothing else moves focus on its own.

### Target size

- WCAG 2.2 asks for targets of at least 24 × 24 px (2.5.8). Controls are 28 or 36 px tall, and spaced so that neighbors never overlap.
- On touch screens every control’s hit area grows to 48 × 48 px, `layout.touch-target`, without changing how it looks. Labels of checkboxes and switches are part of the target.

### Motion

- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, every component stops moving things across the screen: menus, dialogs, sheets and toasts appear in place, and shapes change without traveling. Short fades and color changes remain, so state changes are still visible.
- Nothing animates on load, nothing flashes, and nothing moves on its own for more than a moment.

### Keyboard

- Everything that works with a pointer works with a keyboard (2.1.1), in the order the page is read.
- Tab moves between controls; arrow keys move inside a group of options, a menu or a chart, as the platform does. Each component page lists its keys under Accessibility.
- Only a modal dialog keeps focus inside it, by design, and Escape always leaves it (2.1.2).

### Screen readers

- **Native first.** Buttons, checkboxes, switches, radios, fields and dialogs are the browser’s own elements, so their roles and states are right in every screen reader. Base UI supplies the rest (menus, tooltips, toasts) following the WAI-ARIA patterns.
- **Every control has a name.** Icon buttons require one; icons are hidden; repeated buttons say what they act on.
- **Never color alone** (1.4.1). States are written; legends name every color; charts list their values in words.
- **Changes are announced.** Toasts arrive in a polite live region, and a card announces what its step buttons change: the day, the due date, the month.
- **Regions.** Each card of the overview is a region named by its title, so the overview can be read card by card.

### Reflow and text

- Pages reflow down to 320 px without scrolling sideways (1.4.10). Long code and wide tables scroll inside their own block, which can be focused and scrolled from the keyboard.
- Text sizes are in the type roles and scale with the browser’s text size (1.4.4); nothing is set to stop zoom.
- Cards in the overview grid have one of four heights. With very large text or extra text spacing (1.4.12) nothing is cut: content that no longer fits scrolls inside the card, between its header and footer, and can be scrolled from the keyboard.

### How it is checked

- **On every build, automatically:** the 125 contrast pairs in both themes; every component rendered and checked with axe in its tests.
- **Before every release, by hand and with scripts:** every page of this site at 360, 390, 430, 834, 1024 and 1440 px, light and dark, with every code block open, checked for anything that scrolls the page sideways; a keyboard pass through every component; VoiceOver on iOS and macOS through every component; text at 200%.

### Known limits

- **The Sonar-DB dashboard** is audited on its own, once it is built on these tokens and components; this site covers the system, the patterns and their live examples.

---

# Color · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/color/

> How the Sonar-DB palette is built, the semantic color roles and their measured contrast in both themes.

## Color

A brand green, three status hues and a family of green-tinted neutrals. Components never use the palette directly: they use roles, and every role that carries text is measured against the surfaces it sits on.

### How the palette is built

Brand and status colors are **anchors**, exact values chosen by design. When a role needs another tone of an anchor, for instance red text that must reach 4.5:1, that tone is **derived**: same hue and chroma, different lightness. Derived tones are outlined below.

Neutrals are **generated**. They are the brand green at very low chroma, from one formula. The hue drifts slightly from dark to light, as the hand-picked originals did, and the chroma eases off near black and white, where tint reads as dirt. Every tone is named by its CIELAB lightness L*, from 0 (black) to 100 (white), so the distance between two names predicts their contrast.

Two neutral families are anchors instead: **neutral-dark** holds the product’s exact dark surfaces, lines and grays, and **neutral-light** the few light-theme grays that do not fall on the formula.

 text

```
hue(tone)    = 144° − 0.09 × tone
chroma(tone) = 8.2 − 0.00125 × (tone − 55)²

neutral          chroma(tone)
neutral-tinted   chroma(tone) + 2.4
neutral-subdued  chroma(tone) × 0.5
```

#### neutral

Brand-tinted neutral. Text, lines and most surfaces.

1. 5 `#0B130B`
2. 6 `#0E150E`
3. 10 `#171D17`
4. 12 `#1B211B`
5. 14 `#1F251E`
6. 16 `#232A22`
7. 18 `#272E26`
8. 21 `#2D352C`
9. 22 `#2F372E`
10. 24 `#333B32`
11. 27 `#3A4239`
12. 28 `#3C443B`
13. 31 `#424B42`
14. 33 `#475046`
15. 34 `#495348`
16. 43 `#5E685D`
17. 46 `#667064`
18. 47 `#687266`
19. 48 `#6B7569`
20. 57 `#828C7F`
21. 59 `#879184`
22. 60 `#899487`
23. 65 `#97A194`
24. 67 `#9CA699`
25. 72 `#AAB3A7`
26. 74 `#AFB9AC`
27. 76 `#B5BEB2`
28. 78 `#BAC4B7`
29. 80 `#C0C9BD`
30. 84 `#CBD4C8`
31. 85 `#CED7CB`
32. 88 `#D7DFD4`
33. 90 `#DDE5D9`
34. 91 `#E0E8DC`
35. 92 `#E3EADF`
36. 93 `#E5EDE2`
37. 95 `#EBF3E8`
38. 96 `#EEF6EB`

#### neutral-tinted

A greener neutral for map land use, chart remainders and hover fills on dark surfaces.

1. 19 `#263126`
2. 23 `#2F3A2E`
3. 27 `#374336`
4. 36 `#4C584A`
5. 41 `#576456`

#### neutral-subdued

A quieter neutral for the dark canvas, the inverse surface and the search field.

1. 2 `#040904`
2. 20 `#2E312D`
3. 96 `#F1F5EF`

#### neutral-dark

The exact neutrals of the product’s dark theme, where the formula lands one RGB step away: surfaces, lines and the text levels it names, and the search results’ head and highlighted row (1.1).

1. 2 `#050705`
2. 6 `#0F150F`
3. 12 `#1B221B`
4. 14 `#1F251F`
5. 15 `#212921`
6. 16 `#222B22`
7. 17 `#252C25`
8. 21 `#2C342B`
9. 22 `#2E362E`
10. 23 `#2E392E`
11. 27 `#3A433A`
12. 48 `#6C766A`
13. 59 `#889285`
14. 67 `#9CA699`
15. 80 `#C0C8BC`
16. 88 `#D5DFD2`

### Accent

The brand green marks what can be acted on and what is selected. Its tonal version fills selected navigation items and segments; white text on the solid green reaches 4.5:1. Its container tint fills [drop placeholders](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/#states), the slot a card lands in while the overview is edited.

*Accent roles*

| Token | Preview | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-color-accent`  Brand green: primary buttons, active navigation, selected controls and link icons. |  | palette.green.50 `#1A8838` | palette.green.67 `#76B27C` |
| `--sonar-color-accent-container`  Soft accent background: drop placeholders, the slot a card lands in while the overview is edited. |  | palette.green.91 `#CDEFD0` | palette.green.81 `#97D99C29` |
| `--sonar-color-accent-tonal`  Tonal fill for the selected item in navigation and segmented controls. |  | palette.green.90 `#D0E8CE` | palette.green.29 `#2F4B31` |
| `--sonar-color-accent-inverse`  Accent on inverse surfaces, such as the action in a toast. |  | palette.green.81 `#97D99C` | palette.green.40 `#1E6B30` |
| `--sonar-color-on-accent`  Text and icons on the accent fill. |  | palette.white `#FFFFFF` | palette.green.20 `#00390F` |
| `--sonar-color-on-accent-tonal`  Text and icons on the tonal accent fill. |  | palette.green.11 `#0F2112` | palette.green.90 `#D0E8CE` |
| `--sonar-color-on-emphasis`  Text on saturated fills (accent or danger) that stays white in both themes, such as badges. |  | palette.white `#FFFFFF` | palette.white `#FFFFFF` |

### Text and icons

Emphasis levels, defined by contrast so both themes read alike. **Every level meant to be read passes WCAG AA (4.5:1) on every surface**, containers, selected rows and menus included. Icons use the same levels as the text beside them.

**Placeholder** text is text: WCAG makes no exception for it, so it reads at the tertiary level. It keeps a role of its own so fields can change it without touching tertiary. **Disabled** is exempt in WCAG and takes the product’s own gray; the control keeps its outline or shape, so it still reads as present.

**Muted** is body text one step quieter than default. **Meta** is for dates, units and supporting figures: in dark it is the product’s own gray, quieter than tertiary. In light the product’s gray, `#737D71`, reaches only 4.21:1 on a card and 3.73:1 on the page, below 4.5:1, so meta takes the tertiary tone, `#5E685D`: 5.71:1 on a card, 5.05:1 on the page.

Colored text uses darker tones than the fills of the same hue in light, and lighter ones in dark. It sits on cards, pages, menus and rows; on containers, status is shown with an icon or a chip.

*Text roles*

| Token | Preview | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-color-text-strong`  Titles and key figures. |  | palette.neutral.10 `#171D17` 16.7:1 | palette.neutral.92 `#E3EADF` 12.7:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-default`  Body text. |  | palette.neutral.21 `#2D352C` 12.3:1 | palette.neutral.90 `#DDE5D9` 12.1:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-secondary`  Navigation at rest, secondary text and icons. |  | palette.neutral-light.28 `#3D453B` 9.6:1 | palette.neutral-dark.80 `#C0C8BC` 9.1:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-muted`  Body text one step quieter than default, such as the reading of a search. |  | palette.neutral-light.30 `#424A40` 8.9:1 | palette.neutral-dark.67 `#9CA699` 6.2:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-tertiary`  Placeholders, hints and inactive legend entries: the faintest text, still 4.5:1. |  | palette.neutral.43 `#5E685D` 5.6:1 | palette.neutral.65 `#97A194` 5.8:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-meta`  Metadata and small labels: dates, units, supporting figures. The same as tertiary in light, where the product’s own gray falls below 4.5:1; quieter than tertiary in dark. |  | text.tertiary `#5E685D` 5.6:1 | palette.neutral-dark.59 `#889285` 4.8:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-placeholder`  Placeholder text in fields. Placeholders are text, so they read at the tertiary level; a role of its own lets fields change it without touching tertiary. |  | text.tertiary `#5E685D` 5.6:1 | text.tertiary `#97A194` 5.8:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-disabled`  Disabled controls. Exempt from contrast in WCAG; the control keeps its outline or shape so it still reads as present. |  | palette.neutral-light.76 `#B4BEB1` 1.8:1 | palette.neutral-dark.27 `#3A433A` 1.5:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-inverse`  Text on inverse surfaces: tooltips, toasts. |  | palette.neutral.95 `#EBF3E8` 11.6:1 | palette.neutral.12 `#1B211B` 11.9:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-accent`  Accent-colored text: positive figures, links. |  | palette.green.46 `#047E2F` 5.0:1 | palette.green.67 `#76B27C` 6.2:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-danger`  Danger-colored text. |  | palette.red.46 `#D1282D` 5.0:1 | palette.red.64 `#F97068` 5.6:1 |
| `--sonar-color-text-warning`  Warning-colored text. |  | palette.orange.46 `#A15C00` 5.0:1 | palette.orange.73 `#F2A23F` 7.4:1 |

### Text that is not read

- **Never lower contrast with opacity**, with one exception kept from the product: a chart’s running-total toggle fades to 40 % when off. Its state is also given by `aria-pressed` and by its line leaving the chart.
- **Neighboring days are context, not content.** A month calendar fills its six rows with the days of the months around it in the disabled gray; each of those days reads at full contrast in its own month.
- **Decorative previews are hidden from assistive technology.** A glimpse of the next day at the edge of a scrolling view carries `aria-hidden="true"` and no focusable content. It is exempt from contrast because the same content is one swipe away, at full contrast.

### Surfaces

Light surfaces are achromatic grays with a white top bar; the green tint appears in containers, menus and states. In the dark theme everything is tinted and steps up in lightness as it comes closer.

### Contrast

The colors below are the product’s own. Each is kept as it is because it passes its minimum where it is used: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for icons, chart lines and control boundaries.

*Product colors on cards*

| Role | Used for | Light | Dark | Minimum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text.secondary` | Secondary text and icons | 9.6:1 | 9.1:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.muted` | Quieter body text | 8.9:1 | 6.2:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.meta` | Dates, units, supporting figures | 5.6:1 | 4.8:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.danger` | Red text | 5.0:1 | 5.6:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.accent` | Green text | 5.0:1 | 6.2:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `text.warning` | Orange text | 5.0:1 | 7.4:1 | 4.5:1 |
| `danger` | Alert icons and marks | 4.4:1 | 4.3:1 | 3:1 |
| `border.control` | Field and pill outlines | 3.1:1 | 3.3:1 | 3:1 |
| `chart.primary` | Daily line (dashed) | 4.4:1 | 6.2:1 | 3:1 |
| `chart.secondary` | Running total (dotted) | 20.4:1 | 12.1:1 | 3:1 |
| `text.disabled` | Disabled controls | 1.8:1 (exempt) | 1.5:1 (exempt) | Exempt |

The full matrix is measured from the built tokens, the same way the test suite checks them on every build. Each pair is judged against its own minimum: 4.5:1 for text; disabled is exempt. Lighter figures are pairs the system does not use. Ratios are rounded down.

*Light theme*

| Text role | card | page | menu | container |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| strong | 16.7:1 , passes 4.5:1 | 15.8:1 , passes 4.5:1 | 15.1:1 , passes 4.5:1 | 13.6:1 , passes 4.5:1 |
