### Where the system departs from the product

The rule: the system takes the product’s colors unless a pair fails WCAG AA, and then accessibility wins. These are the roles where the product’s color fails and the system’s replaces it, with both ratios measured on the card (`#FDFDFC` in light, `#1F251F` in dark). Danger in dark follows the same rule: marks and fills keep the product’s `#F04B4B`, red text takes `#F97068`, and a red fill that carries white text takes `#DD3535`.

| Role | Product | Ratio | System | Ratio | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accent (light) | `#1E8A3A` | 4.42:1 | `#1A8838` | 4.54:1 | 4.5:1 on white text on it |
| Chart line, primary (light) | `#1E8A3A` | 4.34:1 | `#1A8838` | 4.46:1 | 3:1 on card |
| Meta text (light) | `#737D71` | 4.21:1 | `#5E685D` | 5.71:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Placeholder text (light) | `#8E988C` | 2.94:1 | `#5E685D` | 5.71:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Placeholder text (dark) | `#6C766A` | 3.30:1 | `#97A194` | 5.84:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Warning text (light) | `#DD8E35` | 2.58:1 | `#A15C00` | 5.10:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Control outline (light) | `#8E988C` | 2.94:1 | `#879184` | 3.22:1 | 3:1 on card |
| Danger text (light) | `#DD3535` | 4.45:1 | `#D1282D` | 5.09:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Danger text (dark) | `#F04B4B` | 4.33:1 | `#F97068` | 5.62:1 | 4.5:1 on card |
| Danger fill with white text (dark) | `#F04B4B` | 3.61:1 | `#DD3535` | 4.53:1 | 4.5:1 on white text on it |

The chart’s primary line passes with the product’s green; it follows the accent so the two never drift apart. Three more roles differ without a contrast reason, because the palette is generated by one formula: the light menu and inverse text (`#EBF3E8` for the product’s `#EEF3EA`), the dark control outline (`#687266` for `#6C766A`) and the dark chart’s second line (`#DCE5D9` for `#B7C3B4`). The light and dark neutrals land within one or two RGB steps of the product’s (ΔE under 1.7, below what the eye tells apart).

---

# Typography · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/typography/

> The Sonar-DB type families and the fourteen type roles, with sizes, weights and where each is used.

## Typography

One superfamily, fourteen roles. The interface is dense with figures, so sizes stay small and steady; hierarchy comes from weight and color more than from size.

### Families

- Orders, deliveries and stock

#### IBM Plex Sans

Every interface text.
 `--sonar-font-family-sans`
- Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su

#### IBM Plex Sans Condensed

Weekday initials and the wordmark, where width is scarce.
 `--sonar-font-family-condensed`
- 2,000 1,500 1,000

#### IBM Plex Mono

Chart axes and navigation overlines.
 `--sonar-font-family-mono`

### Roles

Names follow Material 3: headline, title, body and label, from larger to smaller and from reading to scanning. Two roles are Sonar-DB’s own: `caption` for units in pills and `data` for chart axes. Each role is a font shorthand plus its tracking.

*Type roles*

| Role | Sample | Size / line | Weight | Tracking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `headline-sm`  Amounts in detail panels. | 30,000.00 USD | 26 / 29 px Sans | Semibold | -0.26 px |
| `title-lg`  Card and panel titles. | Daily shipments | 18 / 22 px Sans | Semibold | -0.27 px |
| `title-md`  Highlighted figures and section titles inside panels. | Total 415 plt | 14 / 20 px Sans | Semibold | -0.21 px |
| `title-sm`  Summary lines, month names, document numbers. | Delivery 04-127C | 12 / 14 px Sans | Semibold | 0 |
| `body-lg`  Dialog and empty-state text. | The changes you made to this layout will be lost. | 14 / 20 px Sans | Regular | 0 |
| `body-md`  Rows, descriptions, list items. | Recycled-fiber cases, 120 per pallet, ready for loading. | 12 / 16 px Sans | Regular | 0 |
| `label-lg`  Account selector, legend labels. | All accounts | 14 / 17 px Sans | Medium | 0 |
| `label-md`  Figures in tables and lists, form labels, navigation items. The most used role. | 1,420 plt | 12 / 14 px Sans | Medium | -0.18 px |
| `label-md-condensed`  Weekday initials in calendars and charts. | Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su | 12 / 14 px Sans Condensed | Regular | 0 |
| `label-sm`  Status chips, inline actions such as View, tooltips. | Delayed | 11 / 13 px Sans | Medium | -0.17 px |
| `button`  Filled and outlined buttons. | Create order | 13 / 16 px Sans | Semibold | -0.13 px |
| `caption`  Units in pills (PLT, KG). Always uppercase. | plt | 10 / 12 px Sans, uppercase | Regular | 0 |
| `overline`  Section headings in the navigation. Always uppercase. | Operations | 12 / 14 px Mono, uppercase | Medium | 0 |
| `data`  Chart axes and scales. | 0 500 1,000 1,500 2,000 | 10 / 12 px Mono | Regular | -0.3 px |

### In code

Use the class for markup you control, or the two custom properties inside a component’s styles.

 css

```
@import '@orbex/sonar-tokens/type.css';

<h2 class="sonar-type-title-lg">Daily shipments</h2>

/* or, inside a component */
.card-title {
  font: var(--sonar-type-title-lg);
  letter-spacing: var(--sonar-type-title-lg-tracking);
}
```

### Guidelines

- Join a figure and its unit with a non-breaking space, `1,420&nbsp;plt`, so they never wrap apart.
- Use color, not size, to step down: a tertiary date next to a strong figure reads as secondary at the same size.
- Keep uppercase to the two roles that define it. Everything else is sentence case.
- Titles are short nouns (Orders, Daily shipments). Actions are verbs (Create order, Release stock).

---

# Icons · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/icons/

> The icons of Sonar-DB: the marks the components draw themselves, the Material Symbols the product uses, their sizes, weight and how to import them.

## Icons

Two families, one look. The components draw a handful of marks themselves, so they need nothing else to work; everything else is a Material Symbol, Rounded, weight 400, passed in by the product. Both take the color of the text beside them.

### Marks the components draw

Drawn on a 16 px grid with a 1.75 px round stroke, in currentColor. They are part of the components, not an icon set to pick from: a product never imports them.

### Product icons

Material Symbols, Rounded, weight 400, grade 0, at the optical size of 24. Outlined by default; filled (the -fill variant) only to show a state: in stock, a quick action, a call in progress. The chevrons that step through days and months are weight 500, so they read as bold beside 12 px labels. These are the 62 icons the overview and its panels use, with their Material names.

### Sizes

    16 px `size.icon.small` Inside small controls and text: the unit menu, fields, status lines, the stock line of a product

    20 px `size.icon.medium` Buttons, icon buttons, menu items, search results

    24 px `—` Navigation, the card header’s bolt, the empty state of a calendar day (28)

The two icon tokens, size.icon.small (16 px) and size.icon.medium (20 px), are the boxes the components give an icon; the icon fills its box. On touch screens icons keep their size and the control around them grows to the 48 px target.

### Weight and color

- **One weight.** Symbols at 400 match the 1.75 px stroke of the marks at 16 px and the medium weight of labels. Never mix weights in one screen.
- **The color of the text.** Icons are drawn in currentColor, so they follow the text level, the theme and the disabled state with no extra token.
- **Color says nothing alone.** A red icon always comes with words: a status, an alert with its name.

### Use

- **Decorative by default.** An icon beside a label is hidden from assistive technology; the label names the action.
- **Icon-only buttons have a name.** IconButton requires a label, read by screen readers; pair it with a tooltip where there is room to hover.
- **One meaning per icon.** The truck is a delivery everywhere; the receipt, an invoice. A new meaning takes a new icon.
- **Icons support words, not replace them,** except for the few actions everyone knows: close, search, add, more.

### Import them

Components take any icon as a React node, so the product chooses how to load them. This is how this site does it, with no icon font and no runtime download: only the icons used end up in the bundle.

 tsx

```
/* 1. Install the symbols: one SVG per icon, weight 400, outlined, rounded or sharp, each with a -fill variant */
npm install @material-symbols/svg-400 @material-symbols/svg-500

/* 2. Make a component from the SVG’s path. With Vite, ?raw reads the file as text at build time */
import truck from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/local_shipping.svg?raw'

const path = truck.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]

export const ShippingIcon = (props) => (
  <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
    <path d={path} />
  </svg>
)

/* 3. Pass it to a component: the component sizes it and the label names the action */
<IconButton label="Track delivery" icon={<ShippingIcon />} />
<Button icon={<AddIcon />}>New order</Button>
```

---

# Spacing · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/spacing/

> The Sonar-DB spacing scale: fourteen steps on a 2 px base, and where each one is used.

## Spacing

Fourteen steps on a 2 px base. The scale is fine at the small end, where figures, units and status dots need exact distances, and opens up for layout.

### Scale

Steps are named by their value in pixels, so `--sonar-space-12` is 12 px wherever you read it. Use the closest step; if none fits, the design probably needs a different structure, not a new number.

1. 2 `--sonar-space-2`
2. 4 `--sonar-space-4`
3. 6 `--sonar-space-6` Icon to label, status dot to its text. The most common gap inside rows.
4. 8 `--sonar-space-8`
5. 10 `--sonar-space-10`
6. 12 `--sonar-space-12` Between related controls in a row.
7. 14 `--sonar-space-14`
8. 16 `--sonar-space-16`
9. 20 `--sonar-space-20` Between cards: the layout gap.
10. 24 `--sonar-space-24`
11. 28 `--sonar-space-28` Card padding, left and right, at every size.
12. 32 `--sonar-space-32` Page margin on desktop.
13. 40 `--sonar-space-40`
14. 48 `--sonar-space-48` Minimum touch target on tablets and phones.

### Cards on the grid

Cards keep 28 px of side padding at every size and sit 20 px apart, in columns and in rows. Content inside a card aligns to the padding, so titles, rules and figures line up from card to card.

*Figure: Two cards, each with 28 px side padding, separated by a 20 px gap.*

---

# Shape · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/shape/

> The Material 3 Expressive corner scale as used in Sonar-DB, and which components take each corner.

## Shape

The corner scale of Material 3 Expressive. Corners grow with the container: a chip is barely rounded, a side panel is generously so, and pills and dots are fully round.

### Corner scale

- #### none

0 px
 `--sonar-shape-corner-none`
- #### extra-small

4 px

Tooltips, small marks.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-extra-small`
- #### small

8 px

Chips, pressed buttons.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-small`
- #### medium

12 px

Cards, fields, menu items.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-medium`
- #### large

16 px

Menus, banners, buttons.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-large`
- #### large-increased

20 px

The step between large and extra-large in the Material 3 scale. No component uses it yet.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-large-increased`
- #### extra-large

28 px

Side panels, search field.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-extra-large`
- #### full

Full

Pills, avatars, status dots.
 `--sonar-shape-corner-full`

### Guidelines

- Nested shapes take a smaller corner than their container, so the curves stay parallel.
- A pressed button changes shape instead of shrinking: its corner goes from large to small, the Material 3 Expressive way of acknowledging a tap.
- Only edges that float get rounded. A sheet attached to the bottom of the screen is rounded on top only.

---

# Elevation · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/elevation/

> The four Sonar-DB elevation levels, the edges of panels, sheets and bars, and where each is used, in light and dark.

## Elevation

Four levels, as in Material 3, for things that sit above the page, plus the edges of panels and sheets. Shadows carry the depth; in dark they are stronger, and side panels gain a hairline edge.

### Levels

Each level is two shadows: a tight one that defines the edge and a soft one that sets the distance. Light shadows are tinted with the darkest neutral, so they stay green-gray rather than dirty; dark shadows are pure black.

### Edges

Panels, sheets and bars cast their shadow toward the page they cover. In light the shadow alone separates them; in dark a shadow barely shows, so the side panel, the top bar, the sidebar and the Edit layout bar draw a 1 px edge in a darker neutral instead of, or as well as, the shadow.

### Where each is used

| Token | Used by | In the system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `elevation.1` | Cards of the overview, tables and demo frames of this site | Card |
| `elevation.2` | Menus, the search results, the controls of the route map, the Edit layout bar | Menu, SearchField |
| `elevation.3` | Dialogs and toasts | Dialog, Toast |
| `elevation.4` | A card while it is dragged; it settles back to 1 when dropped, over its drop placeholder | Editing the overview |
| `elevation.panel` | Side panels: delivery and invoice details, New order, Reorder | Dialog (end) |
| `elevation.sheet` | Sheets that hang from the top bar | All modules |
| `elevation.sheet-up` | Bottom sheets and the navigation drawer on phones | Dialog (bottom) |
| `elevation.top-bar` | The top bar over the scrolling page | App shell |
| `elevation.sidebar` | The sidebar’s edge: nothing in light, a hairline in dark | App shell |
| `elevation.edit-bar` | The bar at the foot of Edit layout: level 2 in light, a hairline in dark | Editing the overview |

### Tokens

*Elevation tokens*

| Token | Preview | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-elevation-1`  Cards. |  | `0 1px 2px 0 #171D16 6.4% 0 1px 8px 2px #171D16 4%` | `0 1px 2px 0 #000000 28.2% 0 1px 8px 2px #000000 17.6%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-2`  Menus and map controls. |  | `0 1px 2px 0 #171D16 12.8% 0 2px 6px 2px #171D16 8%` | `0 1px 2px 0 #000000 56.3% 0 2px 6px 2px #000000 35.2%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-3`  Dialogs and toasts. |  | `0 1px 2px 0 #171D16 16% 0 4px 8px 2px #171D16 10%` | `0 1px 2px 0 #000000 70.4% 0 4px 8px 2px #000000 44%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-4`  A card lifted while it is dragged. |  | `0 1px 2px 0 #171D16 19.2% 0 6px 10px 4px #171D16 12%` | `0 1px 2px 0 #000000 84.5% 0 6px 10px 4px #000000 52.8%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-panel`  Side panels entering from the end. |  | `-6px 0 18px -7px #171D16 20%` | `inset 0 1px 0 0 #1B211B -1px 0 0 0 #1B211B -16px 0 36px -14px #000000 75%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-sheet`  Sheets that hang from the top bar, such as Customize overview: a short shadow below the sheet only. Restored in 1.0.0-alpha.14. |  | `0 8px 18px -7px #171D16 20%` | `0 8px 18px -7px #000000 70%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-sheet-up`  Bottom sheets and the navigation drawer on phones. |  | `0 -12px 32px -8px #000000 25%` | `0 -12px 32px -8px #000000 25%` |
| `--sonar-elevation-top-bar`  The top bar over the page: a faint shadow under it. |  | `0 2px 8px 0 #000000 3.5%` | `0 1px 0 0 #1B211B` |
| `--sonar-elevation-sidebar`  The edge of the sidebar against the page: none in light, where the surfaces already differ. |  | `none` | `1px 0 0 0 #171D17` |
| `--sonar-elevation-edit-bar`  The bar of Edit layout at the foot of the window: level 2. |  | `0 1px 2px 0 #171D16 12.8% 0 2px 6px 2px #171D16 8%` | `0 -1px 0 0 #1B211B` |

### Guidelines

- Elevation follows behavior, not importance: a card is level 1 whatever it contains.
- A card being dragged lifts to level 4 and settles back to level 1 when dropped.
- In the dark theme a shadow alone is hard to see, so side panels and bars also draw a 1 px edge.
- A menu or a list opened from something keeps one level above it: menus at 2 over cards at 1, dialogs at 3.
- Never add a shadow to show state (hover, selection): elevation changes only when something lifts, as a dragged card.

---

# Motion · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/foundations/motion/

> Sonar-DB motion: springs defined by duration and bounce, generated as CSS easing curves, and when to use each.

## Motion

Short, decelerating, and without bounce by default. The interface is a working tool: motion explains what changed and gets out of the way. A small bounce is kept for two moments that deserve it.

### Springs

Springs are described as designers talk about them: a **duration**, the time the spring takes to settle within 0.2% of its target, and a **bounce**. The build turns each pair into a CSS `linear()` curve, so the motion runs like any transition, with no JavaScript.

**Spatial** springs move things: position, size, shape. **Effects** springs change how things look: opacity and color. Effects are quicker, because a fade that lags reads as slowness.

#### `sonar-motion-spatial-fast`

200 ms, bounce 0

Small elements: switches, chips, menus.

#### `sonar-motion-spatial-default`

320 ms, bounce 0

Most layout changes: accordions, cards settling, panels resizing.

#### `sonar-motion-spatial-expressive`

500 ms, bounce 0.3

Only when a dragged card is dropped and for success confirmations.

#### `sonar-motion-effects-fast`

138 ms, bounce 0

#### `sonar-motion-effects-default`

212 ms, bounce 0

#### `sonar-motion-effects-slow`

300 ms, bounce 0

### Easing curves

Cubic curves for what is not a spring: leaving the screen, entering panels, the sidebar folding, the theme switch and cards changing columns.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-exit`

400 ms

Leaving the screen: starts at once and accelerates.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-decelerate`

400 ms

Entering elements that are not springs, such as panels.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-standard`

400 ms

Continuous transforms such as the sidebar folding.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-accelerate`

400 ms

Panels and sheets leaving: starts slow and leaves at speed.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-emphasized`

400 ms

The theme switch’s knob and cards moving between columns.

#### `sonar-motion-easing-crossfade`

400 ms

The page cross-fading from one theme to the other.

### Durations

Fixed durations for the moments that are not a spring. Each is used with the easing named beside it in the guidelines below.

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-state` | `160ms` | Hover and pressed colors of rows, pills and buttons, with easing.decelerate. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-panel-enter` | `420ms` | A side panel or a phone sheet arriving: its slide uses the spatial default spring stretched to this time. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-panel-exit` | `150ms` | A side panel leaving: 28 px and out of sight, with easing.accelerate. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-sheet-fade` | `200ms` | A phone sheet’s opacity while it rises. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-sheet-exit` | `220ms` | A phone sheet going down, with easing.accelerate. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-menu-exit` | `110ms` | A menu closing to 96 %, with easing.exit. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-dropdown` | `180ms` | The search results opening, with easing.decelerate. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-tooltip-delay` | `300ms` | The pointer rests this long before a tooltip opens. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-tooltip-enter` | `140ms` | A tooltip opening from 96 %, with easing.decelerate. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-tooltip-exit` | `90ms` | A tooltip fading out, with easing.exit. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-theme` | `700ms` | The cross-fade of the whole page when the theme changes, with easing.crossfade. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-theme-fallback` | `250ms` | Color transitions when a browser cannot cross-fade the page. |
| `--sonar-motion-duration-reflow` | `620ms` | Cards moving to new places when the number of columns changes, with easing.emphasized. |

### Theme switch

Changing the theme is two steps. The switch’s knob slides first, in 200 ms on `--sonar-motion-easing-emphasized`. At 200 ms the whole page cross-fades into the new theme with a View Transition: 700 ms on `--sonar-motion-easing-crossfade`. Nothing changes color out of step, because the page fades as one picture.

Browsers without View Transitions ease every color over 250 ms instead. With reduced motion requested, the theme changes at once.

 css

```
::view-transition-old(root),
::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation-duration: var(--sonar-motion-duration-theme);          /* 700ms */
  animation-timing-function: var(--sonar-motion-easing-crossfade); /* cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) */
}

/* Without View Transitions: colors ease */
.sonar-theming, .sonar-theming * {
  transition: color var(--sonar-motion-duration-theme-fallback) ease,
              background-color var(--sonar-motion-duration-theme-fallback) ease !important;
}
```

 js

```
function switchTheme(next) {
  const apply = () => (document.documentElement.dataset.theme = next)
  if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return apply()
  if (document.startViewTransition) {
    // the knob slides first (200 ms), then the page cross-fades
    return setTimeout(() => document.startViewTransition(apply), 200)
  }
  document.documentElement.classList.add('sonar-theming')
  apply()
  setTimeout(() => document.documentElement.classList.remove('sonar-theming'), 300)
}
```

### In code

Every spring is two custom properties, a duration and an easing, always used together.

 css

```
.accordion-panel {
  transition: height var(--sonar-motion-spatial-default-duration)
                     var(--sonar-motion-spatial-default-easing);
}

.menu {
  transition: opacity var(--sonar-motion-effects-fast-duration)
                      var(--sonar-motion-effects-fast-easing);
}
```

### Guidelines

- Bounce only when a dragged card lands in its slot and when an action succeeds. Everywhere else, motion settles without overshoot.
- Side panels enter from 48 px in 420 ms with a fade, and leave by 28 px in 150 ms on the accelerate curve. On tablets the panel slides all the way in from the right edge on the default spatial spring (320 ms) and back out the same way, as [Navigation by device](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/navigation/#tablets) shows. On phones the sheet rises in 420 ms (fade 200 ms) and drops in 220 ms.
- Menus open from 0.9 in 200 ms with a 138 ms fade, and close to 0.96 in 110 ms on `cubic-bezier(.3,0,.8,.15)`. The search list drops 4 px from 0.98 in 180 ms.
- Tooltips wait 300 ms, then grow from 0.96 in 140 ms; they leave with a 90 ms fade. The chart bubble only fades, in 200 ms.
- Hover and other state changes take 160 ms on `cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)`.
- Editing the overview: a lifted card grows to 1.03 (200 ms) and rises to elevation 4; its height follows in 320 ms. Dropped, it settles in 500 ms on the expressive spring. Neighbors and resizes move in 320 ms. When the column count changes, cards travel to their new places in 620 ms on `cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)`.
- Theme changes never move content: only the switch’s knob slides, then the page fades.
- With reduced motion requested, spatial movement is replaced by an immediate change; fades stay, shortened, to keep the change perceptible.

---

# Layout · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/

> Window size classes, the grid of the overview, and how navigation changes from phone to desktop.

## Layout

Window size classes, the grid of the overview, and how navigation changes from phone to desktop.

- ### [Breakpoints and grid](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/grid/)

Five size classes, their columns, gaps and margins, with a simulator for any width.
- ### [Navigation by device](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/navigation/)

A bottom bar on phones, a rail on tablets and a sidebar that collapses on desktops.

---

# Breakpoints and grid · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/grid/

> Sonar-DB window size classes, the overview grid, card heights and how one desktop layout is derived for every width.

## Breakpoints and grid

Five size classes and one grid. The window decides how many columns there are; the cards are arranged once, for the desktop, and every other width is derived from that arrangement.

### Size classes

The classes follow Material 3, with thresholds set by the cards: a card should never be narrower than a phone or wider than about 575 px, where a row of figures stops reading as one line. When a column would grow past that, the grid gains a column, up to five: on the widest monitors, cards reach 614 px.

*Size classes and their grid*

| Size class | Window | Columns | Navigation | Margins | Card width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `compact` Phones | 360–767 px | 1 | Bottom bar | 16 px | 328–735 px |
| `medium` Tablets | 768–1279 px | 2 | Rail | 24 px | 320–575 px |
| `expanded` Desktops | 1280–2047 px | 3 | Sidebar | 32 px | 317–573 px |
| `large` Wide monitors | 2048–2649 px | 4 | Sidebar | 32 px | 425–575 px |
| `extra-large` Ultra-wide monitors | 2650 px and wider | 5 | Sidebar | 32 px | 456–614 px |

Card widths with the sidebar open. Collapsing it to the rail gives the columns its width.

### The grid at any width

*Figure: Cards are numbered in the reading order of the desktop layout. With any other number of columns, each card goes, in that order, into the shortest column.*

### Column width

Columns are fluid: they share whatever the navigation and the margins leave, rounded down to whole pixels so card edges stay sharp. Collapsing the sidebar on a 1440 px desktop widens every column from 370 to 425 px; the cards follow with the same spring as the sidebar.

 text

```
column = ⌊(window − navigation − 2 × margin
           − (columns − 1) × gap) ÷ columns⌋

1440 px desktop, sidebar open:
⌊(1440 − 224 − 2 × 32 − 2 × 20) ÷ 3⌋ = 370 px
```

### Card heights

Cards come in four heights. Width is the column’s; a card never spans two. The heights are chosen so that **M + L = S + XL**: two columns built from different sizes end level, and the overview keeps a straight bottom edge as people rearrange it.

*Figure: 375 + 20 + 405 = 245 + 20 + 535 = 800 px*

### One layout, derived

- **The desktop layout is the one people design.** They choose each card’s column, position and size on a three-column desktop.
- **Every other width reads it in order.** Cards are taken by how far down they start, and left to right when two start level. Each goes into the shortest column. One column on phones keeps the same order, so the first card on a desktop is the first card on a phone.
- **A layout edited at another width is kept for that width.** Rearranging cards on a tablet stores a tablet layout; until then, the tablet follows the desktop. What is shown is shared: hiding a card hides it everywhere.

On a tablet, the six cards of the default overview land as  Orders, Balance, Recurring orders  and Daily shipments, Deliveries, Inventory  .

### In code

Media queries cannot read custom properties, so the token build writes the breakpoints into them. Three properties follow the size class on their own:  `--sonar-layout-columns`  , `--sonar-layout-margin`  and `--sonar-layout-bar-top`  . Components read those, never a breakpoint.

 css

```
/* The overview grid: columns, gap and margins follow the size class */
.overview {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--sonar-layout-columns), minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: var(--sonar-layout-gap);
  padding-inline: var(--sonar-layout-margin);
}

.top-app-bar {
  block-size: calc(var(--sonar-layout-bar-top) + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px));
  padding-block-start: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
}
```

For scripts, the package exports each size class with a media query for exactly its range.

 ts

```
import { sizeClasses } from '@orbex/sonar-tokens'

/* The current size class, kept up to date as the window changes */
const current = () => sizeClasses.find(({ media }) => matchMedia(media).matches)!.name
```

### Safe areas

On phones and tablets in full screen, the system draws its status bar and home indicator over the page. The app bars grow by `env(safe-area-inset-*)` so their background reaches the edge, and the content starts below them. In a browser tab the insets are zero and nothing changes.

### Tokens

*Layout tokens*

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--sonar-layout-columns-compact` | `1` |
| `--sonar-layout-columns-medium` | `2` |
| `--sonar-layout-columns-expanded` | `3` |
| `--sonar-layout-columns-large` | `4` |
| `--sonar-layout-columns-extra-large` | `5` |
| `--sonar-layout-margin-compact` | `16px` |
| `--sonar-layout-margin-medium` | `24px` |
| `--sonar-layout-margin-expanded` | `32px` |
| `--sonar-layout-gap`  Between cards, in every size class. | `20px` |
| `--sonar-layout-sidebar`  Full navigation beside the content on desktops. On tablets it opens over the content. | `224px` |
| `--sonar-layout-rail`  Navigation as icons only: the rail on tablets and the collapsed sidebar on desktops. | `60px` |
| `--sonar-layout-drawer`  The sidebar as a drawer on phones. It never covers more than 84% of the window. | `304px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-top-compact` | `56px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-top-medium` | `68px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-bottom`  Bottom app bar on phones: Alerts, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu. | `60px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-footer`  Footer and edit bar on tablets and desktops. | `46px` |
| `--sonar-layout-card-s` | `245px` |
| `--sonar-layout-card-m` | `375px` |
| `--sonar-layout-card-l` | `405px` |
| `--sonar-layout-card-xl` | `535px` |
| `--sonar-layout-touch-target`  Minimum hit area on touch screens. | `48px` |

---

# Navigation by device · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/navigation/

> Where Sonar-DB navigation and panels live on phones, tablets and desktops, and how they behave.

## Navigation by device

The same destinations in every size class, placed where the hand or the pointer already is: a bottom bar on phones, a rail on tablets, a sidebar on desktops. Panels follow the same logic.

### Phones

*Figure: Compact, 390 × 844 Open the menu Open details*

- **Bottom app bar**, 60 px plus the safe area: What’s new, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu, at the end. What’s new carries the count of new notices; a red dot on Menu says something inside it needs a look.
- **Menu opens the whole sidebar as a drawer** from the left, 304 px wide and never more than 84% of the window, over a scrim. Choosing a destination or touching the scrim closes it.
- **Panels are bottom sheets** with a handle, from under the top bar: details, new orders, notifications and the assistant. There is no scrim. They close by swiping down from the handle or the header, with the close button, or with Escape.
- **The top bar is compact**, 56 px: the brand, All accounts and search. Search opens across the whole bar, with Cancel. The page title moves to a header at the top of the page.

### Tablets

*Figure: Medium, 834 × 1194 Expand the rail Open details*

- **A rail**, 60 px, always in place: icons only, with the destination’s name on touch and hold.
- **Expanding the rail opens the full sidebar over the content**, with a scrim. The columns do not move. Choosing a destination or touching the scrim folds it back.
- **Panels are side sheets** from the right, 402 px, under the top bar and with no scrim: the overview stays in view and the row they came from stays marked. They slide in from the right edge, all the way, on the default spatial spring, and slide back out the same way. They fit from 768 px up, so tablets and desktops share them. All six are in [Patterns › Panels](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/panels/).
- **The top bar keeps one line.** Search gives up width first, down to 150 px, and its results open toward the left at no less than 320 px.

### Desktops

*Figure: Expanded, 1440 × 900. Large and extra-large work the same way, with more columns. Collapse the sidebar Open details*

- **The sidebar sits beside the content**, 224 px, with labels and account details.
- **Collapsing it leaves the rail**, 60 px, and gives its width to the columns: every card widens, and the cards move with the same spring as the sidebar. The choice is remembered.
- **Panels are side sheets** from the right, under the top bar and with no scrim, as on tablets.

### Changing size class

- **Navigation changes place at once.** When the window crosses a breakpoint, the sidebar becomes a rail or a bottom bar without animating: motion between two layouts that never coexist explains nothing.
- **Each class starts from its resting state.** The tablet rail is folded, the phone drawer closed, and a layout edit in progress ends without saving.
- **One mechanism decides the class:** the breakpoints in the tokens, through CSS media queries or `sizeClasses` in scripts. Nothing measures the window on its own.

### Touch

- Every target is at least 48 px on touch screens, even where the visible control is smaller: the hit area grows, the drawing does not.
- Nothing depends on hover. On screens without it (`hover: none`), tooltips open on touch and the hover highlight does not stick after a tap.
- Drag handles get a larger hit area, and the handles of two neighboring cards share the gap between them so they never overlap.

### Tokens

*Navigation tokens*

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--sonar-layout-sidebar`  Full navigation beside the content on desktops. On tablets it opens over the content. | `224px` |
| `--sonar-layout-rail`  Navigation as icons only: the rail on tablets and the collapsed sidebar on desktops. | `60px` |
| `--sonar-layout-drawer`  The sidebar as a drawer on phones. It never covers more than 84% of the window. | `304px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-top-compact` | `56px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-top-medium` | `68px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-bottom`  Bottom app bar on phones: Alerts, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu. | `60px` |
| `--sonar-layout-bar-footer`  Footer and edit bar on tablets and desktops. | `46px` |
| `--sonar-layout-touch-target`  Minimum hit area on touch screens. | `48px` |

---

# Components · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/

> The React components of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: how they are built, installed and tested.

## Components

React components built on native HTML wherever the platform already does the job, and on Base UI where it does not. They are styled only with the tokens, ship one entry point each, and are tested for behavior and accessibility on every build.

### All components

- #### [Button](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/button/)

The action a screen or a card exists for, in four weights and two sizes.

Native HTML · 1.8 KB
- #### [Icon button](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/icon-button/)

A round button that shows only an icon, with a name for screen readers.

Native HTML · 1.5 KB
- #### [Badge](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/badge/)

A small count or dot on a navigation item, an icon button or a tab.

Native HTML · 1.1 KB
- #### [Status](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/status/)

The state of an order, a delivery or an invoice, as a dot or a chip.

Native HTML · 1.1 KB
- #### [Switch](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/switch/)

Turns a setting on or off at once. It works in forms and without JavaScript.

Native HTML · 1.7 KB
- #### [Checkbox](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/checkbox/)

A choice that is confirmed later, alone or in a list where all can be selected at once.

Native HTML · 1.8 KB
- #### [Segmented control](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/segmented-control/)

A choice of one among a few options, shown side by side.

Native HTML · 1.9 KB
- #### [Text field and select](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/field/)

Text fields and selects, each with its label, help and error.

Native HTML · 2.2 KB
- #### [Notice](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/notice/)

A message inside the page that stays until the situation changes.

Native HTML · 1.3 KB
- #### [Toast](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/toast/)

Short feedback on something that just happened, with an undo when it helps.

Base UI · 2.4 KB
- #### [Menu](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/menu/)

A list of actions or choices that opens from a button.

Base UI · 2.0 KB
- #### [Tooltip](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tooltip/)

A short label shown on hover and focus, mostly for icon buttons.

Base UI · 1.2 KB
- #### [Dialog](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/dialog/)

A window that asks for a decision, or a side panel or a bottom sheet.

Native HTML · 9.0 KB
- #### [Scroll area](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/scroll-area/)

Content that scrolls inside a fixed height, with a thin indicator instead of a scrollbar.

Native HTML · 2.0 KB
- #### [Card](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card/)

The unit of the overview: a title, a summary figure, content and a way to the full page.

Native HTML · 4.8 KB with Card link, Card scroll, Unit menu
- #### [Card link](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-link/)

The link at the foot of a card to the page it summarizes.

Native HTML · 4.8 KB with Card, Card scroll, Unit menu
- #### [Card scroll](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-scroll/)

The list in a card that scrolls first when the card’s size leaves no room.

Native HTML · 4.8 KB with Card, Card link, Unit menu
- #### [Unit menu](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/unit-menu/)

The unit a card’s figures are shown in, as a pill that opens a menu.

Native HTML · 4.8 KB with Card, Card link, Card scroll
- #### [Tick bar](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tick-bar/)

A share of a whole as a row of fine ticks.

Native HTML · 1.3 KB
- #### [Ring chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/ring-chart/)

Parts of a whole as a ring of ticks.

Native HTML · 1.4 KB
- #### [Trend chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/trend-chart/)

A daily series as a line, with its running total.

Native HTML · 4.2 KB
- #### [Chart legend](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/chart-legend/)

The key to a chart’s colors.

Native HTML · 0.9 KB
- #### [Search field](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-field/)

A search box whose results open under it as people type.

Base UI · 4.2 KB with Search result
- #### [Search result](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-result/)

One row of results: an icon, a title, a line under it and a status.

Base UI · 4.2 KB with Search field

How they come together in the overview, its cards, charts and search, is in [Patterns](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/).

### How they are built

- **Native HTML first.** Buttons, switches, checkboxes, radios, fields, selects and dialogs are the browser’s own elements. They work before any script loads, in forms, with every assistive technology, and they cost almost nothing to ship.
- **Base UI for complex behavior.** Menus and tooltips need positioning, focus management and typeahead the platform does not offer everywhere yet. Base UI, maintained full-time by the MUI team, provides that behavior unstyled.
- **Plain CSS on tokens.** Each component has one stylesheet in the `sonar.components` cascade layer. Variants are data attributes; values are tokens only. No CSS-in-JS, no utility framework, and an app’s own styles always win without `!important`.
- **One entry point per component.** An app imports `@orbex/sonar-components/button` and its stylesheet and loads nothing else. All 24 weigh 47.8 KB gzipped together, script and styles.

### Install

Installing the packages, setting the cascade layers and importing the tokens are on one page: [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/). Each component page ends with its own import and its API; the props of every component are also published as data at [/api.json](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/api.json).

### Quality gates

- **Types:** strict TypeScript, and the declarations ship with the package.
- **Behavior:** every component is tested in a DOM with Testing Library: roles, names, keyboard and state.
- **Accessibility:** axe runs on every rendered component in the tests; contrast is enforced on the tokens, where it is decided.
- **Weight:** the build fails when a component’s script and styles pass 3 KB gzipped. Two entry points have a larger budget, named in the build with its reason: the trend chart and the card (Card, Card link, Card scroll and Unit menu), at 4 KB.
- **Versions:** tokens and components are released together with Changesets, so one version names one consistent system.

---

# Button · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/button/

> Button, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Button

A native button in four weights. Fully round at rest and squarer while pressed, as in Material 3 Expressive; small and steady in size, because the dashboard is dense.

- Native HTML
- 1.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/button`

### Examples

*Figure: Variants*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'

export default function Variants() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button>Place order</Button>
      <Button variant="tonal">Reorder</Button>
      <Button variant="outlined">Export</Button>
      <Button variant="text">View all</Button>
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Sizes and icons*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import addSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/add.svg?raw'
import downloadSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/download.svg?raw'
import expandSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/keyboard_arrow_down.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const AddIcon = symbol(addSymbol)
const DownloadIcon = symbol(downloadSymbol)
const ExpandIcon = symbol(expandSymbol)

export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button icon={<AddIcon />}>New order</Button>
      <Button variant="outlined" iconEnd={<ExpandIcon />}>
        All accounts
      </Button>
      <Button size="small" variant="tonal" icon={<DownloadIcon />}>
        Invoice
      </Button>
      <Button size="small" variant="outlined">
        Details
      </Button>
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Disabled*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'

export default function Disabled() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button disabled>Place order</Button>
      <Button variant="tonal" disabled>
        Reorder
      </Button>
      <Button variant="outlined" disabled>
        Export
      </Button>
      <Button variant="text" disabled>
        View all
      </Button>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: States*

*Figure: Sizes and icons*

### Usage

- **One filled button per view**, for the action the view exists for: Place order, Save layout.
- **Tonal** for frequent secondary actions; **outlined** for the rest; **text** for actions inside a card or a list, such as View all.
- Medium in forms, panels and dialogs; small in cards and toolbars. Labels are verbs, in sentence case.
- For navigation, use a link with the same look: `<a class="sonar-button" data-variant="text" data-size="medium">`. A button that only navigates confuses screen readers and breaks opening in a new tab.
- Prefer leaving an action enabled and explaining what is missing when it is used. A disabled button cannot say why.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoOne filled button per area, for the action the area exists for. The others step down to outlined or text.*

*Figure: Don’tTwo filled buttons side by side: neither reads as the next step.*

*Figure: DoName the action with a verb and its object, so the button reads on its own.*

*Figure: Don’tVague labels that need the rest of the screen to make sense.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the control, and on. |
| Enter or Space | Activates it. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<button type="button">` | A native button: role, name and states come from the browser. It never submits a form unless asked to. |
| `disabled` | Removes it from the tab order and tells assistive technology it is unavailable. |
| Icons | aria-hidden: the label alone names the action. |

#### Notes

- A native `<button>` with `type="button"` by default, so it never submits a form by accident.
- Icons are hidden from assistive technology; the label names the action.
- The focus ring is drawn outside the button in `color.focus`, at 3:1 or more on every surface.
- On touch screens the hit area grows to 48 px around the button without changing how it looks.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/button.css'
```

### API

*Props of Button*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant`  Visual weight. Filled for the one main action of a view, tonal for secondary actions, outlined and text for the rest. | `'filled' \| 'tonal' \| 'outlined' \| 'text'` | `'filled'` |
| `size`  Medium in forms, panels and dialogs; small in cards and toolbars. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |
| `icon`  Icon before the label. It is decorative: the label names the action. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `iconEnd`  Icon after the label, such as a chevron on a button that opens a menu. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<button>` , and a `ref` to it.

---

# Icon button · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/icon-button/

> Icon button, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Icon button

A round button with one icon, for actions people recognize at a glance: notifications, search, more actions. Its name is required, because nothing else on screen says it.

- Native HTML
- 1.5 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button`

### Examples

*Figure: Variants and sizes*

```
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import addSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/add.svg?raw'
import editSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/edit.svg?raw'
import filterSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/filter_list.svg?raw'
import moreSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/more_vert.svg?raw'
import notificationsSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/notifications.svg?raw'
import searchSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/search.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const AddIcon = symbol(addSymbol)
const EditIcon = symbol(editSymbol)
const FilterIcon = symbol(filterSymbol)
const MoreIcon = symbol(moreSymbol)
const NotificationsIcon = symbol(notificationsSymbol)
const SearchIcon = symbol(searchSymbol)

export default function Variants() {
  return (
    <>
      <IconButton label="Notifications" icon={<NotificationsIcon />} />
      <IconButton label="Search" icon={<SearchIcon />} variant="outlined" />
      <IconButton label="Edit layout" icon={<EditIcon />} variant="tonal" />
      <IconButton label="New order" icon={<AddIcon />} variant="filled" />
      <IconButton label="Filter" icon={<FilterIcon />} size="small" />
      <IconButton label="More actions" icon={<MoreIcon />} size="small" variant="tonal" />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Variants, states and sizes*

### Usage

- **Standard** in bars and on cards; the other weights follow Button.
- Give it a Tooltip with the same words as its label, so sighted people can learn it too.
- When an icon could mean several things, use a Button with a label instead.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoIcon buttons for familiar actions in toolbars and card headers, standard by default.*

*Figure: Don’tA row of filled icon buttons: every one shouts, and none is the main action.*

*Figure: DoA rare or abstract action gets words: a button with a label says what it does.*

*Figure: Don’tAn icon nobody can guess, even with a tooltip to read first.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the control, and on. |
| Enter or Space | Activates it. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | From the required label prop: the button’s name, since it shows no text. |
| Icon | aria-hidden. |

#### Notes

- `label` is required and becomes the button’s accessible name.
- The icon is hidden from assistive technology.
- On touch screens the hit area grows to 48 px.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button.css'
```

### API

*Props of IconButton*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What the button does, read by assistive technology. Pair the button with a Tooltip to show it on hover. | `string` | — |
| `icon` Required  The icon. Decorative: the label names the action. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `variant`  Standard sits on any surface with no fill; the others follow the weights of Button. | `'standard' \| 'filled' \| 'tonal' \| 'outlined'` | `'standard'` |
| `size`  Medium is a 40 px button; small is 32 px, for card headers and dense rows. Both keep a 48 px touch target. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<button>` , except children, and a `ref` to it.

---

# Badge · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/badge/

> Badge, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Badge

A count or a dot on a navigation item or an icon button. Figures are set in the mono face, as everywhere numbers are compared.

- Native HTML
- 1.1 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/badge`

### Examples

*Figure: Count, dot and tones*

```
import { Badge } from '@orbex/sonar-components/badge'
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import notificationsSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/notifications.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const NotificationsIcon = symbol(notificationsSymbol)

/* A badge sits in the flow or is placed by its container; it does not position itself.
   When the element it sits on already says what it counts, the badge is hidden from assistive technology. */
export default function Examples() {
  return (
    <>
      <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, font: 'var(--sonar-type-label-lg)' }}>
        Payments <Badge count={3} label="3 unpaid invoices" />
      </span>
      <span style={{ position: 'relative', display: 'inline-flex' }}>
        <IconButton label="Notifications, 12 unread" icon={<NotificationsIcon />} />
        <Badge count={12} aria-hidden style={{ position: 'absolute', top: -2, right: -4 }} />
      </span>
      <span style={{ position: 'relative', display: 'inline-flex' }}>
        <IconButton label="Notifications, new" icon={<NotificationsIcon />} />
        <Badge aria-hidden style={{ position: 'absolute', top: 7, right: 8 }} />
      </span>
      <Badge count={128} tone="accent" label="128 new documents" />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Forms and tones*

### Usage

- **Danger** for what needs attention, such as unpaid invoices; **accent** for news.
- A dot says that something is new; a count says how much. Counts above 99 show as 99+.
- The badge does not position itself: its container places it, so it fits any shape it sits on.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA count on the thing it counts, with its meaning in the label: “12 unread”.*

*Figure: Don’tWords in a badge. A badge holds a number or a dot; a message goes in a notice.*

*Figure: DoCap large counts: 99+ says “a lot” and keeps its size.*

*Figure: Don’tA four-digit badge that outgrows what it sits on.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | A badge is not interactive; the element it sits on takes focus. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | A visually hidden phrase read instead of the bare number: “3 unpaid invoices”. |
| `aria-hidden` | For a badge whose meaning is already in its container’s name, such as an icon button named “Notifications, 12 unread”. |

#### Notes

- Give it a `label` that says what it counts; the bare number is then hidden from assistive technology.
- When the element it sits on already says it, as an icon button named “Notifications, 12 unread”, hide the badge with `aria-hidden`.
- White on the danger fill reaches 4.5:1 in both themes.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Badge } from '@orbex/sonar-components/badge'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/badge.css'
```

### API

*Props of Badge*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count`  The number to show. Without it, the badge is a dot that only signals something new. | `number` | — |
| `max`  Counts above this show as `99+`. | `number` | `99` |
| `label`  What the badge means, read by assistive technology instead of the bare number, such as “3 unpaid invoices”. Leave it out only when the element the badge sits on already says it. | `string` | — |
| `tone`  Danger for things that need attention; accent for news. | `'danger' \| 'accent'` | `'danger'` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<span>` , except children, and a `ref` to it.

# Status · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/status/

> Status, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Status

The state of an order, a delivery or an invoice, in words with a colored mark. The hue sits in the dot and the tint; the text stays at a reading level, so it passes AA anywhere.

- Native HTML
- 1.1 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/status`

### Examples

*Figure: Dots, for rows and lists*

```
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'

export default function Dots() {
  return (
    <>
      <Status tone="positive">Delivered</Status>
      <Status tone="warning">Due today</Status>
      <Status tone="danger">Delayed</Status>
      <Status>Scheduled</Status>
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Chips, for headers and containers*

```
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'

export default function Chips() {
  return (
    <>
      <Status appearance="chip" tone="positive">Paid</Status>
      <Status appearance="chip" tone="warning">On hold</Status>
      <Status appearance="chip" tone="danger">Overdue</Status>
      <Status appearance="chip">Draft</Status>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Tones and appearances*

### Usage

- **Positive**: done, paid, delivered. **Warning**: pending, on hold, due today. **Danger**: delayed, overdue, canceled. **Neutral**: scheduled, draft.
- Use the chip where status text would sit on a container: colored text does not reach 4.5:1 there.
- One word or two. The detail goes in the panel the row opens.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA dot and a word. The word carries the state; the color helps scanning.*

*Figure: Don’tColor alone. Without the word, the state is lost to anyone who cannot tell the hues apart.*

*Figure: DoOne or two words. The detail goes in the panel the row opens.*

*Figure: Don’tA sentence in a status: it wraps, and the list stops scanning.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | Status is text, not a control. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| Text | The state is always written, so it never depends on color. |
| Dot | aria-hidden. |

#### Notes

- Color never carries the state alone: the word always names it.
- The mark is hidden from assistive technology.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/status.css'
```

### API

*Props of Status*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone`  What the state means. Color never carries it alone: the text always names it. | `'neutral' \| 'positive' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` |
| `appearance`  A dot beside the text, for rows and lists; or a chip, for headers and for containers, where colored text would not reach 4.5:1. | `'dot' \| 'chip'` | `'dot'` |
| `hideLabel`  Only the dot shows; the state stays in the text for assistive technology. For dense rows where a tooltip or the row’s details name the state, as in the overview’s calendars. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `children` Required  The state in words: Delivered, Delayed, Due today. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<span>` , and a `ref` to it.

---

# Switch · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/switch/

> Switch, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Switch

The Material 3 switch on a native checkbox. It turns something on at once, such as a card on the overview, and works before any script has loaded.

- Native HTML
- 1.7 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/switch`

### Examples

*Figure: On, off with help, disabled*

```
import { Switch } from '@orbex/sonar-components/switch'

export default function Examples() {
  return (
    <>
      <Switch label="Daily shipments" defaultChecked />
      <Switch label="Compact figures" description="Shows 1.96K instead of 1,960 where space is short." />
      <Switch label="Recurring orders" disabled />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: States*

### Usage

- For settings that apply immediately. For a choice that is submitted later, use Checkbox.
- Name what is turned on, not the action: “Daily shipments”, not “Show daily shipments”.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA switch acts at once: the setting is on as soon as it is turned on.*

*Figure: Don’tSwitches in a form that waits for Save. Choices confirmed later are checkboxes.*

*Figure: DoName the setting in positive words, so on means yes.*

*Figure: Don’tA negative label, where on means no.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the switch. |
| Space | Turns it on or off. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` | Announced as a switch, on or off; still a checkbox in forms and without JavaScript. |
| `<label>` | Wraps the input, so the label names it and clicking the label toggles it. |
| `aria-describedby` | Ties the help text to the input without adding it to the name. |

#### Notes

- A native checkbox with `role="switch"`: announced as a switch, on or off, toggled with Space.
- The help text sits outside the label, so it describes the switch without lengthening its name.
- On touch screens the row grows to 48 px.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Switch } from '@orbex/sonar-components/switch'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/switch.css'
```

### API

*Props of Switch*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What the switch turns on. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  One line on the effect, read after the label. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<input>` , except type | role, and a `ref` to it.

# Checkbox · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/checkbox/

> Checkbox, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Checkbox

A native checkbox, for choices that are submitted with a form or confirmed later. A dash shows that some, not all, of the items it governs are chosen.

- Native HTML
- 1.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox`

### Examples

*Figure: Checked, with help, disabled*

```
import { Checkbox } from '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox'

export default function Examples() {
  return (
    <>
      <Checkbox label="Include delivered" defaultChecked />
      <Checkbox label="Notify the carrier" description="An email with the new delivery window." />
      <Checkbox label="Split by warehouse" disabled />
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Select all*

```
import { Checkbox } from '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox'
import { useState } from 'react'

const deliveries = ['04-127C', '04-128A', '04-131B']

/* The parent checkbox shows a dash while some, not all, rows are chosen */
export default function SelectAll() {
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState<string[]>(['04-127C'])
  const all = chosen.length === deliveries.length
  const toggle = (id: string) => setChosen((ids) => (ids.includes(id) ? ids.filter((other) => other !== id) : [...ids, id]))
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 10 }}>
      <Checkbox
        label="All deliveries"
        checked={all}
        indeterminate={chosen.length > 0 && !all}
        onChange={() => setChosen(all ? [] : deliveries)}
      />
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 10, paddingLeft: 28 }}>
        {deliveries.map((id) => (
          <Checkbox key={id} label={`Delivery ${id}`} checked={chosen.includes(id)} onChange={() => toggle(id)} />
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: States*

### Usage

- Each checkbox is independent. For one choice among several, use a SegmentedControl or a select.
- The indeterminate state is only shown: a click checks the box, and the app decides what that means for its items.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoCheckboxes for choices that are confirmed together, by a button after them.*

*Figure: Don’tA checkbox that changes something at once. That is a switch.*

*Figure: DoSelect all shows mixed while only some rows are chosen.*

*Figure: Don’tSelect all checked while a row is not: the two disagree.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the checkbox. |
| Space | Checks or unchecks it. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<input type="checkbox">` | Native: checked, unchecked and, through the indeterminate property, mixed. |
| `<label>` | Names the input and enlarges what can be clicked. |
| `aria-describedby` | Ties the help text to the input. |

#### Notes

- A native checkbox: Space toggles it, and the indeterminate state is announced as mixed.
- The help text sits outside the label and is tied to the input with `aria-describedby`.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Checkbox } from '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox.css'
```

### API

*Props of Checkbox*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What is being chosen. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  One line of help, read after the label. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `indeterminate`  Shown as a dash: some, not all, of the items it governs are checked. Clicking it checks it. | `boolean` | `false` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<input>` , except type, and a `ref` to it.

---

# Segmented control · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/segmented-control/

> Segmented control, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Segmented control

One choice among two to five, drawn as pills on a well: the unit figures are shown in, the view of a list. Native radios underneath.

- Native HTML
- 1.9 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control`

### Examples

*Figure: With a legend*

```
import { SegmentedControl } from '@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control'

export default function Units() {
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      legend="Unit"
      defaultValue="plt"
      options={[
        { value: 'plt', label: 'Pallets' },
        { value: 'kg', label: 'Kilograms' },
        { value: 'items', label: 'Items' },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

*Figure: Icons only, small*

```
import { SegmentedControl } from '@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import calendarSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/calendar_month.svg?raw'
import gridSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/grid_view.svg?raw'
import listSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/view_list.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const CalendarIcon = symbol(calendarSymbol)
const GridIcon = symbol(gridSymbol)
const ListIcon = symbol(listSymbol)

export default function Views() {
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      legend="View"
      hideLegend
      iconOnly
      size="small"
      defaultValue="list"
      options={[
        { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: <ListIcon /> },
        { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid', icon: <GridIcon /> },
        { value: 'calendar', label: 'Calendar', icon: <CalendarIcon /> },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Sizes, content and states*

### Usage

- The choice applies at once. More than five options is a select.
- Icons only when each icon is unmistakable in its context; every option keeps a label for assistive technology.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoTwo to five short options that change the view of the same content.*

*Figure: Don’tSeven options, or long ones: use a select.*

*Figure: DoIcons alone only when each one is familiar; the labels stay for screen readers.*

*Figure: Don’tActions in a segmented control. It chooses a state; buttons act.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the chosen option. |
| Arrow keys | Move to the next or previous option and choose it. |
| Space | Chooses the focused option. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<fieldset> and <legend>` | Group the options under one name, read when focus enters. A hidden legend is still read. |
| `<input type="radio">` | One per option: announced as “2 of 3”, with the chosen one checked. |
| Icons only | Each option keeps its label as text for assistive technology. |

#### Notes

- A `<fieldset>` named by its legend, with one native radio per option: arrow keys move the choice, Tab leaves the group.
- The legend can be hidden visually and still names the group.
- It submits with a form without any script, under its `name`.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { SegmentedControl } from '@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control.css'
```

### API

*Props of SegmentedControl*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` Required  What is being chosen, such as “Unit”. Always present for assistive technology; drawn unless `hideLegend`. | `string` | — |
| `hideLegend`  Hides the legend from view while keeping it for assistive technology, when the options explain themselves. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `options` Required  Two to five options. More than that is a select. | `SegmentedOption[]` | — |
| `name`  Shared by the radios, so the choice is submitted with a form. A unique name is made when it is left out. | `string` | — |
| `value`  The chosen value, for a controlled control. | `string` | — |
| `defaultValue`  The value chosen at first, for an uncontrolled control. | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange`  Called with the new value when the choice changes. | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `iconOnly`  Show icons only. Every option still needs a label. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `size`  Medium for toolbars and forms; small inside a card header, beside its title. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<fieldset>` , except onChange | defaultValue, and a `ref` to it.

# Text field and select · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/field/

> Text field and select, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Text field and select

Native inputs and selects with their label above, help and errors below. The edge of the box is the focus ring: 1 px at rest, 2 px while focused, red when something is wrong.

- Native HTML
- 2.2 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/field`

### Examples

*Figure: Text fields*

```
import { TextField } from '@orbex/sonar-components/field'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import searchSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/search.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const SearchIcon = symbol(searchSymbol)

export default function TextFields() {
  return (
    <>
      <TextField label="Product" placeholder="Name or code" />
      <TextField label="Quantity" type="number" inputMode="numeric" defaultValue="40" description="In pallets. Up to 120 per order." />
      <TextField label="Delivery date" defaultValue="May 3" error="Choose a date from May 12 on: earlier days are closed." />
      <TextField label="Search orders" type="search" icon={<SearchIcon />} placeholder="Order, product or carrier" />
      <TextField label="Account" defaultValue="Northwind Foods" disabled />
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Selects*

```
import { SelectField } from '@orbex/sonar-components/field'

export default function Select() {
  return (
    <>
      <SelectField label="Warehouse" defaultValue="north">
        <option value="north">North · Valencia</option>
        <option value="south">South · Seville</option>
        <option value="central">Central · Madrid</option>
      </SelectField>
      <SelectField label="Carrier" size="small" defaultValue="">
        <option value="" disabled>
          Choose a carrier
        </option>
        <option>Iberia Freight</option>
        <option>Atlas Logistics</option>
      </SelectField>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: States*

*Figure: Sizes*

### Usage

- The label is always visible. A placeholder is an example of what to type, never the label.
- An error says what is wrong and how to fix it, in one sentence. Show it when the field is left or the form is sent, not while typing.
- The select is the platform’s own list: the best picker on phones, and complete keyboard and screen reader support everywhere. For searching a long list, a combobox comes later.
- On touch screens fields grow to 48 px and their text to 16 px, below which iOS zooms in when a field is focused.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA label above the field, always visible; the placeholder is an example.*

*Figure: Don’tThe placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.*

*Figure: DoAn error that says what is wrong and how to fix it.*

*Figure: Don’tAn error that only says something is wrong.*

*Figure: DoA select for one choice among many, with a sensible default.*

*Figure: Don’tA select for two options. Two choices side by side are quicker to compare.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the field. |
| Arrow keys, Space, Enter | Open and move through a select’s options, with the platform’s own picker. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<label for>` | Names the input or select. |
| `aria-describedby` | Points at the help and then the error, so both are read after the name. |
| `aria-invalid` | Set while there is an error. |
| Icon | aria-hidden. |

#### Notes

- The label is a `<label for>`; help and error are tied to the control with `aria-describedby`, in that order.
- An error sets `aria-invalid` and is marked by an icon and by words, not by color alone.
- Placeholder text reads at the tertiary level, 5.6:1 on cards.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { TextField, SelectField } from '@orbex/sonar-components/field'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/field.css'
```

### API

#### `TextField`

A native text input with its label, help and error. Any input type that takes text: text, search, email, number…

*Props of TextField*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  The field’s name, always visible above it. Placeholders are examples, never labels. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  Help shown under the field and read after the label. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `error`  What is wrong and how to fix it. When present, the field is marked invalid. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `size`  Height of the field: medium (48 px) in forms, small (36 px) inside rows and panels, such as a quantity in a list. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |
| `icon`  Icon at the start of the control, such as a search glass. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `suffix`  A unit after the value, inside the field, such as plt; it is read after the value. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<input>` , except size, and a `ref` to it.

#### `SelectField`

A native select with its label, help and error. The list is the platform’s own: the best picker on phones and full keyboard and screen reader support everywhere.

*Props of SelectField*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  The field’s name, always visible above it. Placeholders are examples, never labels. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  Help shown under the field and read after the label. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `error`  What is wrong and how to fix it. When present, the field is marked invalid. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `size`  Height of the field: medium (48 px) in forms, small (36 px) inside rows and panels, such as a quantity in a list. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |
| `icon`  Icon at the start of the control, such as a search glass. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `children` Required  The `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<select>` , except size, and a `ref` to it.
