# Notice · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/notice/

> Notice, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Notice

A message inside the page, next to what it is about, that stays until the situation changes. The hue sits in the tint and the icon; the text stays at a reading level.

- Native HTML
- 1.3 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/notice`

### Examples

*Figure: Tones*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Notice } from '@orbex/sonar-components/notice'

export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <>
      <Notice title="Take a look:">
        New recycled-fiber boxes are in the market.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="success" title="Order created.">
        PO-2210 was sent for confirmation.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="warning" title="Carrier changed." action={<Button size="small" variant="text">Review</Button>}>
        Delivery 04-121A now arrives with Atlas Logistics.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="danger" title="2 invoices overdue.">
        Pay them before May 20 to keep your credit line.
      </Notice>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Tones and content*

### Usage

- For a state that lasts: overdue invoices, a changed carrier, a tip. For feedback on an action that just happened, use a toast.
- A few bold words that name the situation, then one or two sentences. At most one action, as a text button.
- Info and success are calm; warning asks to check something; danger means something is wrong and has a way out.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA notice for a situation that lasts, with the step that resolves it.*

*Figure: Don’tA notice for something that just happened and needs nothing. That is a toast.*

*Figure: DoOne notice, the one that matters most.*

*Figure: Don’tA stack of notices: none of them stands out any more.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the notice’s action, when it has one; the notice itself does not take focus. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| No role by default | A notice present when the page loads is read in its place. |
| `role="status" or role="alert"` | Added by the app when a notice appears while the page is in use, so it is announced: status politely, alert at once. |
| Icon | aria-hidden: the tone is also in the words. |

#### Notes

- The icon is decorative; the bold title says what kind of notice it is.
- A notice that appears while someone works takes `role="status"`, or `role="alert"` when it is urgent, so it is announced.
- Text is at the default level on every tint, so it passes AA in both themes.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Notice } from '@orbex/sonar-components/notice'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/notice.css'
```

### API

*Props of Notice*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone`  Info for news and tips, success for a finished task, warning for something to check, danger for a problem. | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` |
| `title`  A few words in bold before the message. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `children` Required  The message, one or two sentences. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `action`  One action at the end, such as a Button with `variant="text"`. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<div>` , except title, and a `ref` to it.

---

# Toast · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/toast/

> Toast, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Toast

Feedback on something that just happened: one line on the inverse surface at the bottom of the window, with at most one action, usually Undo. It rises with the expressive spring, one of the two moments that bounce.

- Behavior from Base UI
- 2.4 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/toast`

### Examples

*Figure: Saved, and removed with undo*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@orbex/sonar-components/toast'
import { useState } from 'react'

/* Saving says it worked; removing offers to take it back. Neither asks first. */
function Actions() {
  const toast = useToast()
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(true)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="tonal" onClick={() => toast({ message: 'Layout saved.' })}>
        Save layout
      </Button>
      <Button
        variant="outlined"
        disabled={!shown}
        onClick={() => {
          setShown(false)
          toast({ message: 'Inventory removed from your overview.', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => setShown(true) } })
        }}
      >
        {shown ? 'Remove Inventory' : 'Inventory removed'}
      </Button>
    </>
  )
}

export default function Undo() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Actions />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Content and action states*

### Usage

- Say what happened in a few words, in the past tense: “Layout saved.”
- Prefer an Undo in a toast to a confirmation before acting. Confirm only what cannot be undone.
- One toast at a time: a new one replaces the last. A toast with an action stays ten seconds instead of five.
- Wrap the app once in a `ToastProvider`, and show toasts from anywhere with `useToast`.
- Toasts centre on the window, 24 px above its foot. In an app with a sidebar, `inset` centres them on the main area and lifts them above a footer or a bottom app bar, as the product does: `inset={{ left: '224px', bottom: '66px' }}`.
- `closeButton={false}` leaves out the close button (on the provider, or on one toast); the toast still goes after its time or with a swipe.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA toast confirms what just happened, and offers to undo it.*

*Figure: Don’tA toast for a problem that needs action: it leaves before it is read. Use a notice or a dialog.*

*Figure: DoA few words, on one line.*

*Figure: Don’tA paragraph in a toast.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| F6 | Moves focus to the notifications region, from anywhere on the page. |
| Tab | Moves to the toast’s action and its close button. |
| Enter or Space | Activates the action, or dismisses the toast. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="region", aria-live="polite"` | The viewport, named “Notifications”: a new toast is announced without interrupting. |
| `role="dialog"` | Each toast, not modal, named by its message. |
| Timers | Pause while the pointer or focus is in the region, so a message never disappears while it is being read. A toast with an action stays for 10 seconds. |

#### Notes

- The message is announced politely by assistive technology, without moving focus.
- The timer pauses while the toast is hovered or focused, so there is time to reach the action.
- It can be dismissed with its close button or swiped away, down or to the side.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { ToastProvider } from '@orbex/sonar-components/toast'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/toast.css'
```

### API

*Props of ToastProvider*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` Required  The part of the app that can show toasts, usually all of it. useToast works anywhere inside. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `timeout`  Time a toast stays, in milliseconds. One with an action stays twice as long, so there is time to use it. | `number` | `5000` |
| `closeLabel`  Name of the close button. | `string` | `'Dismiss'` |
| `label`  Name of the region the toasts appear in. Give each provider its own when a page has more than one. | `string` | `'Notifications'` |
| `inset`  Where the toasts sit, as CSS lengths: `left` and `right` bound the area they centre in (such as the main area, right of a sidebar), `bottom` lifts them above a footer or a bottom app bar. The window’s safe area is added to `bottom`. | `{ left?: string; right?: string; bottom?: string }` | `{ left: 0, right: 0, bottom: 24px }` |
| `closeButton`  Whether toasts carry a close button. One with an action can still be swiped away or wait for its timeout. | `boolean` | `true` |

---

# Menu · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/menu/

> Menu, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Menu

A list of actions in a popup that grows from its trigger. Base UI provides the behavior: focus, arrow keys, typeahead, dismissal and positioning away from the window edges.

- Behavior from Base UI
- 2.0 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/menu`

### Examples

*Figure: Actions on an order*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Menu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/menu'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import copySymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/content_copy.svg?raw'
import deleteSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/delete.svg?raw'
import downloadSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/download.svg?raw'
import expandSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/keyboard_arrow_down.svg?raw'
import printSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/print.svg?raw'
import shareSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/share.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const CopyIcon = symbol(copySymbol)
const DeleteIcon = symbol(deleteSymbol)
const DownloadIcon = symbol(downloadSymbol)
const ExpandIcon = symbol(expandSymbol)
const PrintIcon = symbol(printSymbol)
const ShareIcon = symbol(shareSymbol)

export default function Actions() {
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger render={<Button variant="outlined" iconEnd={<ExpandIcon />} />}>Actions</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Content>
        <Menu.Item icon={<DownloadIcon />} trailing="CSV">
          Export
        </Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Item icon={<PrintIcon />}>Print</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Item icon={<ShareIcon />}>Share link</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Item icon={<CopyIcon />}>Duplicate order</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.Item icon={<DeleteIcon />} tone="danger">
          Cancel order
        </Menu.Item>
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu.Root>
  )
}
```

*Figure: A choice inside a menu*

```
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import { Menu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/menu'
import { useState } from 'react'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import moreSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/more_vert.svg?raw'
import refreshSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/refresh.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const MoreIcon = symbol(moreSymbol)
const RefreshIcon = symbol(refreshSymbol)

export default function Units() {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger render={<IconButton label="Inventory options" icon={<MoreIcon />} />} />
      <Menu.Content align="end">
        <Menu.Group>
          <Menu.GroupLabel>Show figures in</Menu.GroupLabel>
          <Menu.RadioGroup value={unit} onValueChange={(value) => setUnit(String(value))}>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="plt">Pallets</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="kg">Kilograms</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="items">Items</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
        </Menu.Group>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.Item icon={<RefreshIcon />}>Refresh stock</Menu.Item>
      </Menu.Content>
    </Menu.Root>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Kinds of item and their states*

### Usage

- For actions on the thing in view. Choices that change what is shown can live in a menu as a radio group.
- Destructive actions go last, after a separator, in the danger tone. They still need a confirmation or an undo.
- The trigger keeps its look: pass a Button or an IconButton with `render`.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoVerbs, grouped; the destructive item last, after a separator, in danger.*

*Figure: Don’tA destructive item among the others, one slip away from the common ones.*

*Figure: DoA short menu of actions on one thing.*

*Figure: Don’tA long list of places or records. That is navigation, a select or search.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space or Down arrow | On the trigger: opens the menu and focuses the first item. |
| Up and Down arrows | Move between items; disabled items are skipped. |
| Home and End | Go to the first or the last item. |
| A letter | Moves to the next item that starts with it. |
| Enter or Space | Activates the item, or chooses it in a group of choices. |
| Escape | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Tab | Closes the menu and moves on. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `aria-haspopup, aria-expanded` | On the trigger: it opens a menu, and whether it is open. |
| `role="menu"` | The popup; items are menuitem, or menuitemradio with aria-checked in a group of choices. |
| Group labels | Name their group, read when focus enters it. |

#### Notes

- The trigger announces that it opens a menu, and whether it is open.
- Arrow keys move between items, typing jumps to an item, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- The highlight stays neutral behind danger items, so their red text keeps 4.5:1.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Menu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/menu'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
```

### API

#### `Menu.Root`

Holds the menu’s open state.

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.Trigger`

The element that opens the menu. Pass a Button or an IconButton with `render`, so the trigger keeps its look.

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.Content`

The popup, positioned against the trigger and rendered at the end of the document.

*Props of Menu.Content*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className`  Classes added to the menu’s popup, after sonar-menu: a string, or a function of the menu’s state. | `ClassName` | — |
| `side`  Side of the trigger the menu opens on. It flips when there is no room. | `BaseMenu.Positioner.Props['side']` | `'bottom'` |
| `align`  How the menu lines up with its trigger along that side: start, center or end. A menu in a card header aligns to the end, so it opens inward. | `BaseMenu.Positioner.Props['align']` | `'start'` |
| `sideOffset`  Distance from the trigger, in pixels. | `number` | `6` |

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.Item`

An action.

*Props of Menu.Item*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className`  Classes added to the item, after its own: a string, or a function of its state. | `ClassName` | — |
| `icon`  Icon before the label. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `trailing`  Text at the end of the row, such as a shortcut or a count. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `tone`  Danger for destructive actions: the label turns red, and the action should still be confirmed or undoable. | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` |

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.Separator`

A rule between groups of items.

*Props of Menu.Separator*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className`  Classes added to the separator, after its own: a string, or a function of its state. | `ClassName` | — |

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.Group`

Items that belong together, named by a GroupLabel.

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.GroupLabel`

The name of a group, read when focus enters it.

*Props of Menu.GroupLabel*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className`  Classes added to the group label, after its own: a string, or a function of its state. | `ClassName` | — |

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.RadioGroup`

A set of items where exactly one is chosen, such as the unit figures are shown in.

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

#### `Menu.RadioItem`

One choice in a RadioGroup, with a check when chosen.

*Props of Menu.RadioItem*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className`  Classes added to the radio item, after its own: a string, or a function of its state. | `ClassName` | — |

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

# Tooltip · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tooltip/

> Tooltip, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Tooltip

A short label on the inverse surface, shown on hover and on keyboard focus. Base UI positions it and manages the delays.

- Behavior from Base UI
- 1.2 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/tooltip`

### Examples

*Figure: A toolbar of icon buttons*

```
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import { Tooltip, TooltipProvider } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tooltip'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import downloadSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/download.svg?raw'
import filterSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/filter_list.svg?raw'
import printSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/print.svg?raw'
import refreshSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/refresh.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const DownloadIcon = symbol(downloadSymbol)
const FilterIcon = symbol(filterSymbol)
const PrintIcon = symbol(printSymbol)
const RefreshIcon = symbol(refreshSymbol)

/* Inside one provider, once a tooltip is open the next one appears at once */
export default function Toolbar() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <div role="toolbar" aria-label="Orders" style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 4 }}>
        <Tooltip content="Filter">
          <IconButton label="Filter" icon={<FilterIcon />} />
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip content="Refresh">
          <IconButton label="Refresh" icon={<RefreshIcon />} />
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip content="Export as CSV">
          <IconButton label="Export as CSV" icon={<DownloadIcon />} />
        </Tooltip>
        <Tooltip content="Print">
          <IconButton label="Print" icon={<PrintIcon />} />
        </Tooltip>
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: Length*

### Usage

- A name or a hint, never information someone needs to continue: touch screens show tooltips only on a long press.
- Wrap a toolbar in a TooltipProvider: once one tooltip is open, the next appears at once.
- The trigger must be focusable, so keyboard users get the tooltip too.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA tooltip names an icon button, in a few words.*

*Figure: Don’tA tooltip that repeats a button’s own label.*

*Figure: DoInformation someone needs to act goes on the page, where it stays.*

*Figure: Don’tEssential instructions in a tooltip: hard to find, gone on touch, never interactive.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Focusing the trigger shows the tooltip, as hovering does. |
| Escape | Hides it. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| Not read separately | A tooltip repeats its trigger’s name, such as an icon button’s label, for sighted people. Anything that must be read goes in the name or on the page. |

#### Notes

- Keyboard focus opens the tooltip without delay; Escape closes it.
- Text on the inverse surface passes AA in both themes.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Tooltip, TooltipProvider } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tooltip'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/tooltip.css'
```

### API

#### `Tooltip`

A short label on the inverse surface, shown on hover and focus. Wrap groups of triggers in TooltipProvider so that, once one tooltip is open, moving to the next shows it without the delay.

*Props of Tooltip*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` Required  The text shown. Short: a name or a hint, never something the person must read to continue. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `children` Required  The element it describes, usually an IconButton. It must be focusable, so keyboard users get the tooltip too. | `ReactElement` | — |
| `side`  Side of the element the tooltip opens on. It flips when there is no room. | `BaseTooltip.Positioner.Props['side']` | `'top'` |
| `delay`  Time the pointer rests on the trigger before the tooltip opens, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus opens it at once. | `number` | `300` |

#### `TooltipProvider`

Shares the open delay between tooltips, so moving along a toolbar does not wait at every button.

Passes every other prop to Base UI: see the [Base UI reference](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip).

---

# Dialog · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/dialog/

> Dialog, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Dialog

A dialog on the native dialog element, in three placements: centered for a decision, over a scrim; at the end for a side panel beside the page, with no scrim; at the bottom for a sheet on phones. The browser handles focus.

- Native HTML
- 9.0 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/dialog`

### Examples

*Figure: Confirmation*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { useState } from 'react'

/* Confirm only what cannot be undone. The main action goes last; the dialog closes on any choice. */
export default function Confirm() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outlined" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Reset to default
      </Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Reset the overview?"
        description="Your cards go back to the default layout. Cards you added stay available in Customize."
        actions={
          <>
            <Button variant="text" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Keep my layout
            </Button>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Reset</Button>
          </>
        }
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Side panel*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import { useState } from 'react'

const rows = [
  ['Carrier', 'Iberia Freight'],
  ['Window', 'May 12, 08:00–10:00'],
  ['Pallets', '24 plt'],
  ['Dock', 'North · Gate 3'],
]

export default function SidePanel() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="tonal" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Delivery details
      </Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        placement="end"
        modal={false}
        title="Delivery 04-127C"
        actions={<Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Track delivery</Button>}
      >
        <Status tone="warning" appearance="chip">
          Due today
        </Status>
        <dl style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'auto 1fr', gap: '10px 24px', margin: 0, font: 'var(--sonar-type-label-md)' }}>
          {rows.map(([term, value]) => (
            <div key={term} style={{ display: 'contents' }}>
              <dt style={{ color: 'var(--sonar-color-text-tertiary)' }}>{term}</dt>
              <dd style={{ margin: 0, color: 'var(--sonar-color-text-strong)' }}>{value}</dd>
            </div>
          ))}
        </dl>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Bottom sheet*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { TextField } from '@orbex/sonar-components/field'
import { useState } from 'react'

/* On phones, panels rise from the bottom, with no scrim. Typing would be lost, so a tap outside does not close this one. */
export default function Sheet() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="tonal" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        New order on a phone
      </Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        placement="bottom"
        dismissible={false}
        title="New order"
        actions={<Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Place order</Button>}
      >
        <TextField label="Product" placeholder="Name or code" />
        <TextField label="Quantity" type="number" inputMode="numeric" placeholder="0" description="In pallets." />
      </Dialog>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Confirm only what cannot be undone, such as resetting a layout. Everything else gets an undo in a toast.
- The title asks the question; the main action answers it with a verb, last in the row.
- Panels open at the end on tablets and desktops, from 600 px wide (an iPad mini in portrait keeps them at the side), and from the bottom on phones, 44 px from the top of the window. On a tablet this departs from the product’s 768 px size class, on purpose: the side panel keeps the overview in view. On desktops a side panel slides in 48 px with a fade, as in the product; on tablets it slides all the way in from the right edge, as [Navigation by device](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/navigation/#tablets) defines.
- Nothing in a panel or sheet shows the system’s scrollbar: its body scrolls with the product’s thin indicator, 4 px from the edge.
- A side panel is not modal (`modal={false}`): it starts under the top bar, has no scrim, and the overview stays in view with the row it came from marked. Only decisions, such as a confirmation, take a scrim.
- The six panels the overview opens are gathered, live, in [Patterns › Panels](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/panels/).
- Turn `dismissible` off when a stray click outside would lose what someone typed.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA title that asks the question, and buttons that answer it with verbs.*

*Figure: Don’t“Are you sure?” with OK and Cancel: people must read the text to know what OK does.*

*Figure: DoAsk only when the step cannot be undone. Otherwise act, and offer Undo.*

*Figure: Don’tA dialog for every small step: people learn to press OK without reading.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab and Shift Tab | Move among the dialog’s controls only; the page behind is inert. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to what opened it. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<dialog> opened with showModal()` | The browser moves focus in, keeps it inside and makes the rest of the page inert. |
| `aria-labelledby, aria-describedby` | The title names the dialog; the description is read after it. |
| Close button | Named by closeLabel, “Close” by default. |
| Body that scrolls (side panels and sheets) | A group named by the title while it scrolls, so the keyboard can scroll it; the indicator beside it is drawn and hidden. |

#### Notes

- Modal: `showModal()` moves focus into the dialog, keeps it there, makes the rest of the page inert and returns focus to the trigger on close.
- Side panel: focus moves into the panel when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. Tab and Shift+Tab go round inside it, so focus never lands on the page behind; the page stays in view and a click on it still works. On phones, where it is a sheet over the page, the rest of the page is inert while it is open. Escape or a click outside closes it.
- The title names the dialog and the description is read with it.
- Escape and the close button always close it, whatever `dismissible` says.
- With reduced motion, the dialog fades without moving.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { DialogHost, Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog.css'
```

### API

#### `DialogHost`

Holds the side panels and sheets written inside it, as a drawn app frame does, instead of placing them against the window.

#### `Dialog`

*Props of Dialog*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` Required  Whether the dialog is shown. The dialog is always controlled. | `boolean` | — |
| `onOpenChange` Required  Called with `false` when the person closes it: the close button, Escape, a click outside, or a swipe down. | `(open: boolean) => void` | — |
| `title` Required  The heading, which also names the dialog for assistive technology. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  One paragraph under the title, read when the dialog opens. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `placement`  Center for a decision; end for a side panel, such as the details of a delivery; bottom for a sheet on phones. On phones (under 600 px) a side panel becomes a sheet from the bottom, with a handle to swipe it down; tablets and desktops keep it at the side. | `'center' \| 'end' \| 'bottom'` | `'center'` |
| `modal`  Whether the rest of the page waits behind a scrim. A side panel that sits beside the overview, such as the details of a delivery or a new order, is not modal: no scrim, the page stays in view and the row it came from stays marked. It starts under the top bar (--sonar-dialog-top) and closes on Escape or a click outside. | `boolean` | `true` |
| `actions`  Buttons at the foot of the dialog, the main action last. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `closeLabel`  Name of the close button. | `string` | `'Close'` |
| `dismissible`  Whether a click on the scrim, or outside a panel that is not modal, closes it. Turn it off when closing would lose what the person typed. | `boolean` | `true` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<dialog>` , except open | title | onClose | onCancel, and a `ref` to it.

---

# Scroll area · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/scroll-area/

> Scroll area, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Scroll area

Content that scrolls inside a fixed height, as the product’s lists do: no scrollbar of the system, a fade at the edge that has more, and a thin indicator that shows while it scrolls and never covers a row or its buttons.

- Native HTML
- 2.0 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area`

### Examples

*Figure: The Invoices card: the indicator runs in the padding*

```
import { Card, CardLink } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { ScrollArea } from '@orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import downloadSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/download.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const DownloadIcon = symbol(downloadSymbol)

const invoices = [
  ['Tuesday, May 12', 'INV-0025698', '04-118B'],
  ['Monday, May 11', 'INV-0025677', '04-121A'],
  ['Monday, May 11', 'INV-0025671', '04-130A'],
  ['Friday, May 8', 'INV-0025664', '04-112B'],
  ['Thursday, May 7', 'INV-0025642', '04-109C'],
  ['Wednesday, May 6', 'INV-0025631', '04-104A'],
] as const

/* The Invoices card: the list scrolls between the heading and the footer. Its first rule is the heading's (1.0.0-alpha.23:
   the list drew a second one under it), as in the product, where the rule is the list's first line. No scrollbar of the system: the indicator
   runs in the card's padding, beside the download buttons, never over them */
export default function Invoices() {
  return (
    <Card titleAs="h3" title="Invoices" size="m" footer={<CardLink href="/patterns/cards/#optional">Go to Invoices</CardLink>}>
      <ScrollArea label="Invoices" style={{ flex: '1 1 0' }}>
        <ul role="list" style={{ margin: 0, padding: 0 }}>
          {invoices.map(([date, number, order]) => (
            <li key={number} style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12, height: 66, borderBottom: '1px solid var(--sonar-color-divider)' }}>
              <span style={{ font: '400 12px/16px var(--sonar-font-family-sans)', color: 'var(--sonar-color-text-meta)' }}>
                {date}
                <br />
                <strong style={{ color: 'var(--sonar-color-text-strong)', fontWeight: 600 }}>{number}</strong>
                <br />
                {`Order ${order}`}
              </span>
              <button
                type="button"
                aria-label={`Download ${number}`}
                style={{ display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center', width: 24, height: 24, padding: 0, border: 0, borderRadius: '50%', background: 'none', color: 'var(--sonar-color-accent)', boxShadow: 'inset 0 0 0 1px var(--sonar-color-accent)' }}
              >
                <DownloadIcon style={{ width: 15, height: 15 }} />
              </button>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </ScrollArea>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

*Figure: No padding beside it: the indicator takes its own lane*

```
import { ScrollArea } from '@orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area'

const updates = ['2.03 · Route progress on the delivery map', '2.02 · Recurring orders from favorites', '2.01 · Switches for the modules', '2.00 · Dark mode', '1.12 · Invoices from the overview', '1.11 · Help on delivery alerts', '1.10 · Invoices in bulk', '1.09 · Driver contact on delivery notes', '1.08 · Last quantities per product']

/* No padding beside the area: the indicator takes a lane of its own at the end, which the rows never reach */
export default function Inside() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', height: 220, width: 'min(100%, 360px)', borderRadius: 'var(--sonar-shape-corner-medium)', background: 'var(--sonar-color-surface-card)', boxShadow: 'var(--sonar-elevation-1)' }}>
      <ScrollArea label="System updates" indicator="inside">
        <ul role="list" style={{ margin: 0, padding: '4px 16px' }}>
          {updates.map((update) => (
            <li key={update} style={{ padding: '12px 0', borderBottom: '1px solid var(--sonar-color-divider)', font: '400 12px/16px var(--sonar-font-family-sans)', color: 'var(--sonar-color-text-strong)' }}>
              {update}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </ScrollArea>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- For every list that scrolls inside something else: the lists of the optional cards, the bodies of side panels and sheets, the System notifications. The page itself keeps the browser’s scroll.
- A list stops on its rows, scrolling down or up. In a card, a row that stops at the top lies on the title’s rule, with as much room above its content as below it; the last stop mirrors the first, and every stop shows whole rows. The fades cover only the room inside a row (or between bands), never a row that has stopped.
- The indicator is 2 px, in the scrollbar color of each theme, never shorter than 32 px. It shows while scrolling and fades out a second after; it flashes for 0.8 s when the pointer or the keyboard arrives, to say there is more.
- Outside (the default): it runs 4 to 6 px past the end of the area, in the padding of the card or panel around it. Inside: when there is no padding, it takes a 12 px lane at the end of the area, and the content stops before it.
- Never a system scrollbar over the content: on phones it was drawn over the download buttons, white in dark mode.
- A card’s own list that gives way first is a Card scroll, built on the same behavior.

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the area only while it scrolls; when everything fits, focus goes straight to its controls. |
| Up and Down arrows, Page Up and Page Down | Scroll the area once it has focus. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="group" while scrolling` | Named by label (“Invoices”), so focus arriving on it says what it is. |
| Fade and indicator | Drawn, aria-hidden; the area’s own scroll position is what assistive technology reads. No system scrollbar is drawn. |

#### Notes

- While it scrolls, the area is a named group that takes focus, so the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down scroll it. When everything fits, it adds no tab stop.
- Label it with what it holds: “Invoices”, “What’s new”.
- The indicator is decoration, hidden from assistive technology; with reduced motion it appears and goes without fading.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { ScrollArea } from '@orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/scroll-area.css'
```

### API

*Props of ScrollArea*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What the content is, read when the area takes focus to scroll: “Invoices”, “System notifications”. | `string` | — |
| `indicator`  Where the indicator runs. Outside: in the padding beside the area, 4 to 6 px past its end, as in the product’s cards and panels, where there is padding to hold it. Inside: in a lane of its own at the end of the area, which the content never reaches, for an area with no padding beside it. | `'outside' \| 'inside'` | `'outside'` |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<div>` , and a `ref` to it.

# Card · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card/

> Card, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Card

The unit of the overview: a titled region with one figure that sums it up, its detail and a way to the full page. In the grid it takes one of four heights and scrolls what does not fit between its header and footer.

- Native HTML
- 4.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Card link, Card scroll, Unit menu
- `@orbex/sonar-components/card`

### Examples

*Figure: Orders, with a unit, a summary, a tick bar and its link*

```
import { Card, CardLink, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'
import { useState } from 'react'

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
  { value: 'items', short: 'items', name: 'Items' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420, items: 36 }

const may = [
  { label: 'Shipped', tone: 'accent', value: 1420 },
  { label: 'On hold', tone: 'strong', value: 80 },
  { label: 'Pending', tone: 'muted', value: 1100 },
] as const

/* A title, a unit, one figure, its detail and the way to the full page */
export default function Basic() {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  const format = (pallets: number) => `${(pallets * perPallet[unit]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`
  return (
    <Card
      titleAs="h3"
      title="Orders"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />}
      summary={{ label: 'Open total', value: format(3940) }}
      footer={<CardLink href="/patterns/overview/#card-orders">Go to Orders</CardLink>}
    >
      <TickBar label="May orders" format={format} segments={[...may]} />
    </Card>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: States, at rest and while the overview is edited*

### Usage

- **Size**: S, M, L or XL (245, 375, 405 and 535 px) in the overview grid. Without a size, the card follows its content.
- **Summary**: one figure with its unit; tone default for figures that are not the card’s main one.
- **Actions**: a Unit menu, and nothing else. **Footer**: a Card link and at most one action.
- **Label**: only when the same card shows twice on a page, as on [Cards](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/#sizes).
- How the six cards of the overview are composed, and their rules, are in [Patterns › Cards](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/).

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoOne figure first, with its unit; the content explains it.*

*Figure: Don’tSeveral figures of the same weight: nothing says which one matters.*

*Figure: DoAt most one action, beside the way to the full page.*

*Figure: Don’tA footer of buttons: the card becomes the page it should lead to.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the card’s controls in reading order: unit menu, content, footer. |
| Unit menu | Opens with Enter, Space or Down arrow, like any menu. |
| Up and Down arrows, Page Up and Page Down | On content that scrolls, once it has focus: scroll it. It takes focus only while it scrolls. |
| Left and Right arrows | On the chosen day of a calendar (Deliveries, Payment calendar): the previous or next day. In the month, Up and Down move a week. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<section aria-labelledby>` | Each card is a region named by its title, so the overview can be read card by card. Where the same card shows twice, label names each copy: “Orders, size S”. |
| Unit menu | Named with what it shows and what that means: “Unit: plt, Pallets”, so voice control can reach it by its visible text. Its choices are a group of radio items. |
| Summary bar | The bar between label and value is drawn, so it is never read aloud. |
| `role="group" while scrolling` | Content that scrolls is a group named by its list (“Deliveries of May 12”) or by the card’s title, so focus arriving on it says what it is. The fade and the indicator are drawn and hidden. |

#### Notes

- The card is a region named by its title, so the overview reads as a list of landmarks.
- The title’s level follows the page: `titleAs="h3"` under a page section.

### Use it

Card shares its entry point and stylesheet with Card link, Card scroll, Unit menu. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { Card } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
```

### API

*Props of Card*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` Required  The card’s name, which also names the region for assistive technology. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `titleAs`  Heading level of the title, to fit the page’s outline. | `'h2' \| 'h3'` | `'h2'` |
| `actions`  Controls at the end of the header, such as a UnitMenu. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `summary`  The figure that sums the card up, under the title: a label and a value, such as Open total and 6,720 plt. | `{ label: ReactNode; value: ReactNode; tone?: 'accent' \| 'default' }` | — |
| `footer`  The way out of the card, usually a CardLink to the full page. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `size`  Height in the overview grid: S, M, L or XL from the layout tokens. The header and footer stay put; content that does not fit scrolls between them. Without a size the card takes the height of its content. | `'s' \| 'm' \| 'l' \| 'xl'` | — |
| `label`  The region’s accessible name, when the title alone would repeat on the page: the same card shown twice, as in “Orders, size S” and “Orders, size M”. By default the title names the region. | `string` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<section>` , except title, and a `ref` to it.

# Card link · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-link/

> Card link, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Card link

The way out of a card: a link to the page the card sums up, with the arrow in a filled circle. It sits at the foot of the card, beside at most one action.

- Native HTML
- 4.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Card, Card scroll, Unit menu
- `@orbex/sonar-components/card`

### Examples

*Figure: Links to the pages of the overview*

```
import { CardLink } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'

/* “Go to” and the name of the page the card summarizes */
export default function Links() {
  return (
    <>
      <CardLink href="/patterns/overview/#card-orders">Go to Orders</CardLink>
      <CardLink href="/patterns/overview/#card-deliveries">Go to Deliveries</CardLink>
      <CardLink href="/patterns/overview/#card-balance">Go to Balance</CardLink>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: At rest, hovered, focused and pressed*

### Usage

- “Go to” and the name of the page: Go to Orders, Go to Deliveries.
- One per card, in the footer. Rows open their details; the card link leaves the card.
- It is a link, not a button: it navigates, opens in a new tab and can be copied.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoSay where it goes: “Go to” and the page’s name.*

*Figure: Don’t“More” or “Click here”: out of context, they say nothing.*

*Figure: DoOne card link, at the foot of the card.*

*Figure: Don’tA card link on every row: rows open their details; the card link leaves the card.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the control, and on. |
| Enter or Space | Follows the link. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<a href>` | A native link: it opens in a new tab, can be copied and is listed with the page’s links. |
| Text | Says where it goes, “Go to Orders”, so it reads on its own in a list of links. |
| Arrow | Drawn and aria-hidden. |

#### Notes

- The text alone names the destination, so the link reads well in a screen reader’s list of links.

### Use it

Card link shares its entry point and stylesheet with Card, Card scroll, Unit menu. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { CardLink } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
```

### API

*Props of CardLink*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` Required  Where it goes, as a verb phrase: Go to Orders. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<a>` , and a `ref` to it.

# Card scroll · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-scroll/

> Card scroll, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Card scroll

The part of a card’s content that gives way first when the card’s size leaves no room: it keeps its full height while it fits, and scrolls when it does not, while the rest of the card stays in place.

- Native HTML
- 4.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Card, Card link, Unit menu
- `@orbex/sonar-components/card`

### Examples

*Figure: Deliveries in size S: the day’s list scrolls*

```
import { Card, CardLink, CardScroll } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'

const deliveries = [
  { id: '04-118B', items: 2, pallets: 40, status: 'Delivered', tone: 'positive' },
  { id: '04-121A', items: 7, pallets: 150, status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-127C', items: 1, pallets: 15, status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-130A', items: 8, pallets: 210, status: 'Delivered', tone: 'positive' },
] as const

/* Size S leaves no room for the whole day: the list scrolls between the heading and the footer, which stay put */
export default function Scroll() {
  return (
    <Card titleAs="h3" title="Deliveries" size="s" footer={<CardLink href="/patterns/overview/#card-deliveries">Go to Deliveries</CardLink>}>
      <p style={{ margin: '0 0 8px', font: 'var(--sonar-type-label-md)' }}>Tuesday, May 12</p>
      <CardScroll label="Deliveries of May 12">
        <ul role="list" style={{ padding: 0 }}>
          {deliveries.map(({ id, items, pallets, status, tone }) => (
            <li key={id} style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', gap: 12, padding: '10px 0', borderBottom: '1px solid var(--sonar-color-divider)' }}>
              <span>
                {`${id} ${items} ${items === 1 ? 'item' : 'items'} · ${pallets} plt`}
              </span>
              <Status tone={tone}>{status}</Status>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </CardScroll>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Wrap the list that can give way: the deliveries of a day, the products to reorder. Never the summary or a chart.
- One per card. If it is not enough, the card’s whole content scrolls as well.
- No scrollbar: a fade at the edge that has more, and a thin indicator while scrolling.
- Label it with what the list is: “Deliveries of May 12”.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoMark the list that should give way first; the summary and the footer stay in place.*

*Figure: Don’tContent cut at the card’s edge, with nothing to say there is more.*

*Figure: DoA label that names the list, read when it takes focus: “Deliveries of May 12”.*

*Figure: Don’tA generic label: “List”, “Scroll area”. Focus arrives and says nothing useful.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the list only while it scrolls; when everything fits, focus goes straight to its controls. |
| Up and Down arrows, Page Up and Page Down | Scroll the list once it has focus. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="group" while scrolling` | Named by label (“Deliveries of May 12”), so focus arriving on it says what it is. |
| Fade and indicator | Drawn, aria-hidden; the list’s own scroll position is what assistive technology reads. |

#### Notes

- It takes focus only while it scrolls, so a list that fits adds no tab stop.

### Use it

Card scroll shares its entry point and stylesheet with Card, Card link, Unit menu. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { CardScroll } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
```

### API

*Props of CardScroll*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What the list is, read when it takes focus to scroll: “Deliveries of May 12”. | `string` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<div>` , and a `ref` to it.

# Unit menu · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/unit-menu/

> Unit menu, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Unit menu

The unit a card’s figures are shown in, as a small pill that opens a menu: pallets, kilograms or items, dollars or euros. Changing it converts every figure in the card; it is the card’s only setting.

- Native HTML
- 4.8 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Card, Card link, Card scroll
- `@orbex/sonar-components/card`

### Examples

*Figure: A figure that follows its unit*

```
import { UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { useState } from 'react'

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
  { value: 'items', short: 'items', name: 'Items' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420, items: 36 }

/* Changing the unit converts every figure the card shows */
export default function Units() {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
      <span style={{ font: 'var(--sonar-type-title-md)', fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums' }}>
        {`${(2800 * perPallet[unit]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`}
      </span>
      <UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Sizes, variants and states

*Figure: The pill at rest, hovered, focused and pressed*

*Figure: Changing the unit, on a desktop card and a phone card*

### Usage

- At the end of the card’s header, and only there. Load `menu.css` with `card.css`: the pill opens a Menu.
- The pill shows the short code (plt, kg, USD); the menu shows the full names.
- The choice is per card: each team counts in its own unit.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoThe unit is the card’s only setting, at the end of its header.*

*Figure: Don’tSeveral settings in a card header: unit, period and sort compete with the title.*

*Figure: DoA short code on the pill; the full name in the menu.*

*Figure: Don’tFull words on the pill: it grows and crowds the title.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the pill. |
| Enter, Space or Down arrow | Opens the menu on the chosen unit. |
| Up and Down arrows | Move between units; typing a letter jumps to it. |
| Enter or Space | Chooses the unit and closes the menu; focus returns to the pill. |
| Escape | Closes the menu without a change. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| aria-label on the trigger | What it measures and what the pill shows: “Unit: plt, Pallets”, so voice control can reach it by its visible text. |
| `aria-haspopup and aria-expanded` | From Base UI: the pill says it opens a menu, and whether it is open. |
| `role="menuitemradio"` | The units are a group of radio items under a label; the chosen one is checked. |

#### Notes

- The pill is named with what it measures and what it shows, so “Unit: plt, Pallets” is both read and reachable by voice.

### Use it

Unit menu shares its entry point and stylesheet with Card, Card link, Card scroll. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
```

### API

*Props of UnitMenu*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What the unit measures, read with the current value: “Unit: plt, Pallets”. | `string` | — |
| `value` Required  The value of the unit shown, one of the options' values. The menu is always controlled. | `string` | — |
| `options` Required  The units to choose from: a short code, shown in caps on the pill and in the menu, and the full name, read with it. | `{ value: string; short: string; name: string }[]` | — |
| `onValueChange` Required  Called with the value of the unit chosen. The card converts its figures; the menu closes on its own. | `(value: string) => void` | — |

---

# Tick bar · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tick-bar/

> Tick bar, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Tick bar

A share of a whole as one row of fine ticks, each part in its share of the width and in its chart role. The parts meet without a gap, and no tick is ever split between two colors.

- Native HTML
- 1.3 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar`

### Examples

*Figure: Orders of a month, and an overdue share*

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'

const orders = [
  { value: 1420, tone: 'accent', label: 'Shipped' },
  { value: 80, tone: 'strong', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1100, tone: 'muted', label: 'Pending' },
] as const

const balance = [
  { value: 2_230_800, tone: 'danger', label: 'Overdue' },
  { value: 1_669_200, tone: 'muted', label: 'Not due yet' },
] as const

const plt = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} plt`
const usd = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} USD`

export default function TickBars() {
  return (
    <div className="chart-demo" data-shape="bars">
      <figure>
        <figcaption>May orders</figcaption>
        <TickBar label="May orders" format={plt} segments={[...orders]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={orders.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
      <figure>
        <figcaption>Overdue share of the balance</figcaption>
        <TickBar label="Overdue share of the balance" format={usd} segments={[...balance]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={balance.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Two or three parts of one whole. The first in accent, then strong, the rest in muted; danger only for an alert.
- A [Chart legend](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/chart-legend/) under it names the colors; the card states the figures in text.
- Give it a label and a format: they make its accessible name.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoThe parts of one whole, in their chart roles, named by a legend.*

*Figure: Don’tDanger for a part that is not an alert: the bar warns where nothing is wrong.*

*Figure: DoTwo or three parts, so each one reads.*

*Figure: Don’tMany small parts: the ticks blur into one color.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | A tick bar is a picture; the card states its figures in text. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="img" with aria-label` | One name lists every part with its value: “May orders: Shipped 1,420 plt, On hold 80 plt, Pending 1,100 plt”. |
| Ticks | Drawn in CSS, so they are never read one by one. |

#### Notes

- One name lists every part with its value, so the bar is read once, whole.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar.css'
```

### API

*Props of TickBar*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` Required  The parts of a whole, in order. Each takes its share of the width. | `ChartSegment[]` | — |
| `label` Required  What the bar measures, read before its parts: “May orders”. | `string` | — |
| `format`  Formats values for the accessible description. | `(value: number) => string` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<div>` , except children, and a `ref` to it.

# Ring chart · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/ring-chart/

> Ring chart, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Ring chart

Parts of a whole as a ring of ticks, 96 by default. The hole can hold the total; the parts run clockwise from the top, or counterclockwise toward a figure on their left.

- Native HTML
- 1.4 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart`

### Examples

*Figure: Two and three parts*

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { RingChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart'

const inventory = [
  { value: 840, tone: 'danger', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1960, tone: 'muted', label: 'Available' },
] as const

const orders = [
  { value: 1420, tone: 'accent', label: 'Shipped' },
  { value: 80, tone: 'strong', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1100, tone: 'muted', label: 'Pending' },
] as const

const plt = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} plt`

export default function Rings() {
  return (
    <div className="chart-demo" data-shape="rings">
      <figure>
        <figcaption>Inventory</figcaption>
        <RingChart label="Inventory" format={plt} style={{ width: 128 }} segments={[...inventory]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={inventory.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
      <figure>
        <figcaption>May orders</figcaption>
        <RingChart label="May orders" format={plt} style={{ width: 160 }} segments={[...orders]}>
          <span className="ring-total">
            <strong>2,600</strong>
            <span>plt</span>
          </span>
        </RingChart>
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={orders.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Two or three parts of one whole, never values over time.
- Set the width with CSS; the ring scales.
- `direction="counterclockwise"` when the first part’s figure sits on the left, as in Inventory.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoParts of a whole, with the figures beside the ring.*

*Figure: Don’tA ring for values over time. Months are a sequence: use a bar or a line.*

*Figure: DoThe alert in danger, the rest in the rest tone.*

*Figure: Don’tEvery part in a strong color: the one that needs attention no longer stands out.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | A ring is a picture; the figures beside it carry the values. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="img" with aria-label` | One name lists every part with its value, written by format. |
| Content in the hole | Read after the name, when it adds to it, such as a total. |

#### Notes

- One name lists every part with its value, written by `format`.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { RingChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart.css'
```

### API

*Props of RingChart*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` Required  The parts of the whole, in order around the ring: each with a label, a value and a chart tone. | `ChartSegment[]` | — |
| `label` Required  What the ring measures, read before its parts: “Inventory”. | `string` | — |
| `ticks`  Ticks around the ring. Fewer read as coarser; the dashboard uses 96. | `number` | `96` |
| `format`  Writes a value for the chart’s accessible name: “On hold 1,420 plt”. Plain numbers when left out. | `(value: number) => string` | — |
| `direction`  Which way the parts run from twelve o’clock. Counterclockwise puts the first part on the left, beside a label set on that side, as in the Inventory card. | `'clockwise' \| 'counterclockwise'` | `'clockwise'` |
| `children`  Content in the hole of the ring, such as the total. | `ReactNode` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<figure>` , except children, and a `ref` to it.

# Trend chart · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/trend-chart/

> Trend chart, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Trend chart

A month day by day as a line, with its running total dotted against a second axis. The legend turns each series off and on; hovering, touching or the arrow keys read a day.

- Native HTML
- 4.2 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart`

### Examples

*Figure: Daily shipments in April*

```
/* A month day by day, with its running total: daily shipments in April */
import { TrendChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart.css'

const shipped = [
  355, 375, 310, 510, 405, 430, 325, 305, 300, 285, 405, 455, 370, 295, 350, 445, 450, 395, 365, 335, 310, 360, 345, 285,
  485, 360, 365, 340, 330, 375,
]
const days = shipped.map((_, index) => `Apr ${index + 1}`)
const total = shipped.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)

export default function Trend() {
  return (
    <div style={{ width: 'min(100%, 560px)' }}>
      <TrendChart
        label={`Daily shipments in April, ${total.toLocaleString('en-US')} pallets in total`}
        categories={days}
        series={{ name: 'Shipments (plt)', values: shipped }}
        cumulative={{ name: 'Cumulative (plt)' }}
        unit="plt"
        axisLabels={[0, 14, days.length - 1]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- One series, and its running total when the month’s sum matters. Days still to come are null and leave the line open.
- Label three days on the axis: the first, the middle and the last.
- The width follows its container; the height is a prop.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA month day by day, with its key figure stated in text beside the chart.*

*Figure: Don’tThe chart alone: people have to read the line to find the figure they came for.*

*Figure: DoA series that is off keeps its name readable, with a hollow marker.*

*Figure: Don’tA faded series: its name drops below a readable contrast.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the chart and then its legend buttons. |
| Left and Right arrows | Read the previous or next day. |
| Home and End | Go to the first day or the last day with data. |
| Escape | Clears the day being read. |
| Enter or Space | On a legend button: shows or hides that series. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="group"` | Named by its label, with a hint to use the arrow keys. |
| `aria-live="polite"` | Reads the chosen day: “May 12: 350 plt, 4,485 plt so far”. |
| `aria-pressed` | Legend buttons say whether their series is shown. |

#### Notes

- The chart is a group with a live region: the day being read is announced with both values.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { TrendChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart.css'
```

### API

*Props of TrendChart*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  One sentence that sums the chart up, read first: “Daily shipments in May, 11,940 pallets in total”. | `string` | — |
| `categories` Required  The label of each point along the x axis, such as the days of the month. | `string[]` | — |
| `series` Required  The series drawn as a solid line. Missing points (null) leave a gap: days still to come. | `{ name: string; values: (number \| null)[] }` | — |
| `cumulative`  A second series drawn dotted against its own axis on the right: the running total of the first. | `{ name: string }` | — |
| `unit` Required  Unit of the values, after each figure in the tooltip. | `string` | — |
| `axisLabels`  Indices of the categories labeled on the x axis. | `number[]` | `first, middle and last` |
| `height`  Height of the chart in pixels, axes included. The width follows its container. | `number` | `200` |
| `className`  Classes added to the chart’s root element, after sonar-trend-chart. | `string` | — |

# Chart legend · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/chart-legend/

> Chart legend, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Chart legend

The key to a chart’s colors: a dot in each part’s tone, then its name, and its value when the chart has none of its own.

- Native HTML
- 0.9 KB gzipped · script and styles
- `@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend`

### Examples

*Figure: Names, and names with values*

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'

/* Names alone, under a chart that states its figures; or names with values, when the chart has none */
export default function Legend() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 20 }}>
      <ChartLegend
        items={[
          { label: 'Shipped', tone: 'accent' },
          { label: 'On hold', tone: 'strong' },
          { label: 'Pending', tone: 'muted' },
        ]}
      />
      <ChartLegend
        items={[
          { label: 'Overdue', tone: 'danger', value: '2,230,800 USD' },
          { label: 'Not due yet', tone: 'muted', value: '1,669,200 USD' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Under the chart, in the order of the chart’s parts.
- Hide it from assistive technology when the chart’s name already lists the parts.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoThe legend lists the parts in the order the chart draws them.*

*Figure: Don’tA legend in another order: the eye has to match colors back and forth.*

*Figure: DoValues in the legend when the chart has no figures of its own.*

*Figure: Don’tA legend for a single series: the title already names it.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | The legend is text, not a control. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<ul role="list">` | A list of names, read in the order of the chart’s parts. |
| `aria-hidden` | When the chart’s own name already lists the parts, the legend is hidden so they are not read twice. |
| Dots | Drawn; the name always says what the color stands for. |

#### Notes

- Every color has a name beside it, so no part depends on telling hues apart.

### Use it

Each component is its own entry point with its own stylesheet, so an app loads only what it uses. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend.css'
```

### API

*Props of ChartLegend*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` Required  One entry per color, in the order of the chart’s parts. | `ChartLegendItem[]` | — |

Also takes every attribute of the native `<ul>` , except children, and a `ref` to it.
