# Search field · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-field/

> Search field, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Search field

A search box whose results open under it as people type. Base UI’s Autocomplete provides the behavior; the app does the searching and passes the results, with a status line that says how the text was read.

- Behavior from Base UI
- 4.2 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Search result
- `@orbex/sonar-components/search`

### Examples

*Figure: Deliveries and invoices, in plain words*

```
/* The app reads the text and passes the results; SearchField shows them as people type */
import { SearchField, SearchResult } from '@orbex/sonar-components/search'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/search.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/status.css'
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

type Tone = 'neutral' | 'positive' | 'warning' | 'danger'
interface Item {
  id: string
  kind: 'Delivery' | 'Invoice'
  day: string
  text: string
  status: string
  tone: Tone
}

const items: Item[] = [
  { id: '04-127C', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Tue May 12', text: '04-127C 1 item · 15 plt', status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-121A', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Tue May 12', text: '04-121A 7 items · 150 plt', status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-133B', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Wed May 13', text: '04-133B 3 items · 60 plt', status: 'Scheduled', tone: 'neutral' },
  { id: 'INV-7712', kind: 'Invoice', day: 'Tue May 12', text: 'INV-7712 · 30,000 USD', status: 'Due today', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: 'INV-7716', kind: 'Invoice', day: 'Tue May 12', text: 'INV-7716 · 16,800 USD', status: 'Paid', tone: 'positive' },
]

/* The app’s own reading of the text: here, a kind, a state and a code */
function search(text: string) {
  const query = text.toLowerCase()
  const kind = /deliver/.test(query) ? 'Delivery' : /invoice/.test(query) ? 'Invoice' : null
  const late = /late|delay|overdue/.test(query)
  const words = query.split(/\s+/).filter((word) => /\d/.test(word))
  return items.filter(
    (item) =>
      (!kind || item.kind === kind) &&
      (!late || ['Delayed', 'Overdue'].includes(item.status)) &&
      words.every((word) => item.id.toLowerCase().includes(word)),
  )
}

export default function Basic() {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState<Item | null>(null)
  const [value, setValue] = useState('')
  const [results, setResults] = useState<Item[]>([])
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)

  /* Search after a short pause in typing, not on every key */
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!value.trim()) return setResults([])
    setBusy(true)
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setResults(search(value))
      setBusy(false)
    }, 380)
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [value])

  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12, width: '100%', maxWidth: 480 }}>
    <SearchField
      label="Search orders, deliveries and invoices"
      placeholder="Search…"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      items={results}
      itemToString={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={(item) => (
        <SearchResult title={item.text} description={`${item.kind} · ${item.day}`} trailing={<Status tone={item.tone}>{item.status}</Status>} />
      )}
      onItemChoose={(item) => {
        setValue('')
        setOpened(item)
      }}
      status={busy ? `Understanding “${value}”…` : `${results.length} results for “${value}”`}
      busy={busy}
      empty="No results. Try “late deliveries” or “INV-77”."
    />
    <p aria-live="polite" style={{ margin: 0, font: 'var(--sonar-type-body-md)' }}>
      {opened ? `Opened ${opened.kind.toLowerCase()} ${opened.id}.` : 'Type “late”, “invoices” or “127”.'}
    </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Always controlled: the app keeps the text and decides the results. Search after a short pause in typing, not on every key.
- Return `true` from `onItemChoose` to keep the list open, as a suggestion that fills the field does.
- Draw each result with [Search result](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-result/). The whole pattern, with its rules, is in [Patterns › Search](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/search/).
- In the app’s top bar, use `variant="top-bar"`: no box of its own, it fills the bar’s 39 px search pill with a 22 px icon, 12 px text and an 18 px clear mark, as in the product. On touch screens its text is 16 px drawn at three quarters, so it looks the same and iOS does not zoom in when it takes focus. `icon` and `clearIcon` take the app’s own marks.
- The first result is highlighted whenever the list opens or changes, so Enter takes it at once. Escape clears the text first and keeps the list (now the suggestions); a second Escape closes it.
- `statusIcon` draws a mark in the status line’s 28 px accent circle (the sparkle of a smart search). `popupClassName`, `align` and `popupWidth` place and size the results from the app, such as as wide as the pill on a desktop, or the window less 12 px each side on a phone.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoIn a top bar: the magnifier and an example as placeholder; the label stays for screen readers.*

*Figure: Don’tInstructions as placeholder: long, cut off, and gone at the first key.*

*Figure: DoAn empty result suggests a query that works.*

*Figure: Don’t“No results” and nothing else: a dead end.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Searches; the list opens under the field with the results, the first one highlighted. |
| Down and Up arrows | Move through the results while focus stays in the field. |
| Enter | Chooses the highlighted result. |
| Escape | Closes the list; again, clears the field. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="combobox" on the input` | With aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant: the highlighted result is read as focus moves, without leaving the field. |
| `role="status"` | The status line is announced politely: that the search is running, then how the text was read and how many results there are. |
| `aria-busy` | On the field and the list while results are on their way. |
| Label | Always present for assistive technology, drawn only with showLabel. |

#### Notes

- The input carries its name itself: while the list is open, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology.

### Use it

Search field shares its entry point and stylesheet with Search result. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { SearchField } from '@orbex/sonar-components/search'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/search.css'
```

### API

*Props of SearchField*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` Required  What is searched, read by assistive technology: “Search orders, deliveries and invoices”. | `string` | — |
| `showLabel`  Whether the label is drawn above the field. In a top bar the icon and the placeholder say what it is. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `placeholder`  An example of what to type, never a label. | `string` | — |
| `value` Required  The text in the field. The field is always controlled. | `string` | — |
| `onValueChange` Required  Called with the new text as people type or clear the field; not when a result is chosen. | `(value: string) => void` | — |
| `items` Required  The results for the current text, or suggestions while the field is empty. | `Item[]` | — |
| `itemToString` Required  The text of an item: its key, and what is announced when it is highlighted. | `(item: Item) => string` | — |
| `renderItem` Required  Draws one result, usually as a SearchResult. | `(item: Item) => ReactNode` | — |
| `onItemChoose` Required  Called when a result is chosen, by click or with Enter. Return true to keep the list open with the field focused, as when a suggestion fills the field with its text. | `(item: Item) => boolean \| void` | — |
| `status`  A line at the top of the list, announced politely: how the text was read, or that the search is running. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `busy`  While the results are on their way: the field says so and the list keeps the previous results out of reach. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `empty`  Shown when the text has no results. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `busyIcon`  Icon shown while busy, instead of the magnifier. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `size`  Medium in a top bar; small inside a card or a panel. | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` |
| `className`  Classes added to the field’s wrapper, after sonar-search. | `string` | — |
| `variant`  `field`: the outlined box. `top-bar`: the product’s top-bar search (v38): no box of its own, it fills the app bar’s search pill (39 px), with a 22 px icon, 12 px text and an 18 px clear mark. On touch screens its text is 16 px drawn at three quarters, so it looks the same and iOS does not zoom in. | `'field' \| 'top-bar'` | `'field'` |
| `icon`  Replaces the magnifier, such as the app’s own icon font glyph. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `clearIcon`  Replaces the clear mark. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `statusIcon`  Drawn before the status line as the 28 px accent circle: what reads the text (an AI sparkle). | `ReactNode` | — |
| `popupClassName`  Classes added to the results popup, to place or size it from the app. | `string` | — |
| `align`  Where the results line up with the field. | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'start'` |
| `popupWidth`  Width of the results: `anchor` is the field’s width, `auto` the field’s width but at least 320 px, or any CSS length (`calc(100vw - 24px)`). | `'auto' \| 'anchor' \| string` | `'auto'` |

---

# Search result · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-result/

> Search result, a component of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System: examples, guidance, accessibility and API.

## Search result

One row of results: an icon for the kind of thing, a title, a line under it with the kind and the day, and its state at the end.

- Behavior from Base UI
- 4.2 KB gzipped · script and styles
- Shared with Search field
- `@orbex/sonar-components/search`

### Examples

*Figure: A delivery, an invoice and a page*

```
import { SearchResult } from '@orbex/sonar-components/search'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import receiptSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/receipt_long.svg?raw'
import shippingSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/local_shipping.svg?raw'
import tuneSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/tune.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const ReceiptIcon = symbol(receiptSymbol)
const ShippingIcon = symbol(shippingSymbol)
const TuneIcon = symbol(tuneSymbol)

/* Results as SearchField draws them: what it is, when, and its state; a page has its section instead. Here in a
   plain list, for reference */
export default function Results() {
  return (
    <ul role="list" style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 4, width: '100%', maxWidth: 420, padding: 0 }}>
      <li className="sonar-search-item">
        <SearchResult icon={<ShippingIcon />} title="04-127C 1 item · 15 plt" description="Delivery · Tue May 12" trailing={<Status tone="warning">Delayed</Status>} />
      </li>
      <li className="sonar-search-item">
        <SearchResult icon={<ReceiptIcon />} title="INV-7712 · 30,000 USD" description="Invoice · Tue May 12" trailing={<Status tone="warning">Due today</Status>} />
      </li>
      <li className="sonar-search-item">
        <SearchResult icon={<TuneIcon />} title="Editing the overview" description="Page · Patterns" />
      </li>
    </ul>
  )
}
```

### Usage

- Return it from the search field’s `renderItem`; the field makes it an option of its list.
- Title: the code and its key figure. Description: the kind and the day. Trailing: a Status, in words.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoWhat it is, when it is and its state: an icon, a line under the title and a status.*

*Figure: Don’tA bare code: people cannot tell which result they want.*

*Figure: DoThe state in words, with Status.*

*Figure: Don’tThe state as colored text: too faint on the menu surface, and lost without color.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | A result is chosen through the search field: arrows and Enter. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="option"` | Each result is an option of the list, read by its text. |
| Icon | aria-hidden: the description says what kind of result it is. |
| Trailing Status | Read after the description, in words. |

#### Notes

- The icon is hidden; the description already says what kind of result it is.

### Use it

Search result shares its entry point and stylesheet with Search field. The tokens and the cascade layers are set once for the app: see [Installation](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/get-started/installation/).

 tsx

```
import { SearchResult } from '@orbex/sonar-components/search'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/search.css'
```

### API

*Props of SearchResult*

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon`  What kind of thing it is, as an icon: a truck for a delivery, a receipt for an invoice. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `title` Required  The result itself, on one line: a code and its key figure, such as “04-127C 12 items · 6 plt”. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `description`  A second line: the kind of result and when it is. | `ReactNode` | — |
| `trailing`  At the end of the row, such as a Status dot. | `ReactNode` | — |

# Overview · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/overview/

> The Sonar-DB overview: the six default cards composed on the grid, live, and the rules that keep it legible at every width.

## Overview

The six cards of the default overview on the grid, live, with the figures of one day: Tuesday, May 12, 2026. Change a unit, turn a week, read a day of shipments; narrow the window and the columns follow the reading order of the desktop layout.

### Live

*Figure: The default overview*

```
/* The overview: cards on a grid of columns, each as tall as its size. The grid tokens follow the window */
import { Card, CardLink } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'

const columns = [
  [
    { id: 'orders', title: 'Orders', size: 'm', figure: ['Open total', '3,940 plt'] },
    { id: 'inventory', title: 'Inventory', size: 's', figure: ['Total', '2,800 plt'] },
  ],
  [
    { id: 'deliveries', title: 'Deliveries', size: 'l', figure: null },
    { id: 'balance', title: 'Balance', size: 'm', figure: ['Balance', '3,900,000 USD'] },
  ],
  [
    { id: 'shipments', title: 'Daily shipments', size: 'xl', figure: ['Month to date', '4,485 plt'] },
    { id: 'recurring', title: 'Recurring orders', size: 'l', figure: null },
  ],
] as const

export function Overview() {
  return (
    <div
      style={{
        display: 'grid',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(var(--sonar-layout-columns), minmax(0, 1fr))',
        gap: 'var(--sonar-layout-gap)',
        alignItems: 'start',
      }}
    >
      {columns.map((cards, index) => (
        <div key={index} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--sonar-layout-gap)' }}>
          {cards.map(({ id, title, size, figure }) => (
            <Card key={id} id={`card-${id}`} title={title} size={size} summary={figure ? { label: figure[0], value: figure[1] } : undefined} footer={<CardLink href={`/${id}`}>Go to {title}</CardLink>}>
              {/* The card’s content */}
            </Card>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Rules

- **One overview, arranged once.** People arrange it on a desktop; tablets and phones read that arrangement in order. See [Breakpoints and grid](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/grid/).
- **Columns end level.** Card heights are chosen so that M + L = S + XL, and the default overview keeps a straight bottom edge.
- **What matters most goes first.** Orders and Daily shipments open the reading order because they are what people check every morning.
- **Every card leads somewhere.** The overview never becomes the place where work is done; it says where to go.
- **Units are per card.** Pallets, kilograms or items are chosen in each card, because each team counts differently.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoWhat people check first goes first: Orders and Daily shipments open the reading order.*

*Figure: Don’tColumns that end at different heights: the overview looks unfinished.*

*Figure: DoEach card answers one question and leads to the page where the work is done.*

*Figure: Don’tA card that tries to be the page: tables, filters and bulk actions.*

---

# Cards · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/

> The cards of the Sonar-DB overview: their anatomy, sizes, states and rules, the six cards of the default overview and the five optional ones, live.

## Cards

The overview is made of cards. Each sums up one part of the business, a figure first and the detail after, and leads to the page where the work is done. They are built only from the system’s components and tokens: Card, Card link, Card scroll and Unit menu, with the charts.

### Anatomy

1. **Title**, which also names the card as a region of the page.
2. **Unit menu**: the card’s only setting, the unit its figures are shown in. Changing it converts every figure in the card. See [Unit menu](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/unit-menu/).
3. **Summary**: one figure that sums the card up, a label and a value over a rule.
4. **Content**: the detail, at most two levels deep: sections with a small heading, rows, a chart.
5. **Scrolling list**, optional: the part of the content that gives way first when the size leaves no room. See [Card scroll](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-scroll/).
6. **Footer**: the way to the full page, and at most one action, such as New order. See [Card link](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-link/).

#### In edit mode

1. **Move handle**: a pill centered on the top edge. Drag it to move the card; with the keyboard, Space picks the card up and drops it.
2. **Remove**: a red ring outside the top end corner. The card leaves the overview and can be added back from New element.
3. **Dashed edge** in accent: the card is part of a draft until Save layout.
4. **Resize handle**: a pill centered on the bottom edge. Pull it, or use the up and down arrows, to step through the sizes the card offers.
5. **Size**: S, M, L or XL, in a ring beside the resize handle.

### The six cards of the overview

*Figure: Orders · M*

```
/* Orders, size M: the open total, two months as tick bars, New order and the way to the Orders page */
import { Card, CardLink, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar.css'
import addCircle from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/add_circle.svg?raw'
import { useState } from 'react'

const AddIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d={addCircle.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]} />
  </svg>
)

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420 }

const months = [
  { month: 'May 2026', shipped: 1420, onHold: 80, pending: 1100 },
  { month: 'June 2026', shipped: 0, onHold: 160, pending: 2600 },
]
const parts = [
  { key: 'shipped', label: 'Shipped', tone: 'accent' },
  { key: 'onHold', label: 'On hold', tone: 'strong' },
  { key: 'pending', label: 'Pending', tone: 'muted' },
] as const

export function OrdersCard({ onNewOrder }: { onNewOrder: () => void }) {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  const format = (pallets: number) => `${(pallets * perPallet[unit]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`
  const open = months.reduce((sum, { onHold, pending }) => sum + onHold + pending, 0)
  return (
    <Card
      title="Orders"
      size="m"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />}
      summary={{ label: 'Open total', value: format(open) }}
      footer={<CardLink href="/orders">Go to Orders</CardLink>}
    >
      {months.map((month) => (
        <section key={month.month} aria-label={month.month} style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, marginBottom: 16 }}>
          <h3 style={{ margin: 0, font: 'var(--sonar-type-label-md)' }}>{month.month}</h3>
          <TickBar
            label={`${month.month} orders`}
            format={format}
            segments={parts.map(({ key, label, tone }) => ({ label, tone, value: month[key] }))}
          />
        </section>
      ))}
      <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={parts.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between', marginTop: 16 }}>
        <span>New order</span>
        <IconButton variant="tonal" label="New order" icon={<AddIcon />} aria-haspopup="dialog" onClick={onNewOrder} />
      </div>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Inventory · S*

```
/* Inventory, size S: the total, and on hold against available as a ring */
import { Card, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { RingChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart.css'
import { useState } from 'react'

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420 }
const stock = { available: 1960, onHold: 840 }

export function InventoryCard() {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  const format = (pallets: number) => `${(pallets * perPallet[unit]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`
  const parts = [
    { label: 'On hold', tone: 'danger', value: stock.onHold },
    { label: 'Available', tone: 'muted', value: stock.available },
  ] as const
  return (
    <Card
      title="Inventory"
      size="s"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />}
      summary={{ label: 'Total', value: format(stock.available + stock.onHold) }}
    >
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '1fr auto 1fr', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
        <p>{format(stock.onHold)}<br />On hold</p>
        <RingChart label="Inventory" direction="counterclockwise" format={format} segments={[...parts]} style={{ width: 96 }} />
        <p style={{ textAlign: 'end' }}>{format(stock.available)}<br />Available</p>
      </div>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Daily shipments · XL*

```
/* Daily shipments, size XL: the month to date, its key figures and the month’s line */
import { Card, CardLink, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { TrendChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart.css'
import { useState } from 'react'

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420 }

/* May up to the 12th: the days still to come are null and leave the line open */
const shipped = [320, 410, 360, 300, 455, 385, 290, 430, 470, 345, 370, 350]
const days = Array.from({ length: 31 }, (_, index) => `May ${index + 1}`)
const values = days.map((_, index) => shipped[index] ?? null)

export function ShipmentsCard() {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  const inUnit = (pallets: number) => pallets * perPallet[unit]!
  const format = (pallets: number) => `${inUnit(pallets).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`
  const total = shipped.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
  const stats = [
    ['Today', shipped.at(-1)!],
    ['Yesterday', shipped.at(-2)!],
    ['This month', total],
    ['Returns', 40],
  ] as const
  return (
    <Card
      title="Daily shipments"
      size="xl"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />}
      summary={{ label: 'Month to date', value: format(total) }}
      footer={<CardLink href="/shipments">Go to Shipments</CardLink>}
    >
      <dl style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, 1fr)', gap: 8 }}>
        {stats.map(([term, value]) => (
          <div key={term}>
            <dt>{term}</dt>
            <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>{format(value)}</dd>
          </div>
        ))}
      </dl>
      <TrendChart
        label={`Daily shipments in May 2026, ${format(total)} so far`}
        categories={days}
        series={{ name: `Shipments (${unit})`, values: values.map((value) => (value === null ? null : inUnit(value))) }}
        cumulative={{ name: `Cumulative (${unit})` }}
        unit={unit}
        axisLabels={[0, 14, days.length - 1]}
      />
    </Card>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Balance · M*

```
/* Balance, size M: the balance, its overdue share as a tick bar, and the invoices due today */
import { Card, CardLink, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/status.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar.css'
import { useState } from 'react'

const currencies = [
  { value: 'USD', short: 'USD', name: 'US dollars' },
  { value: 'EUR', short: 'EUR', name: 'Euros' },
]
const perDollar: Record<string, number> = { USD: 1, EUR: 0.92 }
const balance = { total: 3_900_000, overdue: 2_230_800 }
/* The invoices due today */
const today = [
  { id: 'INV-7712', amount: 30_000, status: 'Due today', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: 'INV-7716', amount: 16_800, status: 'Paid', tone: 'positive' },
] as const

export function BalanceCard() {
  const [currency, setCurrency] = useState('USD')
  const format = (dollars: number) => `${Math.round(dollars * perDollar[currency]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${currency}`
  const parts = [
    { label: 'Overdue', tone: 'danger', value: balance.overdue },
    { label: 'Not due yet', tone: 'muted', value: balance.total - balance.overdue },
  ] as const
  return (
    <Card
      title="Balance"
      size="m"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Currency" value={currency} options={currencies} onValueChange={setCurrency} />}
      summary={{ label: 'Balance', value: format(balance.total) }}
      footer={<CardLink href="/balance">Go to Balance</CardLink>}
    >
      <TickBar label="Overdue share of the balance" format={format} segments={[...parts]} />
      <ChartLegend items={parts.map(({ label, tone, value }) => ({ label, tone, value: format(value) }))} aria-hidden="true" />
      <ul role="list" style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, marginTop: 16, padding: 0 }}>
        {today.map(({ id, amount, tone, status }) => (
          <li key={id} style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', gap: 12 }}>
            <span>{id}</span>
            <span>{format(amount)}</span>
            <Status tone={tone}>{status}</Status>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

*Figure: Deliveries · L*

```
/* Deliveries, size L: the deliveries of the chosen day, in a list that scrolls first when the card runs out of room */
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Card, CardLink, CardScroll, UnitMenu } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/button.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/menu.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/status.css'
import { useState } from 'react'

const units = [
  { value: 'plt', short: 'plt', name: 'Pallets' },
  { value: 'kg', short: 'kg', name: 'Kilograms' },
]
const perPallet: Record<string, number> = { plt: 1, kg: 420 }

const deliveries = [
  { id: '04-118B', items: 2, pallets: 40, status: 'Delivered', tone: 'positive' },
  { id: '04-121A', items: 7, pallets: 150, status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-127C', items: 1, pallets: 15, status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-130A', items: 8, pallets: 210, status: 'Delivered', tone: 'positive' },
] as const

export function DeliveriesCard({ onView }: { onView: (id: string) => void }) {
  const [unit, setUnit] = useState('plt')
  const format = (pallets: number) => `${(pallets * perPallet[unit]!).toLocaleString('en-US')} ${unit}`
  return (
    <Card
      title="Deliveries"
      size="l"
      actions={<UnitMenu label="Unit" value={unit} options={units} onValueChange={setUnit} />}

              <span style={{ flex: 1 }}>
                {id} · {items} {items === 1 ? 'item' : 'items'} · {format(pallets)}
              </span>
              <Status tone={tone}>{status}</Status>

                View
              </Button>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </CardScroll>
    </Card>
  )
}

*Figure: Recurring orders · L*

```
/* Recurring orders, size L: the products ordered most often, to choose and reorder in one step */
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Card, CardLink, CardScroll } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { Checkbox } from '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/button.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/card.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/checkbox.css'
import { useState } from 'react'

const products = [
  { code: 'CB-4030', name: 'Corrugated box / Double wall', stock: 380 },
  { code: 'SF-2300', name: 'Stretch film 23 µm', stock: 560 },
  { code: 'KP-1200', name: 'Kraft paper 120 g', stock: 210 },
  { code: 'EP-5050', name: 'Edge protector 50×50', stock: 940 },
  { code: 'CB-2010', name: 'Corrugated box / Single wall', stock: 640 },
]

export function RecurringCard({ onReorder }: { onReorder: (codes: string[]) => void }) {
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState(['CB-4030'])
  const toggle = (code: string, on: boolean) => setChosen((current) => (on ? [...current, code] : current.filter((other) => other !== code)))
  return (
    <Card
      title="Recurring orders"
      size="l"
      footer={
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between', width: '100%' }}>
          <CardLink href="/market">Go to Orbex Market</CardLink>
          <Button disabled={chosen.length === 0} onClick={() => onReorder(chosen)}>
            Reorder
          </Button>
        </div>
      }
    >
      <CardScroll label="Products to reorder">
        <ul role="list" style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 12, padding: 0 }}>
          {products.map(({ code, name, stock }) => (
            <li key={code}>
              <Checkbox
                label={name}
                description={`Packaging ${code} · ${stock.toLocaleString('en-US')} plt in stock`}
                checked={chosen.includes(code)}
                onChange={(event) => toggle(code, event.currentTarget.checked)}
              />
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </CardScroll>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

  The layout styles the cards share

/* Layout inside the overview cards. Only arrangement lives here: every color, type and size comes from the
   components and the tokens. */

@import './typography.css';

/* ---------- Card tokens ----------
   Distances inside the cards are steps of the spacing scale. A few values are not, because a card's rhythm depends on
   them; each is named here with its reason, and nothing else in this file uses a bare distance. */
.sonar-card {
  /* Deliveries and Balance: a row of a day is 38 px between rules, one line of 14 px text, so its air is 11.5 px
     above and below. Rows of every card line up with it */
  --card-row-height: 38px;
  --card-row-line: 14px;
  --card-row-air: calc((var(--card-row-height) - var(--card-row-line) - 1px) / 2);
  /* Deliveries: the band that holds the chosen day between two rules. 41 px gives the date the same air as a row,
     and the rules stay put while the rows scroll */
  --card-day-band: 41px;
  /* Recurring orders: one distance between anything and its rule, so a product row is 80 px: 13 + 54 + 13 */
  --card-list-rhythm: 13px;
  --card-thumbnail: 54px;
}

### Optional cards

Five more modules can join the overview, from New element while editing or from [All modules](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/customize/): Invoices, Credit notes, Notifications, Latest documents and Scheduled orders. They come in one size, L (405 px), and are built like the six: a title, a list that scrolls between header and footer, and a link to their page. A new module goes to the foot of the shortest column.

*Figure: Invoices · L*

*Figure: Credit notes · L*

*Figure: Notifications · L*

*Figure: Latest documents · L*

*Figure: Scheduled orders · L*

### Sizes

In the overview a card is 245, 375, 405 or 535 px high and as wide as its column. Each card is designed for the sizes where its content reads well, and offers only those when people edit the overview. A larger size shows more of the same content, never different content.

*Figure: Orders · S, M*

```
<OrdersCard size="s" />
<OrdersCard size="m" />
```

*Figure: Inventory · S, M*

```
<InventoryCard size="s" />
<InventoryCard size="m" />
```

*Figure: Balance · S, M, L*

```
<BalanceCard size="s" />
<BalanceCard size="m" />
<BalanceCard size="l" />
```

*Figure: Daily shipments · L, XL*

```
<ShipmentsCard size="l" />
<ShipmentsCard size="xl" />
```

*Figure: Deliveries · M, L, XL*

```
<DeliveriesCard size="m" />
<DeliveriesCard size="l" />
<DeliveriesCard size="xl" />
```

*Figure: Recurring orders · M, L, XL*

```
<RecurringCard size="m" />
<RecurringCard size="l" />
<RecurringCard size="xl" />
```

### States

At rest a card is a region with its own controls. While the overview is edited it gains a dashed edge, a handle to move it, a button to remove it and a handle to resize it; it lifts while it is dragged and leaves a drop placeholder where it will land. The live version is in [Editing the overview](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/editing/#desktop).

*Figure: A card while the overview is edited, in light and dark*

- **Edit**: a 1 px dashed edge in accent. The handles are pills of 36 × 16 px with an accent ring on the card’s surface; remove is a 22 px ring in danger outside the top end corner. Each is a button with a name: “Move Orders”, “Remove Orders from the overview”, “Resize Orders”.
- **Hover and focus** fill the handle with accent and turn its icon to on-accent; remove fills with danger.
- **Lifted**: the card rises to elevation 4 at 103 % and loses its dashed edge, and its move handle stays solid while it is held.
- **Drop placeholder**: the slot the card leaves, as tall as the card, with a dashed accent edge on the accent container.
- **Resizing** steps through the sizes the card offers, never in between. A label over the handle names the size and its height, and says when the columns end level.

*Figure: The unit menu and the card link*

### Rules

- **A figure first.** The summary says the one number someone opens the overview for; the content explains it.
- **Figures align.** They use tabular numerals, and a figure keeps its unit beside it: 1,420 plt, never a bare 1,420.
- **Status in words.** Rows show state with the Status component, a dot and a word, never color alone.
- **A card summarizes; the page acts.** Long tasks open their panel or page; the card keeps at most one action.
- **Header and footer stay put.** When content does not fit a size, it scrolls between them: a list marked with CardScroll gives way first (the deliveries of a day, the products to reorder), and the whole content scrolls only if that is not enough. A fade at the edge says there is more; a thin indicator shows while scrolling.
- **Days of another month are not shown** in a card’s month grid: their cells stay empty. The week strip runs on across months, since the chosen day always sits in its middle.
- **A card that opens grows.** The month view of a calendar and the payment calendar of Balance take the height they need; they fold back to the card’s size.
- **Rows open their details beside the overview.** View, New order and Reorder open a side panel; the row whose details are open stays marked.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoA figure keeps its unit beside it, in tabular numerals.*

*Figure: Don’tA bare figure: pallets, kilograms or items?*

*Figure: DoDays of another month are left empty in a month grid.*

*Figure: Don’tDays of the months around it, grayed out: they read as days with nothing on them.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the card’s controls in reading order: unit menu, content, footer. |
| Unit menu | Opens with Enter, Space or Down arrow, like any menu. |
| Up and Down arrows, Page Up and Page Down | On content that scrolls, once it has focus: scroll it. It takes focus only while it scrolls. |
| Left and Right arrows | On the chosen day of a calendar (Deliveries, Payment calendar): the previous or next day. In the month, Up and Down move a week. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `<section aria-labelledby>` | Each card is a region named by its title, so the overview can be read card by card. Where the same card shows twice, label names each copy: “Orders, size S”. |
| Unit menu | Named with what it shows and what that means: “Unit: plt, Pallets”, so voice control can reach it by its visible text. Its choices are a group of radio items. |
| Summary bar | The bar between label and value is drawn, so it is never read aloud. |
| `role="group" while scrolling` | Content that scrolls is a group named by its list (“Deliveries of May 12”) or by the card’s title, so focus arriving on it says what it is. The fade and the indicator are drawn and hidden. |

#### Notes

- Buttons repeated in rows carry names that say what they act on: “View delivery 04-127C”, not “View” six times.
- What changes when a step button is used is announced: the day of a delivery list, the due date in Balance, the month in Daily shipments.
- The faded next day in Deliveries (XL, and the month view) is a preview: it is hidden from assistive technology and takes no focus.
- In the week strip only the chosen day is in the tab order; the arrow keys move the day and focus follows it. Each day is named in full: “Saturday, May 16, no deliveries”.
- Where the same card shows in several sizes, as on this page, each copy is named with its size, so no two regions share a name.
- See [Charts](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/charts/#accessibility) for the charts inside the cards.

### Built with

The cards are built from [Card](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card/), [Card link](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-link/), [Card scroll](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/card-scroll/) and [Unit menu](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/unit-menu/), with [Tick bar](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tick-bar/), [Ring chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/ring-chart/), [Trend chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/trend-chart/) and [Chart legend](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/chart-legend/). Each page has its API.

---

# Charts · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/charts/

> The three chart shapes of the Sonar-DB overview: tick bars, ring charts and the trend chart, with the legend they share and their rules.

## Charts

Three shapes cover the overview: a tick bar for a share, a ring for the parts of a whole, a line for a month day by day, and one legend for all of them. They are drawn in SVG and CSS with the chart roles of the tokens; no charting library.

### Tick bar

One row of fine ticks, each part in its share of the width and in its chart role. The parts meet without a gap, and a legend under the bar names each color.

*Figure: Orders of a month, and an overdue share*

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { TickBar } from '@orbex/sonar-components/tick-bar'

const orders = [
  { value: 1420, tone: 'accent', label: 'Shipped' },
  { value: 80, tone: 'strong', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1100, tone: 'muted', label: 'Pending' },
] as const

const balance = [
  { value: 2_230_800, tone: 'danger', label: 'Overdue' },
  { value: 1_669_200, tone: 'muted', label: 'Not due yet' },
] as const

const plt = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} plt`
const usd = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} USD`

export default function TickBars() {
  return (
    <div className="chart-demo" data-shape="bars">
      <figure>
        <figcaption>May orders</figcaption>
        <TickBar label="May orders" format={plt} segments={[...orders]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={orders.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
      <figure>
        <figcaption>Overdue share of the balance</figcaption>
        <TickBar label="Overdue share of the balance" format={usd} segments={[...balance]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={balance.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Ring chart

Parts of a whole as a ring of 96 ticks, the Inventory donut. The hole can hold the total; the legend names each color.

*Figure: Two and three parts*

```
import { ChartLegend } from '@orbex/sonar-components/chart-legend'
import { RingChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/ring-chart'

const inventory = [
  { value: 840, tone: 'danger', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1960, tone: 'muted', label: 'Available' },
] as const

const orders = [
  { value: 1420, tone: 'accent', label: 'Shipped' },
  { value: 80, tone: 'strong', label: 'On hold' },
  { value: 1100, tone: 'muted', label: 'Pending' },
] as const

const plt = (value: number) => `${value.toLocaleString('en-US')} plt`

export default function Rings() {
  return (
    <div className="chart-demo" data-shape="rings">
      <figure>
        <figcaption>Inventory</figcaption>
        <RingChart label="Inventory" format={plt} style={{ width: 128 }} segments={[...inventory]} />
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={inventory.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
      <figure>
        <figcaption>May orders</figcaption>
        <RingChart label="May orders" format={plt} style={{ width: 160 }} segments={[...orders]}>
          <span className="ring-total">
            <strong>2,600</strong>
            <span>plt</span>
          </span>
        </RingChart>
        <ChartLegend aria-hidden="true" items={orders.map(({ label, tone }) => ({ label, tone }))} />
      </figure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Trend chart

A month day by day as a line, with its running total dotted against a second axis. The legend turns each series off and on; hovering, touching or the arrow keys read a day.

*Figure: Daily shipments in April*

```
/* A month day by day, with its running total: daily shipments in April */
import { TrendChart } from '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/trend-chart.css'

const shipped = [
  355, 375, 310, 510, 405, 430, 325, 305, 300, 285, 405, 455, 370, 295, 350, 445, 450, 395, 365, 335, 310, 360, 345, 285,
  485, 360, 365, 340, 330, 375,
]
const days = shipped.map((_, index) => `Apr ${index + 1}`)
const total = shipped.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)

export default function Trend() {
  return (
    <div style={{ width: 'min(100%, 560px)' }}>
      <TrendChart
        label={`Daily shipments in April, ${total.toLocaleString('en-US')} pallets in total`}
        categories={days}
        series={{ name: 'Shipments (plt)', values: shipped }}
        cumulative={{ name: 'Cumulative (plt)' }}
        unit="plt"
        axisLabels={[0, 14, days.length - 1]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Rules

- **Color by role.** The first series in accent, the second in the strong neutral, the rest of a whole in the rest tone, alerts in danger. Never a hue that means nothing.
- **A series that is off keeps its name readable.** It drops to the tertiary level at full opacity and its marker turns hollow; it is never faded.
- **Figures in the data role**, the mono face at 10 px, with tabular numerals; gridlines dotted and quiet.
- **Labels beside the chart, not inside it.** The card states the key figures in text; the chart shows their shape.
- **No animation on load.** A chart draws at once; values move only when the unit or the period changes.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoColor by role: the first part in accent, then strong, the rest in the rest tone.*

*Figure: Don’tWarning and danger for parts that are not alerts: the chart cries wolf.*

*Figure: DoLabels beside the chart: the card states the key figures in text.*

*Figure: Don’tA chart with no figure anywhere: its shape alone has to be decoded.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reaches the trend chart and its legend buttons. Tick bars and rings take no focus. |
| Left and Right arrows | In the trend chart: read the previous or next day. |
| Home and End | Go to the first day or the last day with data. |
| Escape | Clears the day being read. |
| Enter or Space | On a legend button: shows or hides that series. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="img" with aria-label` | Tick bars and rings: one name lists every part with its value. |
| `role="group"` | The trend chart, named by its label with a hint to use the arrow keys. |
| `aria-live="polite"` | The trend chart reads the chosen day: “May 12: 350 plt, 4,485 plt so far”. |
| `aria-pressed` | Legend buttons say whether their series is shown. |
| Chart legend | aria-hidden when the chart’s own name already lists the parts, as in every demo here. |

#### Notes

- A chart is never the only way to a figure: the card states its key figures in text beside it.
- Color is never the only cue: a legend names every color, and a series that is off keeps its name readable.
- The parts of one chart differ in lightness as well as hue (accent, strong and rest; or danger and rest), so they stay distinct without color vision.

### Chart roles

*Figure: The tones, as a tick bar and in the legend*

*Chart roles*

| Token | Preview | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sonar-color-chart-primary`  First series. |  | accent `#1A8838` | accent `#76B27C` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-secondary`  Second series (cumulative). |  | palette.black `#000000` | palette.neutral-dark.90 `#DCE5D9` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-alert`  Values that need attention, such as stock on hold. |  | danger `#DD3535` | danger `#F04B4B` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-rest`  Remainder of a whole: the rest of a donut or bar. |  | palette.neutral.76 `#B5BEB2` | palette.neutral-tinted.36 `#4C584A` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-grid`  Grid lines. |  | palette.neutral.90 `#DDE5D9` | palette.neutral.21 `#2D352C` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-axis`  Axis figures. |  | text.default `#2D352C` | text.default `#DDE5D9` |
| `--sonar-color-chart-tip-shadow`  The chart bubble’s drop shadow; none in dark, where the bubble is light. |  | palette.black `#0000001F` | palette.black `#00000000` |

### Built with

Each chart is its own component, with its API: [Tick bar](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/tick-bar/), [Ring chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/ring-chart/), [Trend chart](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/trend-chart/) and [Chart legend](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/chart-legend/). The trend chart has a budget of 4 KB instead of 3: it draws axes, two series, a legend and reading by pointer and keys.

---

# Search · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/search/

> Searching Sonar-DB in plain words: how a query is read, what the results show and how to reach them, with the search field it is built on.

## Search

One field in the top bar finds deliveries, invoices and actions. People type in plain words, “delayed deliveries this week” or “INV-77”, and the results open under the field as they type, with a line that says how the words were read.

### Try it

The data is the overview’s: every card reads Tuesday, May 12, 2026. Choose a delivery or an invoice to open its details, New order to open its panel, or a page to go to its card on the Overview. With the field empty, the list suggests a few questions.

*Figure: Smart search in the top bar*

```
/* Search in plain words: the app reads the text and passes the results; SearchField shows them as people type */
import { SearchField, SearchResult } from '@orbex/sonar-components/search'
import { Status } from '@orbex/sonar-components/status'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/search.css'
import '@orbex/sonar-components/status.css'
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

type Tone = 'neutral' | 'positive' | 'warning' | 'danger'
interface Item {
  id: string
  kind: 'Delivery' | 'Invoice'
  day: string
  text: string
  status: string
  tone: Tone
}

const items: Item[] = [
  { id: '04-127C', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Tue May 12', text: '04-127C 1 item · 15 plt', status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-121A', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Tue May 12', text: '04-121A 7 items · 150 plt', status: 'Delayed', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '04-133B', kind: 'Delivery', day: 'Wed May 13', text: '04-133B 3 items · 60 plt', status: 'Scheduled', tone: 'neutral' },
  { id: 'INV-7712', kind: 'Invoice', day: 'Tue May 12', text: 'INV-7712 · 30,000 USD', status: 'Due today', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: 'INV-7716', kind: 'Invoice', day: 'Tue May 12', text: 'INV-7716 · 16,800 USD', status: 'Paid', tone: 'positive' },
]

/* The app’s own reading of the text: here, a kind, a state and a code */
function search(text: string) {
  const query = text.toLowerCase()
  const kind = /deliver/.test(query) ? 'Delivery' : /invoice/.test(query) ? 'Invoice' : null
  const late = /late|delay|overdue/.test(query)
  const words = query.split(/\s+/).filter((word) => /\d/.test(word))
  return items.filter(
    (item) =>
      (!kind || item.kind === kind) &&
      (!late || ['Delayed', 'Overdue'].includes(item.status)) &&
      words.every((word) => item.id.toLowerCase().includes(word)),
  )
}

export function SmartSearch({ onOpen }: { onOpen: (item: Item) => void }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('')
  const [results, setResults] = useState<Item[]>([])
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)

  /* Search after a short pause in typing, not on every key */
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!value.trim()) return setResults([])
    setBusy(true)
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setResults(search(value))
      setBusy(false)
    }, 380)
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [value])

  return (
    <SearchField
      label="Search orders, deliveries and invoices"
      placeholder="Search…"
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      items={results}
      itemToString={(item) => item.id}
      renderItem={(item) => (
        <SearchResult title={item.text} description={`${item.kind} · ${item.day}`} trailing={<Status tone={item.tone}>{item.status}</Status>} />
      )}
      onItemChoose={(item) => {
        setValue('')
        onOpen(item)
      }}
      status={busy ? `Understanding “${value}”…` : `${results.length} results for “${value}”`}
      busy={busy}
      empty="No results. Try “late deliveries” or “INV-77”."
    />
  )
}
```

### How a query is read

The search listens for five things and ignores the rest of the sentence. What it understood goes in the status line above the results, so a wrong reading is visible at once: “Smart search · delayed deliveries · May 9 – May 15”.

| What | Words | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A kind | deliveries, shipment, pallets, truck · invoices, payment, bill, owe | Only deliveries, or only invoices |
| A state | late, delayed, overdue, unpaid, due · paid, delivered, done · upcoming, scheduled, soon | Needs attention, done, or still to come |
| A day or a week | today, tomorrow, yesterday, this week, last week, next week | A range of days around May 12 |
| A month | March, April, May, June | That month |
| A code | Any other word: 04-127, INV-77 | Codes that contain it |

### Anatomy

1. **Field**, in the top bar: a magnifier, the text and a button to clear it. While the search runs, the magnifier gives way to a pulsing spark.
2. **Status line**, at the top of the list: “Understanding …” while it runs, then how the text was read and, when there are more results than shown, how many.
3. **Results**: at most six deliveries and invoices, each with its kind, its day and its state in words.
4. **Actions** whose name matches, after the results: New order, Release stock, a page.
5. **Suggestions**, while the field is empty: questions to start from. Choosing one fills the field and searches.

### Rules

- **Nearest to today first.** Results run by their distance from today; at the same distance, what needs attention comes first.
- **Say what was understood.** The status line always shows the reading, so people can rephrase instead of guessing why a result is missing.
- **Wait for a pause.** The search runs after a short pause in typing (380 ms here), not on every key.
- **A result opens where the work is.** A delivery or an invoice opens its details panel; an action opens its panel or page. The field clears behind it.
- **No result is never a dead end.** The empty list says so and suggests a query that works.
- **State in words.** Results show their state with Status, as the cards do.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoSay how the text was read, so a wrong reading can be fixed at once.*

*Figure: Don’tResults with no reading: people guess why one is missing.*

*Figure: DoNearest to today first.*

*Figure: Don’tOldest first: today’s results sink under months of past ones.*

### Accessibility

#### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Searches; the list opens under the field with the results, the first one highlighted. |
| Down and Up arrows | Move through the results while focus stays in the field. |
| Enter | Chooses the highlighted result. |
| Escape | Closes the list; again, clears the field. |

#### Roles and attributes

| Element or attribute | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `role="combobox" on the input` | With aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant: the highlighted result is read as focus moves, without leaving the field. |
| `role="listbox" and role="option"` | The results; each is read by its text, its icon hidden. |
| `role="status"` | The status line is announced politely: that the search is running, then how the text was read and how many results there are. |
| `aria-busy` | On the field and the list while results are on their way. |
| Label | Always present for assistive technology, drawn only with showLabel. |

### Built with

The field is [Search field](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-field/), built on Base UI’s Autocomplete, and each row is a [Search result](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/search-result/) with a [Status](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/components/status/). The app does the searching: it passes the results for the current text and the status line.

---

# Editing the overview · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/editing/

> How people arrange the Sonar-DB overview: which cards it shows, where and at what size, on desktops, tablets and phones.

## Editing the overview

People choose which cards their overview shows, where, and at what size. On desktops and tablets they drag the cards themselves; on phones the overview becomes a list. Every edit is a draft until it is saved, and saving can be undone.

### As a list, on phones

*Figure: Edit layout on a phone*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { Switch } from '@orbex/sonar-components/switch'
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@orbex/sonar-components/toast'
import { useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent } from 'react'
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import dragSymbol from '@material-symbols/svg-400/rounded/drag_indicator.svg?raw'

/* Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, as icon components (Foundations › Icons) */
const symbol = (svg: string) => {
  const path = svg.match(/ d="([^"]+)"/)?.[1]
  return (props: ComponentProps<'svg'>) => (
    <svg viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" {...props}>
      <path d={path} />
    </svg>
  )
}

const DragIcon = symbol(dragSymbol)

/*
 * Edit layout on a phone: the overview becomes a list. Each row is one line: a grip to drag it, the card’s name, its
 * sizes and a switch to show or hide it. Hidden cards wait in a list of their own. Reset to default, Cancel and Save
 * layout stay at the foot.
 */

type Size = 'S' | 'M' | 'L' | 'XL'
export interface Entry {
  id: string
  title: string
  size: Size
  sizes: Size[]
  hidden?: boolean
}

const reducedMotion = () => matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches

const HEIGHTS: Record<Size, number> = { S: 245, M: 375, L: 405, XL: 535 }

/* The default overview in reading order, then the cards that can be added */
const DEFAULT: Entry[] = [
  { id: 'orders', title: 'Orders', size: 'M', sizes: ['S', 'M'] },
  { id: 'shipments', title: 'Daily shipments', size: 'XL', sizes: ['L', 'XL'] },
  { id: 'balance', title: 'Balance', size: 'M', sizes: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
  { id: 'deliveries', title: 'Deliveries', size: 'L', sizes: ['M', 'L', 'XL'] },
  { id: 'recurring', title: 'Recurring orders', size: 'L', sizes: ['M', 'L', 'XL'] },
  { id: 'inventory', title: 'Inventory', size: 'S', sizes: ['S', 'M'] },
  { id: 'notifications', title: 'Notifications', size: 'L', sizes: ['L'], hidden: true },
  { id: 'invoices', title: 'Invoices', size: 'L', sizes: ['L'], hidden: true },
  { id: 'documents', title: 'Latest documents', size: 'L', sizes: ['L'], hidden: true },
  { id: 'credits', title: 'Credit notes', size: 'L', sizes: ['L'], hidden: true },
  { id: 'scheduled', title: 'Scheduled orders', size: 'L', sizes: ['L'], hidden: true },
]

export interface EditListProps {
  /** The list to edit (the app shell's phone passes its overview); the default overview otherwise */
  initial?: Entry[]
  /** Inside the app shell's phone: Save layout and Cancel hand the list back (null: canceled) instead of staying here */
  onDone?: (list: Entry[] | null) => void
  /** The scale the phone frame is drawn at; a finger's moves are divided by it */
  zoom?: number
}

function Editor({ initial = DEFAULT, onDone, zoom = 1 }: EditListProps) {
  const toast = useToast()
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(initial)
  const [list, setList] = useState(initial)
  /* A drag: the row follows the finger by y; the rows between its place and to slide by its height to make room */
  const [drag, setDrag] = useState<{ id: string; from: number; to: number; y: number; height: number } | null>(null)
  const [settle, setSettle] = useState<{ id: string; y: number } | null>(null)
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState<{ id: string; before: Entry[] } | null>(null)
  const [ask, setAsk] = useState<'reset' | 'discard' | null>(null)
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState('')
  const gesture = useRef<{ id: string; pointer: number; startY: number; from: number; centers: number[]; height: number; to: number; y: number; stop: () => void } | null>(null)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const shown = list.filter((entry) => !entry.hidden)
  const hidden = list.filter((entry) => entry.hidden)
  const dirty = JSON.stringify(list) !== JSON.stringify(saved)

  const setSize = (id: string, size: Size) => setList((current) => current.map((entry) => (entry.id === id ? { ...entry, size } : entry)))

  /* Showing a card puts it at the end of the shown ones; hiding it leaves it where it was */
  const toggle = (id: string, on: boolean) =>
    setList((current) => {
      const next = current.map((entry) => ({ ...entry }))
      const index = next.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === id)
      const [entry] = next.splice(index, 1)
      entry!.hidden = !on
      if (on) next.splice(next.reduce((last, other, at) => (other.hidden ? last : at), -1) + 1, 0, entry!)
      else next.splice(index, 0, entry!)
      return next
    })

  const moveTo = (id: string, place: number) =>
    setList((current) => {
      const visible = current.filter((entry) => !entry.hidden && entry.id !== id)
      visible.splice(Math.max(0, Math.min(place, visible.length)), 0, current.find((entry) => entry.id === id)!)
      return [...visible, ...current.filter((entry) => entry.hidden)]
    })

  /*
   * Pointer, with a finger or a mouse: the row lifts and follows; the others slide out of its way. The order only
   * changes when the row is let go, so nothing in the list moves under the finger while it holds the row. The gesture
   * ends however the browser ends it (up, cancel, lost capture, touchend) and always clears.
   */
  const end = (commit: boolean) => {
    const current = gesture.current
    if (!current) return
    gesture.current = null
    current.stop()
    const entry = list.find((other) => other.id === current.id)!
    if (commit && current.to !== current.from) {
      /* The row lands in its new place from where the finger left it */
      const offset = (current.to - current.from) * current.height
      moveTo(current.id, current.to)
      setSettle({ id: current.id, y: current.y - offset })
      setAnnouncement(`${entry.title} dropped at position ${current.to + 1} of ${shown.length}.`)
    } else {
      setSettle(current.y ? { id: current.id, y: current.y } : null)
      if (commit) setAnnouncement(`${entry.title} dropped at position ${current.from + 1} of ${shown.length}.`)
    }
    setDrag(null)
  }
  const onDown = (id: string) => (event: PointerEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    if (event.button !== 0 || gesture.current) return
    event.preventDefault()
    const handle = event.currentTarget
    handle.setPointerCapture?.(event.pointerId)
    const rows = [...(listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > .edit-list-row') ?? [])]
    const from = rows.findIndex((row) => row.dataset.rowId === id)
    const boxes = rows.map((row) => row.getBoundingClientRect())
    const height = boxes[from]?.height ?? 56
    const pointer = event.pointerId
    const move = (next: globalThis.PointerEvent) => {
      const current = gesture.current
      if (!current || next.pointerId !== current.pointer) return
      next.preventDefault()
      const y = next.clientY - current.startY
      const center = current.centers[current.from]! + y
      /* Its place: after every other row whose middle it has passed */
      const to = current.centers.reduce((place, other, index) => (index === current.from ? place : center > other ? place + 1 : place), 0)
      current.y = y
      current.to = to
      setDrag({ id, from: current.from, to, y, height: current.height })
    }
    const up = (next: globalThis.PointerEvent) => next.pointerId === pointer && end(next.type === 'pointerup')
    const lost = () => end(true)
    const touchEnd = (next: TouchEvent) => next.touches.length === 0 && end(true)
    window.addEventListener('pointermove', move, { passive: false })
    window.addEventListener('pointerup', up)
    window.addEventListener('pointercancel', up)
    window.addEventListener('touchend', touchEnd)
    window.addEventListener('touchcancel', touchEnd)
    handle.addEventListener('lostpointercapture', lost)
    gesture.current = {
      id,
      pointer,
      startY: event.clientY,
      from,
      centers: boxes.map((box) => box.top + box.height / 2),
      height,
      to: from,
      y: 0,
      stop: () => {
        window.removeEventListener('pointermove', move)
        window.removeEventListener('pointerup', up)
        window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', up)
        window.removeEventListener('touchend', touchEnd)
        window.removeEventListener('touchcancel', touchEnd)
        handle.removeEventListener('lostpointercapture', lost)
        if (handle.hasPointerCapture?.(pointer)) handle.releasePointerCapture(pointer)
      },
    }
    setSettle(null)
    setDrag({ id, from, to: from, y: 0, height })
  }
  /* A gesture still open when the list goes away is closed with it */
  useEffect(() => () => gesture.current?.stop(), [])
  /* A document-wide touchmove listener, in place before a finger lands, refuses the page's scroll while a row is held:
     iOS only lets a move be cancelled when such a listener exists as the touch starts (1.0.0-alpha.21, as EditCards) */
  useEffect(() => {
    const hold = (event: TouchEvent) => {
      if (gesture.current && event.cancelable) event.preventDefault()
    }
    document.addEventListener('touchmove', hold, { passive: false })
    return () => document.removeEventListener('touchmove', hold)
  }, [])
  /* Let go: the row glides from under the finger into its slot, then drops its lift */
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (!settle) return
    const row = listRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-row-id="${settle.id}"]`)
    if (!row || !settle.y || reducedMotion()) {
      setSettle(null)
      return
    }
    const glide = row.animate([{ translate: `0 ${settle.y / zoom}px` }, { translate: '0 0' }], { duration: 220, easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)' })
    glide.onfinish = glide.oncancel = () => setSettle((current) => (current?.id === settle.id ? null : current))
    return () => glide.cancel()
  }, [settle])

  /* Keyboard: Space picks the row up and drops it, the arrow keys move it, Escape puts it back */
  const onKey = (entry: Entry, index: number) => (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    if (event.key === ' ' || event.key === 'Enter') {
      event.preventDefault()
      if (picked?.id === entry.id) {
        setPicked(null)
        setAnnouncement(`${entry.title} dropped at position ${index + 1} of ${shown.length}.`)
      } else {
        setPicked({ id: entry.id, before: list })
        setAnnouncement(`Picked up ${entry.title}. Use the arrow keys to move it, Space to drop it, Escape to cancel.`)
      }
      return
    }
    if (picked?.id !== entry.id) return
    const by = event.key === 'ArrowUp' ? -1 : event.key === 'ArrowDown' ? 1 : 0
    if (by) {
      event.preventDefault()
      const place = Math.max(0, Math.min(index + by, shown.length - 1))
      moveTo(entry.id, place)
      setAnnouncement(`${entry.title} moved to position ${place + 1} of ${shown.length}.`)
      requestAnimationFrame(() => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-row-id="${entry.id}"] .edit-list-grip`)?.focus())
    } else if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      event.preventDefault()
      setList(picked.before)
      setPicked(null)
      setAnnouncement(`Moving ${entry.title} canceled.`)
    }
  }

  const save = () => {
    if (onDone) return onDone(list)
    const previous = saved
    setSaved(list)
    toast({ message: 'Layout saved', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => (setSaved(previous), setList(previous)) } })
  }

  /* While a row is dragged: the row under the finger, and the rows between its place and its target slide by its height */
  const shift = (entry: Entry, index: number) => {
    if (!drag || entry.hidden) return undefined
    if (entry.id === drag.id) return { translate: `0 ${drag.y / zoom}px`, transition: 'none' }
    if (index > drag.from && index <= drag.to) return { translate: `0 ${-drag.height / zoom}px` }
    if (index < drag.from && index >= drag.to) return { translate: `0 ${drag.height / zoom}px` }
    return undefined
  }
  const row = (entry: Entry, index: number) => {
    const on = !entry.hidden
    const lifted = drag?.id === entry.id || settle?.id === entry.id
    return (
      <li
        key={entry.id}
        className="edit-list-row"
        data-row-id={entry.id}
        data-off={on ? undefined : ''}
        data-lifted={lifted || picked?.id === entry.id || undefined}
        style={shift(entry, index)}
      >
        {on ? (
          <button
            type="button"
            className="edit-list-grip"
            aria-label={`Move ${entry.title}`}
            aria-pressed={picked?.id === entry.id}
            onPointerDown={onDown(entry.id)}
            onKeyDown={onKey(entry, index)}
          >
            <DragIcon />
          </button>
        ) : (
          <span className="edit-list-grip" aria-hidden="true" />
        )}
        <span className="edit-list-name">{entry.title}</span>
        {on && entry.sizes.length > 1 && (
          <span className="edit-list-sizes" role="group" aria-label={`Size of ${entry.title}`}>
            {entry.sizes.map((size) => (
              <button key={size} type="button" aria-pressed={entry.size === size} title={`${HEIGHTS[size]} px`} onClick={() => setSize(entry.id, size)}>
                {size}
              </button>
            ))}
          </span>
        )}
        <Switch label={<span className="visually-hidden">{`Show ${entry.title}`}</span>} checked={on} onChange={(event) => toggle(entry.id, event.currentTarget.checked)} />
      </li>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="edit-list">
      <div className="edit-list-head">
        <h3>Edit layout</h3>
        <p>Drag to reorder. Switch modules on or off and pick their size.</p>
      </div>
      <h4 className="edit-list-label">
        On your overview<span aria-hidden="true">|</span>
        <span className="edit-list-count">{shown.length}</span>
      </h4>
      <ul ref={listRef} className="edit-list-rows" role="list" data-dragging={drag ? '' : undefined} data-settling={settle && !drag ? '' : undefined}>
        {shown.map(row)}
      </ul>
      {hidden.length > 0 && (
        <>
          <h4 className="edit-list-label">Hidden</h4>
          <ul className="edit-list-rows" role="list">
            {hidden.map(row)}
          </ul>
        </>
      )}
      <p className="visually-hidden" aria-live="polite">
        {announcement}
      </p>
      <div className="edit-list-bar">
        <button type="button" className="edit-reset" onClick={() => setAsk('reset')}>
          Reset to default
        </button>
        <Button size="small" variant="outlined" className="edit-cancel" onClick={() => (dirty ? setAsk('discard') : onDone ? onDone(null) : setList(saved))}>
          Cancel
        </Button>
        <Button size="small" disabled={!dirty} onClick={save}>
          Save layout
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Dialog
        open={ask !== null}
        onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setAsk(null)}
        title={ask === 'reset' ? 'Reset to default layout?' : 'Discard changes?'}
        description={ask === 'reset' ? 'All cards go back to their original position and size. Changes you have not saved will be lost.' : 'The changes you made to the layout will be lost.'}
        actions={
          <>
            <Button variant="text" onClick={() => setAsk(null)}>
              {ask === 'reset' ? 'Cancel' : 'Keep editing'}
            </Button>
            <Button
              onClick={() => {
                if (ask !== 'reset' && onDone) onDone(null)
                else setList(ask === 'reset' ? DEFAULT : saved)
                setAsk(null)
              }}
            >
              {ask === 'reset' ? 'Reset' : 'Discard'}
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      />
    </div>
  )
}

/** Edit layout inside the app shell's phone frame */
export function EditListPanel(props: EditListProps) {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Editor {...props} />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}

/** The phone's default overview, in reading order, then the cards that can be added */
export const LIST_DEFAULT = DEFAULT

export default function EditList() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Editor />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

### On desktops and tablets

*Figure: Edit layout at real size, on a desktop or a tablet grid*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Card, CardLink } from '@orbex/sonar-components/card'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { IconButton } from '@orbex/sonar-components/icon-button'
import { SegmentedControl } from '@orbex/sonar-components/segmented-control'
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@orbex/sonar-components/toast'
import { useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentType, type CSSProperties, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent, type ReactNode, type RefObject } from 'react'
import {
  AddCircleIcon,
  AddIcon,
  AutorenewIcon,
  BankIcon,
  CheckIcon,
  CloseIcon,
  DescriptionIcon,
  DragIcon,
  EditIcon,
  EventRepeatIcon,
  InStockIcon,
  ListAltIcon,
  MonitoringIcon,
  NotificationsIcon,
  ReceiptIcon,
  RequestQuoteIcon,
  ShippingIcon,
  UnfoldIcon,
  WarehouseIcon,
} from '@orbex/sonar-patterns/icons.tsx'

/*
 * Editing the overview at its real size: the six cards of the default overview, each with its content, in three
 * columns of 370 px as on a 1440 px desktop, or two of 346 px after the 60 px rail as on an 820 px tablet. The frame scrolls sideways when
 * the page is narrower. Edit layout turns the grid into a draft. Drag a card by its top handle (or focus it, press Space and move it
 * with the arrow keys), pull its bottom handle to change its size, remove it with ×, bring it back from New element,
 * then Save layout, Cancel or Reset to default from the bar at the foot.
 */

export type Size = 'S' | 'M' | 'L' | 'XL'
export interface Entry {
  id: string
  size: Size
  hidden?: boolean
}
export type Layout = Record<string, Entry[]>

/* The overview's heights and gap, in pixels, drawn at 1:1 */
const HEIGHTS: Record<Size, number> = { S: 245, M: 375, L: 405, XL: 535 }
const GAP = 20

/* Two grids: a 1440 px desktop has three columns of 370 px; an 820 px tablet, after its 60 px rail and 24 px margins,
   two of 346 px */
type Mode = 'desktop' | 'tablet'
const GRIDS: Record<Mode, { columns: string[]; width: number }> = {
  desktop: { columns: ['c1', 'c2', 'c3'], width: 370 },
  tablet: { columns: ['t1', 't2'], width: 346 },
}

/* Motion, from the product */
const NEIGHBOURS = 320
const REFLOW = 620
const SETTLE = 500

const CARDS: Record<string, { title: string; sizes: Size[] }> = {
  orders: { title: 'Orders', sizes: ['S', 'M'] },
  deliveries: { title: 'Deliveries', sizes: ['M', 'L', 'XL'] },
  shipments: { title: 'Daily shipments', sizes: ['L', 'XL'] },
  inventory: { title: 'Inventory', sizes: ['S', 'M'] },
  balance: { title: 'Balance', sizes: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
  recurring: { title: 'Recurring orders', sizes: ['M', 'L', 'XL'] },
  /* Modules that can be added from New element; they come in one size */
  notifications: { title: 'Notifications', sizes: ['L'] },
  invoices: { title: 'Invoices', sizes: ['L'] },
  documents: { title: 'Latest documents', sizes: ['L'] },
  credits: { title: 'Credit notes', sizes: ['L'] },
  scheduled: { title: 'Scheduled orders', sizes: ['L'] },
}
const OPTIONAL = ['invoices', 'documents', 'notifications', 'credits', 'scheduled']

/* What each card shows: here its title, at its size; in the product, the card itself with its content */
const BODIES: Record<string, ComponentType<{ size?: any }>> = Object.fromEntries(
  Object.entries(CARDS).map(([id, { title }]) => [id, ({ size }: { size?: any }) => <Card titleAs="h3" title={title} size={size} />]),
)

/* New element's list: an icon and a line for every module */
const INFO: Record<string, [ComponentType, string]> = {
  invoices: [ReceiptIcon, 'Latest invoices with direct download'],
  documents: [DescriptionIcon, 'Documents grouped by order'],
  notifications: [NotificationsIcon, 'Delivery alerts and updates'],
  credits: [RequestQuoteIcon, 'Credits issued to your account'],
  scheduled: [EventRepeatIcon, 'Upcoming orders by date'],
  orders: [ListAltIcon, 'Open orders by month'],
  deliveries: [ShippingIcon, 'Deliveries by day'],
  shipments: [MonitoringIcon, 'Shipments this month'],
  inventory: [WarehouseIcon, 'Stock on hold and available'],
  balance: [BankIcon, 'Overdue, due today and payment calendar'],
  recurring: [AutorenewIcon, 'Quick reorder of favourite products'],
}

const DEFAULT: Layout = {
  c1: [{ id: 'orders', size: 'M' }, { id: 'deliveries', size: 'L' }],
  c2: [{ id: 'shipments', size: 'XL' }, { id: 'inventory', size: 'S' }],
  c3: [{ id: 'balance', size: 'M' }, { id: 'recurring', size: 'L' }],
}

/* The tablet's layout comes from the desktop's: cards are read top to bottom (left to right at the same height) and
   each goes into the shorter column. Orders, Balance and Recurring orders on the left; Daily shipments, Deliveries and
   Inventory on the right. */
function deriveTablet(desk: Layout): Layout {
  const items: { entry: Entry; y: number; column: number }[] = []
  Object.values(desk).forEach((column, index) => {
    let y = 0
    for (const entry of column) {
      items.push({ entry, y, column: index })
      if (!entry.hidden) y += HEIGHTS[entry.size] + GAP
    }
  })
  const out: Layout = { t1: [], t2: [] }
  for (const { entry } of items.sort((a, b) => a.y - b.y || a.column - b.column)) out[shortest(out)]!.push({ ...entry })
  return out
}
const DEFAULTS_FOR: Record<Mode, () => Layout> = { desktop: () => clone(DEFAULT), tablet: () => deriveTablet(DEFAULT) }

const clone = (layout: Layout): Layout => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(layout))
const visible = (column: Entry[]) => column.filter((entry) => !entry.hidden)
const bottomOf = (column: Entry[]) => visible(column).reduce((sum, entry, index) => sum + HEIGHTS[entry.size] + (index ? GAP : 0), 0)
const shortest = (layout: Layout) => Object.keys(layout).reduce((a, b) => (bottomOf(layout[b]!) < bottomOf(layout[a]!) ? b : a))
const columnOf = (layout: Layout, id: string) => Object.keys(layout).find((column) => layout[column]!.some((entry) => entry.id === id))!
const DEFAULTS = Object.values(DEFAULT).flatMap((column) => column.map(({ id }) => id))

/** The pills and the remove button of a card in edit mode, as the product draws them */
export function Handles({
  title,
  size,
  preview,
  guide,
  moveProps,
  resizeProps,
  onRemove,
}: {
  title: string
  size: Size
  /** Draw a state without interaction: a handle hovered or focused, or held */
  preview?: { move?: 'hover' | 'focus' | 'on'; resize?: 'on'; remove?: 'hover' }
  guide?: ReactNode
  moveProps?: Record<string, unknown>
  resizeProps?: Record<string, unknown>
  onRemove?: () => void
}) {
  const state = (value?: string) => (value === 'on' ? { 'data-on': '' } : {})
  return (
    <>
