```
      <span style={{ display: 'contents' }} data-preview={preview?.move !== 'on' ? preview?.move : undefined}>
        <button type="button" className="edit-handle" data-handle="move" aria-label={`Move ${title}`} {...state(preview?.move)} {...moveProps}>
          <DragIcon />
        </button>
      </span>
      <span style={{ display: 'contents' }} data-preview={preview?.remove}>
        <button type="button" className="edit-remove" aria-label={`Remove ${title} from the overview`} onClick={onRemove}>
          <CloseIcon />
        </button>
      </span>
      {guide}
      <span className="edit-size" aria-hidden="true">
        {size}
      </span>
      <button type="button" className="edit-handle" data-handle="resize" aria-label={`Resize ${title}. Current size ${size}. Use arrow up or down.`} {...state(preview?.resize)} {...resizeProps}>
        <UnfoldIcon />
      </button>
    </>
  )
}

/** The label over the bottom pill while a card is resized */
export const Guide = ({ size, aligned }: { size: Size; aligned: boolean }) => (
  <span className="edit-guide" aria-live="polite">
    {aligned ? (
      <>
        <CheckIcon aria-hidden="true" />
        Aligned · {size}
      </>
    ) : (
      `${size} · ${HEIGHTS[size]} px`
    )}
  </span>
)

/* Cards travel from where they were to where they are: 320 ms while editing, 620 ms when the number of columns changes.
   The card under the pointer is left alone; it follows the pointer. Each grid watches only its own cards, so several
   grids on one page (the app shell's three frames) never animate each other's. */
function useTravel(root: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, key: string, mode: string, skip: string | undefined, zoom = 1) {
  const rects = useRef(new Map<string, DOMRect>())
  const lastMode = useRef(mode)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const cards = [...(root.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-edit-id]') ?? [])]
    const reflow = lastMode.current !== mode
    lastMode.current = mode
    const still = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
    const spring = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--sonar-motion-spatial-default-easing').trim() || 'ease-out'
    const next = new Map<string, DOMRect>()
    for (const card of cards) {
      const id = card.dataset.editId!
      const now = card.getBoundingClientRect()
      next.set(id, now)
      const was = rects.current.get(id)
      if (still || !was || id === skip) continue
      /* Rectangles are on screen; the translation is inside the zoomed canvas */
      const [dx, dy] = [(was.left - now.left) / zoom, (was.top - now.top) / zoom]
      if (!dx && !dy) continue
      card.getAnimations().forEach((animation) => animation.cancel())
      card.animate([{ translate: `${dx}px ${dy}px` }, { translate: '0 0' }], {
        duration: reflow ? REFLOW : NEIGHBOURS,
        easing: reflow ? 'cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)' : spring,
      })
    }
    rects.current = next
  }, [key, mode, skip, zoom])
}

/* The nearest box that scrolls up and down: the app frame's own overview, or else the page */
function scrollerOf(element: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  for (let node = element.parentElement; node && node !== document.body; node = node.parentElement) {
    const { overflowY } = getComputedStyle(node)
    if (/(auto|scroll)/.test(overflowY) && node.scrollHeight > node.clientHeight + 1) return node
  }
  return null
}

export interface EditCardsProps {
  /** The layout drawn: the draft while editing, the saved one otherwise */
  layout: Layout
  /** Changes the draft (only called while editing) */
  setLayout: (update: (current: Layout) => Layout) => void
  editing: boolean
  /** The scale the grid is drawn at (a fitted canvas or a scaled device frame); pointer moves are divided by it */
  zoom?: number
  /** Changing it (a new number of columns) makes the cards travel on the slower reflow */
  mode?: string
  onAnnounce: (text: string) => void
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
  /** Where New element's All modules link goes (the module sheet; 1.1.5, was Customize overview) */
  customizeHref?: string
  /** The cards' own buttons work while the layout is not edited (the app shell); the editing demo draws them still */
  interactive?: boolean
}

/**
 * The overview's grid, and Edit layout on it. Shared by the editing demo and the app shell's frames.
 *
 * Moving a card: the pointer is held by the grid itself (pointer capture), which is never redrawn. A card that changes
 * column is drawn anew, and on iPhone and iPad a finger stays tied to the element it first touched: when that element
 * left the page, the moves stopped reaching the page and the card froze, lifted, until the next touch. Where the card
 * lands is worked out from the layout (each card's height and the gap), not from what is under the finger, so the
 * card never jumps to the end of its own column and the neighbours never shake while they travel. The card is placed
 * under the finger again after every redraw, from its new slot, so it never drifts. Near the top or bottom edge the
 * overview (or the page) scrolls.
 */
export function EditCards({ layout, setLayout, editing, zoom = 1, mode = '', onAnnounce, className = 'edit-grid', style, customizeHref = '/patterns/editing/#list', interactive = false }: EditCardsProps) {
  const grid = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [drag, setDrag] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [settling, setSettling] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const settleTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined)
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState<{ id: string; before: Layout } | null>(null)
  const [resizing, setResizing] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false)
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState<string[]>([])
  const resizeStart = useRef<{ y: number; height: number } | null>(null)
  const gesture = useRef<{ id: string; pointerId: number; x: number; y: number; grabX: number; grabY: number; scroller: HTMLElement | null; frame: number; stop: () => void } | null>(null)
  /* What the window listeners read: always this render's values */
  const now = useRef({ layout, zoom })
  now.current = { layout, zoom }
  useTravel(grid, JSON.stringify(layout), mode, drag ?? undefined, zoom)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (editing) return
    setPicked(null)
    setAdding(false)
    setChosen([])
  }, [editing])
  useEffect(() => () => gesture.current?.stop(), [])

  const shown = Object.values(layout).flatMap((column) => visible(column).map(({ id }) => id))
  const removed = DEFAULTS.filter((id) => !shown.includes(id))
  const change = (fn: (next: Layout) => void) =>
    setLayout((current) => {
      const next = clone(current)
      fn(next)
      return next
    })
  const entryOf = (next: Layout, id: string) => next[columnOf(next, id)]!.find((entry) => entry.id === id)!
  const cardOf = (id: string) => grid.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-edit-id="${id}"]`) ?? null

  /* Moves a card to a column, before another card or at its end */
  const moveTo = (id: string, column: string, before?: string) =>
    change((next) => {
      const from = next[columnOf(next, id)]!
      const [entry] = from.splice(from.findIndex((other) => other.id === id), 1)
      const target = next[column]!
      const index = before ? target.findIndex((other) => other.id === before) : target.length
      target.splice(index < 0 ? target.length : index, 0, entry!)
    })

  const position = (id: string, from = layout) => {
    const column = columnOf(from, id)
    return `column ${Object.keys(from).indexOf(column) + 1}, position ${visible(from[column]!).findIndex((entry) => entry.id === id) + 1}`
  }

  /* ---------- Moving: the top handle ---------- */
  /* The lifted card is drawn where the finger holds it, measured from its slot as it is now */
  const place = () => {
    const g = gesture.current
    const card = g && cardOf(g.id)
    if (!g || !card) return
    const slot = card.getBoundingClientRect()
    card.style.setProperty('--drag-x', `${(g.x - g.grabX - slot.left) / now.current.zoom}px`)
    card.style.setProperty('--drag-y', `${(g.y - g.grabY - slot.top) / now.current.zoom}px`)
  }
  useLayoutEffect(place)

  /* Where the card would land: the column nearest its middle, and in it, before the first card whose middle is below
     the lifted card's middle, counted as if the lifted card had already left (so the answer never flips back and forth) */
  const aim = () => {
    const g = gesture.current
    const root = grid.current
    const card = g && cardOf(g.id)
    if (!g || !root || !card) return
    const { layout: current, zoom: k } = now.current
    const me = entryOf(current, g.id)
    const cx = g.x - g.grabX + (card.offsetWidth * k) / 2
    const cy = g.y - g.grabY + (HEIGHTS[me.size] * k) / 2
    let best: HTMLElement | null = null
    let distance = Infinity
    for (const column of root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-edit-column]')) {
      const box = column.getBoundingClientRect()
      const d = cx < box.left ? box.left - cx : cx > box.right ? cx - box.right : 0
      if (d < distance) [best, distance] = [column, d]
    }
    if (!best) return
    const column = best.dataset.editColumn!
    let y = best.getBoundingClientRect().top
    let before: string | undefined
    for (const other of visible(current[column]!)) {
      if (other.id === g.id) continue
      const height = HEIGHTS[other.size] * k
      if (cy < y + height / 2) {
        before = other.id
        break
      }
      y += height + GAP * k
    }
    const from = columnOf(current, g.id)
    const list = visible(current[from]!)
    if (from === column && list[list.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === g.id) + 1]?.id === before) return
    moveTo(g.id, column, before)
  }

  /* Near an edge the overview scrolls, faster the closer the finger is */
  const scroll = () => {
    const g = gesture.current
    if (!g) return
    const edge = 56
    const box = g.scroller?.getBoundingClientRect()
    const top = Math.max(box?.top ?? 0, 0)
    const bottom = Math.min(box?.bottom ?? innerHeight, innerHeight)
    const dy = g.y < top + edge ? -Math.min(18, Math.ceil((top + edge - g.y) / 3)) : g.y > bottom - edge ? Math.min(18, Math.ceil((g.y - bottom + edge) / 3)) : 0
    if (dy) {
      const before = g.scroller ? g.scroller.scrollTop : scrollY
      if (g.scroller) g.scroller.scrollTop += dy
      else scrollBy(0, dy)
      if ((g.scroller ? g.scroller.scrollTop : scrollY) !== before) {
        place()
        aim()
      }
    }
    g.frame = requestAnimationFrame(scroll)
  }

  /* While the layout is edited, a document-wide touchmove listener that can refuse the move is in place before any
     finger lands (1.0.0-alpha.21). iOS decides when a touch starts whether its moves may be cancelled; a listener added
     on pointerdown came too late, and in the App shell's frames, drawn scaled, the handle's touch-action region did not
     follow the scale on the iPad: the frame scrolled under the finger and the drag was cancelled */
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!editing) return
    const hold = (event: TouchEvent) => {
      if ((gesture.current || resizeStart.current) && event.cancelable) event.preventDefault()
    }
    /* A finger landing on a handle of this grid never starts a scroll: refused at touchstart, the handle keeps its
       pointer events (the handles have no click of their own) */
    const grab = (event: TouchEvent) => {
      const target = event.target instanceof Element ? event.target : null
      if (event.cancelable && target?.closest('[data-handle]') && grid.current?.contains(target)) event.preventDefault()
    }
    document.addEventListener('touchmove', hold, { passive: false })
    document.addEventListener('touchstart', grab, { passive: false })
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('touchmove', hold)
      document.removeEventListener('touchstart', grab)
    }
  }, [editing])

  const onMoveDown = (id: string) => (event: PointerEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    if (event.button !== 0 || gesture.current) return
    const card = cardOf(id)
    if (!card) return
    event.preventDefault()
    card.getAnimations().forEach((animation) => animation.cancel())
    const slot = card.getBoundingClientRect()
    const root = grid.current!
    const pointerId = event.pointerId
    try {
      root.setPointerCapture(pointerId)
    } catch {
      /* A pointer the browser no longer knows: the window still hears it */
    }
    const move = (e: globalThis.PointerEvent) => {
      const g = gesture.current
      if (!g || e.pointerId !== g.pointerId) return
      g.x = e.clientX
      g.y = e.clientY
      place()
      aim()
    }
    const up = (e: globalThis.PointerEvent) => {
      if (e.pointerId === pointerId) drop()
    }
    /* Older iPads scroll the page under a finger unless the move is refused while a card is held */
    const hold = (e: TouchEvent) => e.cancelable && e.preventDefault()
    const stop = () => {
      window.removeEventListener('pointermove', move)
      window.removeEventListener('pointerup', up)
      window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', up)
      window.removeEventListener('touchmove', hold)
      cancelAnimationFrame(gesture.current?.frame ?? 0)
      try {
        if (root.hasPointerCapture(pointerId)) root.releasePointerCapture(pointerId)
      } catch {
        /* already released */
      }
    }
    window.addEventListener('pointermove', move)
    window.addEventListener('pointerup', up)
    window.addEventListener('pointercancel', up)
    window.addEventListener('touchmove', hold, { passive: false })
    gesture.current = { id, pointerId, x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY, grabX: event.clientX - slot.left, grabY: event.clientY - slot.top, scroller: scrollerOf(card), frame: 0, stop }
    gesture.current.frame = requestAnimationFrame(scroll)
    setPicked(null)
    setDrag(id)
  }
  /* Dropped, the card glides from the pointer into its slot on the expressive spring and comes back down */
  const drop = () => {
    const g = gesture.current
    if (!g) return
    g.stop()
    gesture.current = null
    setDrag(null)
    setSettling(g.id)
    clearTimeout(settleTimer.current)
    settleTimer.current = setTimeout(() => {
      setSettling(null)
      const card = cardOf(g.id)
      card?.style.removeProperty('--drag-x')
      card?.style.removeProperty('--drag-y')
    }, SETTLE)
    onAnnounce(`${CARDS[g.id]!.title} dropped at ${position(g.id, now.current.layout)}.`)
  }

  /* Keyboard: Space picks the card up and drops it, the arrow keys move it, Escape puts it back */
  const onMoveKey = (id: string) => (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    const title = CARDS[id]!.title
    if (event.key === ' ' || event.key === 'Enter') {
      event.preventDefault()
      if (picked?.id === id) {
        setPicked(null)
        onAnnounce(`${title} dropped at ${position(id)}.`)
      } else {
        setPicked({ id, before: clone(layout) })
        onAnnounce(`${title} picked up. Use the arrow keys to move it, Space to drop it, Escape to cancel.`)
      }
      return
    }
    if (picked?.id !== id) return
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      event.preventDefault()
      const before = picked.before
      setLayout(() => before)
      setPicked(null)
      onAnnounce(`Moving ${title} canceled.`)
      return
    }
    const columns = Object.keys(layout)
    const column = columnOf(layout, id)
    const list = visible(layout[column]!)
    const index = list.findIndex((entry) => entry.id === id)
    if (event.key === 'ArrowUp' && index > 0) moveTo(id, column, list[index - 1]!.id)
    else if (event.key === 'ArrowDown' && index < list.length - 1) moveTo(id, column, list[index + 2]?.id)
    else if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' || event.key === 'ArrowRight') {
      const target = columns[columns.indexOf(column) + (event.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -1 : 1)]
      if (!target) return
      moveTo(id, target, visible(layout[target]!)[index]?.id)
    } else return
    event.preventDefault()
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      cardOf(id)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-handle="move"]')?.focus()
      onAnnounce(`${title} moved to ${position(id, now.current.layout)}.`)
    })
  }

  /* ---------- Resizing: the bottom handle steps through the sizes the card offers ---------- */
  const setSize = (id: string, size: Size) => change((next) => void (entryOf(next, id).size = size))
  const onResizeDown = (entry: Entry) => (event: PointerEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    event.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)
    resizeStart.current = { y: event.clientY, height: HEIGHTS[entry.size] }
    setResizing(entry.id)
  }
  const onResizeMove = (entry: Entry) => (event: PointerEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    if (!resizeStart.current) return
    const target = resizeStart.current.height + (event.clientY - resizeStart.current.y) / zoom
    const sizes = CARDS[entry.id]!.sizes
    const best = sizes.reduce((a, b) => (Math.abs(HEIGHTS[b] - target) < Math.abs(HEIGHTS[a] - target) ? b : a), sizes[0]!)
    if (best !== entry.size) setSize(entry.id, best)
  }
  const onResizeUp = () => {
    resizeStart.current = null
    setResizing(null)
  }
  const onResizeKey = (entry: Entry) => (event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => {
    const sizes = CARDS[entry.id]!.sizes
    const step = event.key === 'ArrowUp' ? -1 : event.key === 'ArrowDown' ? 1 : 0
    if (!step) return
    event.preventDefault()
    const next = sizes[sizes.indexOf(entry.size) + step]
    if (next) setSize(entry.id, next)
  }
  const aligned = (id: string) => {
    const column = columnOf(layout, id)
    const mine = bottomOf(layout[column]!)
    return Object.keys(layout).some((other) => other !== column && visible(layout[other]!).length > 0 && bottomOf(layout[other]!) === mine)
  }

  /* ---------- Removing, and bringing back from New element ---------- */
  const remove = (id: string) => {
    change((next) => void (entryOf(next, id).hidden = true))
    onAnnounce(`${CARDS[id]!.title} removed from the overview.`)
  }
  const addChosen = () => {
    change((next) => {
      for (const id of chosen) {
        const column = Object.keys(next).find((key) => next[key]!.some((other) => other.id === id))
        const from = column ? next[column]! : null
        const entry = from ? from.splice(from.findIndex((other) => other.id === id), 1)[0]! : { id, size: CARDS[id]!.sizes[0]! }
        next[shortest(next)]!.push({ ...entry, hidden: false })
      }
    })
    onAnnounce(chosen.length === 1 ? `${CARDS[chosen[0]!]!.title} added.` : `${chosen.length} modules added.`)
    setChosen([])
    setAdding(false)
  }

  const newIn = editing ? shortest(layout) : null
  return (
    <div ref={grid} className={className} style={style}>
      {Object.entries(layout).map(([column, entries]) => (
        <div key={column} className="edit-column" data-edit-column={column}>
          {visible(entries).map((entry) => {
            const card = CARDS[entry.id]!
            const Body = BODIES[entry.id]!
            const lifted = drag === entry.id
            return (
              <div
                key={entry.id}
                className="edit-card"
                data-edit-id={entry.id}
                data-size={entry.size}
                data-editing={editing || undefined}
                data-lifted={lifted || undefined}
                data-settling={settling === entry.id || undefined}
              >
                {lifted && <span className="edit-placeholder" />}
                <div className="edit-body">
                  {/* The card as the overview shows it; while the layout is edited it only moves */}
                  <div className="edit-scale" inert={editing || !interactive || undefined}>
                    <Body size={entry.size.toLowerCase()} />
                  </div>
                  {editing && (
                    <Handles
                      title={card.title}
                      size={entry.size}
                      preview={{ move: lifted || picked?.id === entry.id ? 'on' : undefined, resize: resizing === entry.id ? 'on' : undefined }}
                      guide={resizing === entry.id ? <Guide size={entry.size} aligned={aligned(entry.id)} /> : undefined}
                      onRemove={() => remove(entry.id)}
                      moveProps={{
                        'aria-pressed': picked?.id === entry.id,
                        onKeyDown: onMoveKey(entry.id),
                        onPointerDown: onMoveDown(entry.id),
                      }}
                      resizeProps={
                        card.sizes.length > 1
                          ? {
                              onPointerDown: onResizeDown(entry),
                              onPointerMove: onResizeMove(entry),
                              onPointerUp: onResizeUp,
                              onPointerCancel: onResizeUp,
                              onFocus: () => setResizing(entry.id),
                              onBlur: () => setResizing(null),
                              onKeyDown: onResizeKey(entry),
                            }
                          : { disabled: true, hidden: true }
                      }
                    />
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
            )
          })}
          {newIn === column && (
            /* New element: a card of size S at the foot of the shortest column, only while the layout is edited */
            <div className="edit-card edit-new-slot">
              <div className="edit-scale">
                {adding ? (
                  <Card
                    titleAs="h3"
                    title="New element"
                    className="new-element"
                    data-open=""
                    actions={<IconButton size="small" label="Close" icon={<CloseIcon />} onClick={() => (setAdding(false), setChosen([]))} />}
                    footer={
                      <div className="new-element-foot">
                        <CardLink href={customizeHref}>All modules</CardLink>
                        {chosen.length > 0 && (
                          <Button size="small" iconEnd={<AddIcon />} onClick={addChosen}>
                            {chosen.length === 1 ? 'Add module' : `Add ${chosen.length} modules`}
                          </Button>
                        )}
                      </div>
                    }
                  >
                    <p className="new-element-lead">Choose one or more modules for your overview.</p>
                    <div className="new-element-list" role="group" aria-label="Modules">
                      {[...OPTIONAL, ...removed].map((id, index) => {
                        const [Icon, line] = INFO[id]!
                        const added = shown.includes(id)
                        const on = chosen.includes(id)
                        const toggle = () => !added && setChosen((current) => (on ? current.filter((other) => other !== id) : [...current, id]))
                        return (
                          <div key={id} style={{ display: 'contents' }}>
                            {index === OPTIONAL.length && <p className="new-element-section">Removed from your overview</p>}
                            <div
                              className="new-element-option"
                              role="checkbox"
                              aria-checked={added || on}
                              aria-disabled={added || undefined}
                              tabIndex={added ? -1 : 0}
                              data-added={added || undefined}
                              data-chosen={on || undefined}
                              style={{ ['--i' as string]: index }}
                              onClick={toggle}
                              onKeyDown={(event) => {
                                if (event.key === ' ' || event.key === 'Enter') {
                                  event.preventDefault()
                                  toggle()
                                }
                              }}
                            >
                              <span className="new-element-icon">
                                <Icon />
                              </span>
                              <span>
                                <span className="new-element-name">{CARDS[id]!.title}</span>
                                <span className="new-element-line">{line}</span>
                              </span>
                              <span className="new-element-mark">{added || on ? <InStockIcon key="on" /> : <AddCircleIcon key="off" />}</span>
                            </div>
                          </div>
                        )
                      })}
                    </div>
                  </Card>
                ) : (
                  <Card titleAs="h3" title="New element" size="s" className="new-element">
                    <button type="button" className="new-element-add" onClick={() => setAdding(true)}>
                      <span className="new-element-plus">
                        <AddIcon aria-hidden="true" />
                      </span>
                      Add a module to your overview
                    </button>
                  </Card>
                )}
              </div>
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function Editor() {
  const toast = useToast()
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<Mode>('desktop')
  /* Fit to width: the whole canvas laid out at its real size and drawn smaller with one scale, like the product's own
     fit; nothing reflows (a transform, not CSS zoom, which made Safari re-measure the cards at the zoomed size) */
  const [fit, setFit] = useState(false)
  const frame = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [room, setRoom] = useState(0)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = frame.current
    if (!el) return
    const measure = () => setRoom(el.clientWidth)
    measure()
    const watch = new ResizeObserver(measure)
    watch.observe(el)
    return () => watch.disconnect()
  }, [])
  const canvasWidth = mode === 'tablet' ? 820 : 32 + 3 * 370 + 2 * 20 + 32
  const zoom = fit && room ? Math.min(1, room / canvasWidth) : 1
  /* The canvas's real height (a transform does not change it), so the fitted box is exactly the drawn size */
  const canvas = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [canvasHeight, setCanvasHeight] = useState(0)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = canvas.current
    if (!el) return
    const measure = () => setCanvasHeight(el.offsetHeight)
    measure()
    const watch = new ResizeObserver(measure)
    watch.observe(el)
    return () => watch.disconnect()
  }, [])
  const [savedBy, setSavedBy] = useState<Record<Mode, Layout>>(() => ({ desktop: DEFAULTS_FOR.desktop(), tablet: DEFAULTS_FOR.tablet() }))
  const saved = savedBy[mode]
  const setSaved = (layout: Layout) => setSavedBy((current) => ({ ...current, [mode]: layout }))
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<Layout | null>(null)
  const [ask, setAsk] = useState<'reset' | 'discard' | null>(null)
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState('')
  const editing = draft !== null
  const layout = draft ?? saved
  const dirty = editing && JSON.stringify(draft) !== JSON.stringify(saved)

  /* ---------- The bar ---------- */
  const enter = () => {
    setDraft(clone(saved))
    setAnnouncement('Editing layout. Drag a card by its top handle. Pull the bottom handle to change its size.')
  }
  const leave = () => setDraft(null)
  const save = () => {
    const previous = saved
    setSaved(draft!)
    leave()
    toast({ message: 'Layout saved', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => setSaved(previous) } })
  }

  return (
    <div className="edit-demo">
      <div className="edit-demo-top">
        <SegmentedControl
          legend="Screen"
          hideLegend
          size="small"
          value={mode}
          onValueChange={(value) => !editing && setMode(value as Mode)}
          disabled={editing}
          options={[
            { value: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop · 1440' },
            { value: 'tablet', label: 'Tablet · 820' },
          ]}
        />
        <label className="edit-fit">
          <input type="checkbox" checked={fit} onChange={(event) => setFit(event.target.checked)} />
          Fit to width
        </label>
        {!editing && (
          <Button variant="outlined" icon={<EditIcon />} onClick={enter}>
            Edit layout
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>
      {/* At 1:1 the grid is wider than most pages: the frame scrolls sideways, the cards are never scaled */}
      <div ref={frame} className="edit-frame" data-scroll-region tabIndex={zoom < 1 ? undefined : 0} aria-label={zoom < 1 ? undefined : 'Overview, scrolls sideways'}>
      {/* Fitted, the canvas keeps its real layout and is drawn smaller as one picture; this box takes the drawn size */}
      <div className="edit-fit-box" style={zoom < 1 ? { width: canvasWidth * zoom, height: canvasHeight * zoom } : undefined}>
      <div ref={canvas} className="edit-canvas" data-mode={mode} style={{ ['--cols' as string]: GRIDS[mode].columns.length, ['--col' as string]: `${GRIDS[mode].width}px`, ...(zoom < 1 ? { transform: `scale(${zoom})`, transformOrigin: '0 0' } : {}) }}>
      <p className="edit-demo-title">Overview</p>
      <EditCards
        layout={layout}
        setLayout={(update) => setDraft((current) => (current ? update(current) : current))}
        editing={editing}
        zoom={zoom}
        mode={mode}
        onAnnounce={setAnnouncement}
      />
      </div>
      </div>
      </div>
      {editing && (
        <div className="edit-bar" role="toolbar" aria-label="Edit layout">
          <p className="edit-bar-text">
            <strong>Editing layout</strong>
            <span>Drag a card by its top handle. Pull the bottom handle to change its size.</span>
          </p>
          <div className="edit-bar-actions">
            <button type="button" className="edit-reset" onClick={() => setAsk('reset')}>
              Reset to default
            </button>
            <Button size="small" variant="outlined" className="edit-cancel" onClick={() => (dirty ? setAsk('discard') : leave())}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button size="small" disabled={!dirty} onClick={save}>
              Save layout
            </Button>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
      <p className="visually-hidden" aria-live="polite">
        {announcement}
      </p>
      <Dialog
        open={ask !== null}
        onOpenChange={(open) => !open && setAsk(null)}
        title={ask === 'reset' ? 'Reset to default layout?' : 'Discard changes?'}
        description={ask === 'reset' ? 'All cards go back to their original position and size. Changes you have not saved will be lost.' : 'The changes you made to the layout will be lost.'}
        actions={
          <>
            <Button variant="text" onClick={() => setAsk(null)}>
              {ask === 'reset' ? 'Cancel' : 'Keep editing'}
            </Button>
            <Button
              onClick={() => {
                if (ask === 'reset') setDraft(DEFAULTS_FOR[mode]())
                else leave()
                setAsk(null)
              }}
            >
              {ask === 'reset' ? 'Reset' : 'Discard'}
            </Button>
          </>
        }
      />
    </div>
  )
}

export default function EditGrid() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider label="Layout notifications">
      <Editor />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

- **Real size.** On a 1440 px desktop the overview has three columns of 370 px with 20 px between them and 32 px margins; on an 820 px tablet, the 60 px rail, 24 px margins and two columns of 346 px. The demo draws them at 1:1 and scrolls sideways when the page is narrower; **Fit to width** draws the whole canvas smaller with one zoom, like the product, never each card.
- **Edit layout** turns the overview into a draft: each card gets a dashed edge, a handle on its top edge to move it, a remove button outside its top end corner and a handle on its bottom edge to resize it, with its size beside it. A bar rises at the foot: “Editing layout. Drag a card by its top handle. Pull the bottom handle to change its size.”, with Reset to default, Cancel and Save layout. Every state a card goes through is drawn on [Cards](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/#states).
- **Moving.** A card lifts while dragged: it grows to 103 % in 200 ms and rises to elevation 4. The others make room in 320 ms; its [drop placeholder](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/#states) shows where it will land. Dropped, it glides into its slot in 500 ms on the expressive spring.
- **Resizing** steps through the sizes the card offers, never in between, and the card eases to its new height in 320 ms; a label over the handle names the size and says when the columns end level.
- **Tablets** take their layout from the desktop’s: cards are read top to bottom, then left to right, and each goes into the shorter column. Handles grow to 44 × 20 px and the remove button to 28 px. When the number of columns changes, every card travels to its new place in 620 ms on `cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)`.
- **New element** waits at the foot of the shortest column: it brings back the cards that were removed.
- **Touch** uses the same handles with a larger hit area; the handles of two neighboring cards share the gap between them.
- **Keyboard.** Every handle is a button: Space picks a card up, the arrow keys move it, Space drops it, Escape puts it back.

### Rules

- **A draft until saved.** Save layout stays off until something changes. Cancel leaves at once when nothing changed, and asks before it discards changes.
- **Save, then Undo.** Saving does not ask; its toast offers to undo.
- **Reset to default asks first.** It puts every card back in its place and size; the draft can still be canceled.
- **Each size class keeps its own layout** once edited there; what is shown is shared. Hiding a card on a phone hides it everywhere.
- **Moves are announced.** “Inventory moved to position 2 of 6.”

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoEvery edit is a draft: Reset, Cancel and Save layout wait at the foot.*

*Figure: Don’tEach move saved as it happens, with no way back but to move it again.*

*Figure: DoResizing steps through the sizes a card offers, so columns end level.*

*Figure: Don’tA free resize: every card a different height, and ragged columns.*

---

# Panels · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/panels/

> The six side panels and sheets the overview opens: what opens each one, its parts, and how it opens on phones, tablets and desktops.

## Panels

The overview answers some actions with a panel instead of a new page: a new order, a reorder, the details of an invoice, an order or a delivery, and the system’s notifications. They are drawn with the Dialog component and live elsewhere only as answers to a click; here they are side by side, each one live.

### By device

- **Phones**: a bottom sheet with a handle, from under the top bar and with no scrim. Swipe it down from the handle or the header, use ×, or press Escape to close it.
- **Tablets**: a side sheet from the right, 402 px, under the top bar and with no scrim, as [Navigation by device](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/layout/navigation/#tablets) defines it. It slides in from the right edge, all the way, on the default spatial spring, and slides back out the same way.
- **Desktops**: a side sheet from the right, under the top bar and with no scrim, as in the product. It comes in 48 px from the right as it fades in, and leaves the same way, faster.
- The overview stays in view beside a side sheet, and the row a panel came from stays marked. With reduced motion requested, panels fade without moving.

### New order

**Opens from**: New order in the Orders card, and a search for an order that does not exist yet.

- **Header**: “New order”, “Create a new purchase order.” and ×.
- **Body**: One line per product: the product, its quantity in the card’s unit and, from two lines on, a red ring to take it out; Add product; the delivery month and a reference.
- **Actions**: The total, Cancel and Create order. Create order leads to Confirm order, with Back, Cancel and Confirm order, then to Order placed with Continue.

Closing it with changes asks first: “Discard this order?”, with Keep editing and Discard.

### Reorder

**Opens from**: Reorder in the Recurring orders card, with the favorites chosen in it.

- **Header**: “Confirm reorder”, “Review your recurring order. Quantities are the ones you used last time.” and ×. It starts at the review: the products arrive ready.
- **Body**: Each product with its packaging and quantity, then the delivery date, the total, where it goes and a reference.
- **Actions**: Cancel and Confirm reorder, then Reorder placed with Continue.

### Invoice details

**Opens from**: View on an invoice in the Balance card’s payment calendar.

- **Header**: “Invoice details”, then the invoice’s code, status, amount and due date, and ×.
- **Body**: Invoice info (customer, dates, payment terms, PO number, payment method and currency), its line items and its payment history.
- **Actions**: Go to Balance and Download PDF.

### Order details

**Opens from**: Open order on a row of the Scheduled orders card. The row stays marked while the panel is open.

- **Header**: “Order details”, then the order’s code, status, items, quantity and delivery day, and ×.
- **Body**: Order info (customer, PO number, order and delivery dates, delivery window and where it ships), its items and its schedule.
- **Actions**: Go to Scheduled orders.

### Delivery details

**Opens from**: View on a delivery in the Deliveries card’s calendar, and Open delivery on an alert in the Notifications card.

- **Header**: “Delivery details”, then the delivery’s code, status, items, quantity and date, and ×.
- **Body**: The route map with where it is now, its last stop and its destination, then its itinerary, step by step.
- **Actions**: Go to Deliveries.

### What’s new

**Opens from**: The bell in the top bar on desktops and tablets, What’s new in the bottom app bar on phones.

- **Header**: “What’s new”, how many are unread with Mark all as read, and ×.
- **Body**: The product’s notes on what changed, newest first. Unread ones carry a ring and a red dot; each links to the improvement and can be marked as read.
- **Actions**: View update history.

### Accessibility

- Each panel is a dialog named by its title; its first line is its description.
- Opening one moves focus into it. Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, Escape or × closes it, and focus goes back to what opened it.
- On phones the page behind a sheet is inert, so a screen reader stays in the sheet.
- What opens a panel reports it with `aria-expanded`; pressing it again closes the panel.

---

# Feedback · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/feedback/

> How Sonar-DB tells people what happened: toasts, undo, confirmations, notices and field errors, and when to use each.

## Feedback

Say what happened, close to where it happened, and only interrupt for what cannot be undone. Most actions act at once and offer an Undo; a confirmation is the exception.

### Which one

*Which feedback to use*

| When | Use | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Something just happened | Toast | Layout saved. Order PO-2210 created. |
| It can be taken back | Toast with Undo | Inventory removed from your overview. |
| It cannot be taken back | Dialog, before acting | Reset the overview? Discard the new order? |
| A state that lasts | Notice, in place | 2 invoices overdue. The carrier changed. |
| A field is wrong | Error under the field | Choose a date from May 12 on. |

### Act, then offer to undo

*Figure: Saved, and removed with undo*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from '@orbex/sonar-components/toast'
import { useState } from 'react'

/* Saving says it worked; removing offers to take it back. Neither asks first. */
function Actions() {
  const toast = useToast()
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(true)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="tonal" onClick={() => toast({ message: 'Layout saved.' })}>
        Save layout
      </Button>
      <Button
        variant="outlined"
        disabled={!shown}
        onClick={() => {
          setShown(false)
          toast({ message: 'Inventory removed from your overview.', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => setShown(true) } })
        }}
      >
        {shown ? 'Remove Inventory' : 'Inventory removed'}
      </Button>
    </>
  )
}

export default function Undo() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <Actions />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

### Confirm what cannot be undone

*Figure: Resetting the overview*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Dialog } from '@orbex/sonar-components/dialog'
import { useState } from 'react'

/* Confirm only what cannot be undone. The main action goes last; the dialog closes on any choice. */
export default function Confirm() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outlined" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Reset to default
      </Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Reset the overview?"
        description="Your cards go back to the default layout. Cards you added stay available in Customize."
        actions={
          <>
            <Button variant="text" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
              Keep my layout
            </Button>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Reset</Button>
          </>
        }
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### States that last

*Figure: Notices*

```
import { Button } from '@orbex/sonar-components/button'
import { Notice } from '@orbex/sonar-components/notice'

export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <>
      <Notice title="Take a look:">
        New recycled-fiber boxes are in the market.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="success" title="Order created.">
        PO-2210 was sent for confirmation.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="warning" title="Carrier changed." action={<Button size="small" variant="text">Review</Button>}>
        Delivery 04-121A now arrives with Atlas Logistics.
      </Notice>
      <Notice tone="danger" title="2 invoices overdue.">
        Pay them before May 20 to keep your credit line.
      </Notice>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Loading

The product waits in two places, and each shows it in place, with the words of what is happening rather than an empty shape. While the search reads a query, its status line says “Understanding “…”…” and a light band in the accent green crosses the words once a second; the results replace it. While the AI assistant writes an answer, three dots pulse in its bubble, 1 s each, 150 ms apart. Cards arrive with their data, so the overview has no skeleton screens; a module that someday needs to load reuses the shimmer on its own words. With reduced motion requested, the words stay still and the dots stop.

*Figure: Search, reading the query*

*Figure: AI assistant, writing an answer*

### Writing it

- Past tense for what happened (“Layout saved.”), a question for a decision (“Reset the overview?”).
- Name the thing: “Inventory removed”, not “Item removed”.
- The button that answers a question repeats its verb: Reset, Discard. Never Yes or OK.
- No exclamation marks and no apologies. Errors say how to fix them.

### Do and don’t

*Figure: DoDone: a toast, with Undo when it helps.*

*Figure: Don’tA dialog to say something went well: one more click for nothing.*

*Figure: DoOngoing: a notice in the page, until the situation changes.*

*Figure: Don’tOngoing problems in a toast: gone in seconds, and still unresolved.*

---

# App shell · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/app-shell/

> The frame every screen of Sonar-DB sits in: the sidebar and its rail, the top bar, the phone bars and the drawer, and how the 1440 canvas fits a window.

## App shell

The sidebar, the top bar and, on phones, the top bar and bottom app bar: the frame every screen sits in. It is drawn here from the product’s own markup and CSS, live, at the product’s real sizes.

### Desktop

The desktop is a 1440 × 980 canvas. The sidebar is 224 px wide and folds into a 60 px rail with the double arrow; the cards widen with it on the same spring. Every section name in the rail has a tooltip. The frames on these pages open in dark, the dashboard’s native mode; View mode switches the frame between dark and light (in an app, where the shell is the page, it switches the whole page). Sections that have no screen yet open the [unbuilt module](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/unbuilt/) page. The sidebar only navigates: the overview is edited with Edit layout in the top bar (its [module sheet](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/customize/) opens from All modules), stock is released from the Inventory card, and the chat button the [AI assistant](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/assistant/).

*Figure: The app at 1440 × 980*

### Fit to width

When the window is narrower than the canvas, the product draws the whole 1440 × 980 frame smaller with one zoom factor, the window’s width over 1440, so nothing reflows and every proportion stays the designed one. Turn **Fit to width** off to see it 1:1: the frame then scrolls sideways. The desktop editing demo has the same switch.

### Tablet

From 768 to 1279 px the sidebar starts as the 60 px rail and opens over the content with a scrim. The top bar keeps the account, the search, which takes the free width, Edit layout, alerts, chat and the avatar; the name and role move into the avatar’s menu. Margins are 24 px, and the two columns share the rest: at 820 px, 2 × 346 px with a 20 px gap.

*Figure: The app at 820 × 1180*

### Phone

On phones the top bar carries the sun, the account and a search button; search takes the whole bar when it opens. The bottom app bar holds actions, not destinations: What’s new with its count, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu, which carries a dot when something inside needs attention and opens the whole sidebar as a drawer from the left. Each button is marked while its sheet is open.

*Figure: The app at 390 × 844*

### Floating bottom bar

Since 1.1.1 the phone’s bottom app bar floats: the same five buttons, icons, labels, active pill and badges, drawn as a capsule that does not touch the edges of the screen. The page scrolls under it.

- **Place:** 12 px from each side and 12 px above the safe area (`bottom: calc(12px + safe area)`); 366 × 64 px on a 390 px screen.
- **Shape:** the full corner radius (`--sonar-shape-corner-full`), 8 px inside each end so the first and last active pills keep clear of the round ends.
- **Depth:** `--sonar-elevation-2`, tight, with no hairline. The shadow is the page’s, so it stays light on a light page.
- **Color:** the same capsule in both themes. The bar is a dark-theme scope (`data-theme="dark"` on the nav, `PhoneNav`’s default), so a light page shows the dark bar: dark surface (surface.container), dark-theme icons, labels, active pill and badges. `theme="light"` or `theme="page"` draws it otherwise.
- **Room around it:** the page ends 100 px plus the safe area lower, so the last card scrolls fully above the bar; the drawer ends in 76 px of empty room, so View mode clears it; toasts over the page sit 92 px up (`PHONE_TOAST_BOTTOM`), 16 px above the bar.
- **States:** while the drawer is open the capsule floats whole over it and the scrim; while the layout is edited it steps aside for Edit layout’s own bar.

Contrast on the capsule (WCAG 2.2 AA): labels and idle icons 5.37:1; the active label 11.03:1; the active icon on its pill 7.42:1; the badge’s white numeral 4.53:1 on the solid danger fill. The capsule against the light page: 12.54:1 (page), 10.76:1 (canvas), 13.21:1 (cards).

### Measures

| Part | Desktop 1440 | Tablet 820 | Phone 390 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar | 224 px, folds to a 60 px rail | 60 px rail, opens over the content | Drawer from the left |
| Top bar | 69 px: name and role, account, alerts, chat, Edit layout, search | Account, search, Edit layout, alerts, chat, avatar | Sun, account, search |
| Content margins | 32 px | 24 px after the rail | 16 px |
| Columns | 3 × 370 px, gap 20 | 2 × 346 px, gap 20 | 1 column |
| Bottom app bar | — | — | Floating capsule, 12 px from the sides and above the safe area, 64 px: What’s new, Assistant, Edit, Account, Menu |

### Accessibility

- The sidebar is a landmark named “Main navigation”; the open section carries `aria-current="page"`.
- The collapse button says what it will do, “Collapse sidebar” or “Expand sidebar”, and reports `aria-expanded`.
- View mode is a switch named “Light mode”, operable with Space and Enter.
- The floating bottom bar keeps every button’s name and state; it is the same landmark (“Actions”) as before, and its colors pass AA in both themes (see Floating bottom bar).
- The phone’s What’s new button reads its count (“What’s new, 2 unread”), and Menu reads “items need attention” when it carries the dot.
- With reduced motion requested, the sidebar folds and opens at once.
- Each frame is an example inside this page: its overview is a named region, not a second main landmark, its titles sit under this page’s section headings, and its icons are hidden from screen readers.
- Edit layout works in every frame, as on the overview: with a pointer or a finger by the top handle, or by focusing the handle, pressing Space and moving the card with the arrow keys.
- Since 1.1.0 the shell is in `@orbex/sonar-patterns` (`app/Shell.tsx`): an app imports it instead of copying the documentation’s source. `SearchSlot` puts the app’s own search in the top bar.
- The sidebar and the phone drawer keep the height of every row: when the window is shorter than the list, the part under the logo scrolls (on an iPad in landscape, about 1180 × 740 in Safari, the logo and the Support rows were squeezed before 1.1.0). The rows scrolled up disappear level with the foot of the top bar: the logo row is as tall as the bar (`--top-h`, 69 px), and the logo’s 32 px of air scrolls with the rows (since 1.1.2). The rail’s tooltips still sit beside their row.
- When the shell is the page itself, put `data-shell="window"` on it or an ancestor: its bars then read the device’s safe areas (the notch, the home indicator). In these frames they stay 0.

---

# AI assistant · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/assistant/

> The Orbex assistant: a floating chat on desktops and tablets, a bottom sheet on phones, with answers that carry a card of the data they talk about.

## AI assistant

A chat with the Orbex assistant, opened from the chat button in the top bar or Assistant in the phone’s bottom bar. It answers about deliveries, stock, payments and orders, and an answer about one thing carries a small card with its figures and the action to take.

### Desktop and tablet

A floating window over the overview, 340 × 460 px, 32 px from the right edge. Drag it by its header, or focus the header and use the arrow keys (Shift moves further). The button next to × toggles 340 × 460 and 520 × 680. On the desktop, with a mouse, any edge or corner also resizes it between 300 × 380 and 640 × 820; on a touch screen only the button does. It never leaves the frame. Escape or × closes it. Try a suggestion, or ask about stock, payments, a reorder or 04-127C.

*Figure: The assistant at 1440 × 980*

### Tablet

The same floating window, over the tablet’s overview and under its top bar, where the chat button opens and closes it. It keeps every measure of the desktop’s and stays inside the 820 × 1180 screen. It does not resize from its edges or corners: the button next to × toggles its two sizes.

*Figure: The assistant at 820 × 1180*

### Phone

A bottom sheet with a handle that covers all but the top 44 px, rising in 420 ms on the default spatial spring and leaving in 150 ms. The size button is gone; × closes it. The input sits above the keyboard.

*Figure: The assistant at 390 × 844*

### Anatomy

- **Header**: the sun on a green disc, “Orbex assistant” with an AI tag, a green dot and what it knows about; size and close buttons.
- **Messages**: the assistant’s on the left in a quiet bubble, the person’s on the right in green, each with its time. While it thinks, three dots pulse.
- **Answer card**: a title, an optional status tag, label and value rows, and one action.
- **Suggestions**: three questions as chips above the input.
- **Input**: a text area that grows to 96 px, Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line; the send button is disabled while it is empty.
- **Note**: “AI answers can be wrong. Check important details.”

### Accessibility

- The window is a dialog named “Chat with the Orbex AI assistant”; focus moves to the input when it opens.
- The message list is a polite live region, so new answers are read as they arrive.
- The header is focusable and moves the window with the arrow keys; the resize edges are for pointers only, and the size button does the same with one press.
- The thinking dots are an image named “The assistant is thinking”.

---

# All modules · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/customize/

> Choosing which modules the overview shows, inside Edit layout: a sheet that hangs from the top bar, with switches, the basic set and predefined layouts.

## All modules

Which modules the overview shows. A sheet hangs from the top bar over a scrim, with a switch per module, the basic set that turns the three essentials on together, and layouts made for a role. Moving and resizing cards belong to Edit layout.

### Try it

Open it from All modules, on the New element card while you edit the layout: the overview is edited in one place, Edit layout, and the sidebar only navigates. Switch a module on and close the sheet: the module goes to the foot of the shortest column and the overview scrolls to it. Save layout keeps the choice; Reset to default goes back to the last saved one.

*Figure: All modules at 1440 × 980*

### Anatomy

- **Header**: “All modules”, one line on what it does, and ×.
- **Basic set**: Orders + Inventory + Shipments, one switch for the three.
- **Modules**: “6 of 11 on” in green, then a switch per module in two columns: the six cards of the default overview and the five [optional cards](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/cards/#optional).
- **Predefined layouts**: a field with the role’s layout, Save layout, and Reset to default.

### Behavior

- It is not modal: the top bar stays usable. Escape, × or a click on the scrim close it.
- On tablets it hangs from the top bar the same way; on phones the modules are switched in Edit, in the bottom bar.
- The switches apply at once, so the overview behind the scrim already shows the change.

### Accessibility

- The sheet is a dialog named by its title and described by its first line; focus moves into it and back to where it was when it closes.
- Each module is a switch labeled with the module’s name, so “Invoices, switch, off” is read as one control.

---

# Unbuilt modules · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/patterns/unbuilt/

> What the product shows for a section that has no screen yet: what happened, what works, and the way back to the overview.

## Unbuilt modules

A section in the navigation that has no screen yet opens this page instead of a dead link: a 404 that says what happened, lists what does work and leads back to the Overview.

### Try it

Choose any sidebar section other than Overview, or one of the Support links. The chips open the sections that work; Edit layout is in the top bar; Back to Overview, or Overview in the sidebar, returns.

*Figure: An unbuilt module at 1440 × 980*

### Anatomy

- **Code**: “404 · Prototype”, small, above the title.
- **Title**: the section’s name, as the sidebar says it, and that it isn’t built: “Orders isn’t part of this prototype”.
- **Explanation**: one sentence on why, and where the interactions are.
- **What works**: the sidebar options that work, as chips that go there, and the rest as a list.
- **Way back**: Back to Overview, the one filled button.

### Rules

- Every entry in the navigation leads somewhere. A section without a screen gets this page, never an empty one or a link that does nothing.
- The sidebar stays as it is, with the section marked, so people know where they are.
- In the product the same page serves any module not built yet; change the code line when it is not a prototype.

### Accessibility

- The page is the main landmark, named by its title.
- The chips and the button are buttons; the list of other things that work is plain text.

---

# Downloads · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/downloads/

> The Orbex Sonar-DB tokens as CSS and JSON, and the API and sizes of every component as data.

## Downloads

The files the packages publish, at version 1.1.6, to open or link to without installing anything. In an app, import them from the packages instead, so they update with the version.

### Files

- [CSS tokens.css](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/downloads/tokens.css)
Every token as a CSS custom property, light and dark, in the sonar.tokens layer. 272 tokens.

`@orbex/sonar-tokens/tokens.css`
- [CSS type.css](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/downloads/type.css)
The type roles as classes, for markup that is not a component.

`@orbex/sonar-tokens/type.css`
- [JSON tokens.json](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/downloads/tokens.json)
Every token resolved in each theme, with its CSS variable, description and reference: for design tools and scripts.

`@orbex/sonar-tokens/tokens.json`
- [JSON api.json](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/api.json)
The props of every component part (35 parts), with types, defaults and descriptions, read from the source at build time.

`@orbex/sonar-components/api.json`
- [JSON sizes.json](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/sizes.json)
The gzipped weight of each entry point, script and styles, with its budget.

`@orbex/sonar-components/sizes.json`
- [Text llms.txt](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/llms.txt)
The system for language models and coding agents: every page, and the API of every component.

`llmstxt.org`

# Contributing · Orbex Sonar-DB Design System

URL: https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/contributing/

> How tokens and components of the Orbex Sonar-DB Design System are proposed, built, tested and released.

## Contributing

The system grows from needs in the product, not from ideas about it. Every change starts with where it is used, reuses what exists when it nearly fits, and arrives with its tests and its documentation.

### A token

1. Start from the need: where the value is used and which existing role nearly fits.
2. Prefer reusing a role. Add one only when the purpose is new, not when the color is.
3. Edit the token source in `packages/tokens/src`, in the W3C Design Tokens format, then run `npm test`: contrast is checked in both themes.
4. Describe the token in its `$description`: this site and `tokens.json` are generated from it.
5. Renaming or removing a token: mark the old one `$deprecated` with what to use instead, and keep it for one minor release.

### A component

1. Native HTML first. Reach for Base UI only for behavior the platform does not offer everywhere: positioning, focus management, typeahead.
2. One folder in `packages/components/src`: the component, its `index.ts` and one `styles.css` in the `sonar.components` layer, styled with role tokens only.
3. Document every prop in its JSDoc: the API tables, `api.json` and `llms.txt` are read from it.
4. Test roles, names, keyboard and states with Testing Library, and run axe on what it renders.
5. Stay within 3 KB gzipped, script and styles. A larger budget is named in the build with its reason.
6. Add its page under Components: examples, sizes, variants and states, do and don’t, accessibility and its keyboard table in `site/src/lib/a11y.ts`.

### Releasing

- Every change carries a changeset that says what it adds, changes, fixes or deprecates. Both packages are released together, under one version.
- The [changelog](https://ds-sonardb.988.gal/resources/changelog/) is written for the people who use the system: what they can now do, what behaves differently and what to replace.
- A release is cut only when the tests, the type check, the size budgets and the contrast contract all pass.
